questions.q: Chlorine occurs in nature in two isotopic forms of masses 35 u and 37 u in the ratio of $3: 1$ respectively. What is the average atomic mass of the Chlorine atom?
questions.solution:
The isotopes of chlorine are in the ratio $3: 1$.
Therefore, in any sample of chlorine, ${ }_{17}^{35} \mathrm{CI}$ will constitute $75 \%$ and ${ }_{17}^{35} \mathrm{CI}$ will constitute $25 \%$.
The proportion in which the isotopes are found in nature is always constant.
Therefore, in a sample of chlorine, the average atomic mass would be,
The average atomic mass of chlorine
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{35 \times 75}{100}\right)+\left(\frac{37 \times 25}{100}\right) \\
& =\frac{105}{4}+\frac{37}{4}=\frac{142}{4} \\
& =35.5 \mathrm{u}
\end{aligned}$
The average atomic mass of chlorine is equal to 35.5 u .

questions.solution:

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Power of lens of focal length 25 cm is
questions.solution:
We define the power of a lens as the reciprocal of the focal length of the lens. So, the power of the lens is expressed as $\mathrm{P}=1 / \mathrm{f}$
Where $f$ is the focal length and is expressed in meters. So, the unit of power of the lens is expressed in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. This is also expressed as diopter.
As we know that the focal length of a convex lens is taken as in positive sign and the focal length of a concave lens is taken negatively. So, the power of a convex lens is positive, and the power of a concave lens is negative.
In this question, it is given that the lens is convex, and its focal length is 25 cm . First, we will convert the focal length into meters.
$\Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{~cm}=0.25 \mathrm{~m} \Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{~cm}=0.25 \mathrm{~m}$
Now, substituting the value of focal length in the formula of power of lens we get
$\begin{aligned}
& P=\frac{1}{0.25} \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \\
& \Rightarrow P=4 \mathrm{~m}^{-1}
\end{aligned}\mathrm{m}-1$ is also expressed as diopters or $D$
As it is a convex lens so its power is positive.
Thus, the power of the lens is +4 D .

questions.solution: Human faeces contain appreciable quantities of vitamin B12 or vitamin B12-like material presumably produced by bacteria in the colon, but this is unavailable to the non-coprophagic individual. However, the human small intestine also often harbours a considerable microflora and this is even more extensive in apparently healthy southern Indian subjects.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: What is the total number of chambers in the stomach of domestic animals like cattle, buffalo, goat and sheep?
questions.solution: Ruminant animals like cattle, sheep, goats, etc. have a four-compartment stomach that is: the rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum. Their stomach occupies threefourth of the abdominal cavity. As these animals' food contain a lot of cellulose thus, they have cellulose enzymes that are absent in mammals. Ruminants are herbivores in nature which make diets rich in cellulose thus, they produce cellulase enzymes within their stomach with the help of bacteria.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: In electrolytic refining of copper, the electrolyte is a solution of
questions.solution:
- Electrolytic refining is the process of refining impure metals by using electricity. In this process impure metal is made as the anode and a strip of pure metal is made the cathode. A solution of a soluble salt of the same metal is taken as the electrolyte.
- In electrolytic refining of copper, the electrolyte is a solution of acidified copper sulphate. The anode is impure copper, whereas the cathode is a strip of pure copper on passing electric current, pure copper is deposited on the cathode.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is <u>not</u> used as a raw material in the manufacture of glass?
questions.solution:
- Glass is made from natural and abundant raw materials (sand, soda ash and limestone) that are melted at very high temperature to form a new material glass
- Alumina is often used in the production of glass products, lending improved strength; it has even been studied for its potential in creating an unbreakable glass
- In the glass and textile fiberglass manufacturing process, boric oxide functions as both a flux and network former. It significantly lowers melting temperature and inhibits crystallization of the glass, both of which greatly facilitate processing

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The statement "friction force is a contact force while magnetic force is a non-contact force" is
options: either true or false depending upon the temperature of the surroundings.
questions.solution:
Magnetic forces are non- contact forces; they pull or push on objects without touching them. Magnets are only attracted to a few 'magnetic' metals and not all matter. Magnets are attracted to and repel other magnet. Non-contact force occurs due to either attraction or repulsion between two objects such that there is no contact between these objects. There is no field linked with the contact force. There is always a field linked with non-contact force.
- Friction is a contact force when two surfaces interact. The static friction case is similar for when the two surfaces are stationary relative to each other. In static friction, the frictional force is whatever value it needs to be to prevent sliding up to some maximum value.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Solder is an alloy of
questions.solution:
- Solder is a metal alloy usually made of tin and lead which is melted using a hot iron.
- Alloys commonly used for electrical soldering are $60 / 40 \mathrm{Sn}-\mathrm{Pb}$, which melts at $188^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\left(370^{\circ} \mathrm{F}\right)$, and $63 / 37 \mathrm{Sn}-\mathrm{Pb}$ used principally in electrical/electronic work. This mixture is a eutectic alloy of these metals, which: has the lowest melting point $\left(183^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right.$ or $\left.361^{\circ} \mathrm{F}\right)$ of all the tin-lead alloys
- The solder composition, being free of lead and other known toxic metals, has a composition range of 0.5 - 4.0% antimony, $0.5-4.0 \%$ zinc, $0.1-3.0 \%$ silver, $0.1-2.0 \%$ copper and $86.8-98.8 \% ~\mathrm{tin}$, is especially adaptable for plumbing applications where solder joints are exposed to potable water.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Reverberation is a phenomenon associated with a
questions.solution: A reverberation, or reverb, is created when a sound or signal is reflected causing numerous reflections to build up and then decay as the sound is absorbed by the surfaces of objects in the space - which could include furniture, people, and air. This is most noticeable when the sound source stops but the reflections continue, their amplitude decreasing until zero is reached.

It applies only to spherical lenses.
It applies to spherical mirrors as well as spherical lenses.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The image we see in plane mirror is
options: real and thus can be photographed.
virtual and nearer than the object.
questions.solution:
The image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual (meaning that the light rays do not actually come from the image), upright, and of the same shape and size as the object it is reflecting. A virtual image is a copy of an object formed at the location from which the light rays appear to come.
An image formed by a plane mirror has the following characteristics: $\square$
- Virtual and erect.
- Behind the mirror.
- The size of the image is equal to the size of the object.
- Laterally inverted image (image of the left side visible on the right side).

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Movement of materials to different parts of cytoplasm and nucleus is generally carried out by
questions.solution:
Transfer of materials to different parts of cytoplasm and nucleus is done by Endoplasmic Reticulum. Endoplasmic reticulum.
- The extensive network can be naturally found in the cell. The nuclear envelope is bound to the endoplasmic reticulum.
- It is a membranous network that typically surrounds a fluid-filled lumen that almost completely fills the intracellular cavity.
- As a direct result, it acts as a protein transport channel between the active nucleus and the cytoplasm.
- The ER allows materials to be transported from one part of the cell to another, arranging the circulatory system of the cell

questions.solution:

Squamous epithelium has cells that are wider than their height (flat and scale-like).

questions.subject: General Ability

options: All the leaves will dry up simultaneously
questions.solution: Applying Vaseline on the surface of the leaf will result in the blockage of small pores(stomata) which are responsible mainly for respiration and thus cutting off the supply of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide. In absence of respiration and photosynthesis, the plant leaf will die

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is <u>not</u> correct for light rays ?
options: Light travels at different speeds in different media.
Light travels at almost 300 million metres per second in air.
Light speeds down as it leaves a water surface and enters the air.
Light speeds up as it leaves a glass surface and enters the air.
questions.solution:
A light ray is a line (straight or curved) that is perpendicular to the light's wavefronts; its tangent is collinear with the wave vector. Light rays in homogeneous media are straight. They bend at the interface between two dissimilar media and may be curved in a medium in which the refractive index changes
Light waves travel fastest through a vacuum and air, and slower through other materials such as glass or water. Light travels at approximately 300,000 kilometers per second in a vacuum, which has a refractive index of 1.0 , but it slows down to 225,000 kilometers per second in water and 200,000 kilometers per second in glass.

Red light will deviate the most and it is because of the refraction of light.
Violet light will deviate the most and it is because of the reflection of light.
questions.solution:
Rayleigh scattering law. It simply states that :
1. U(Refractive index) is inversely proportional to square of the wavelength of light.
2. deviation is directly related to refractive index.
3. Speed of light depends on the medium. Densser the medium lesser the speed and raser the medium greater the speed of light and is maximum $3 \times 10^{\circ} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ in air/ vacuum.
More the index more will be the deviation
- Violet colour deviate most and red deviate the less because the wavelength of a red light is almost double the wavelength of violet light.
- Because of the different indices of refraction for the different wavelengths of visible light, the angle of deviation varies with wavelength. But since the violet light has a shorter wavelength, it would refract more than the longer wavelength red light.

questions.solution: Ramen effect is the process of scattering of light particles by molecules of medium. The scattering occurs due to a change in the wavelength of light as it enters the medium. When light wave strike a medium, some of the energy of incident light may be increased or decreased the molecules of the medium, hence the scattered light may have frequency or wavelength increased or decreased. Rayleigh scattering is a form of elastic scattering in which incident light and scattered light has same frequency.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following conclusions could not be derived from Rutherford's $\alpha$-particle scattering experiment?
options: Most of the space in the atom is empty.
The radius of the atom is about $10^5$ times the radius of the nucleus.
Electrons move in a circular path of fixed energy called orbits.
Nearly all the mass of the atom resides in the nucleus.
questions.solution:
Conclusion of Rutherford's scattering experiment: Most of the space inside the atom is empty because most of the $\alpha$-particles passed through the gold foil without getting deflected.
- Very few particles were deflected from their path, indicating that the positive charge of the atom occupies very little space.
- A very small fraction of $\alpha$-particles were deflected by very large angles, indicating that all the positive charge and mass of the gold atom were concentrated in a very small volume within the atom.
- From the data he also calculated that the radius of the nucleus is about $10^5$ times less than the radius of the atom.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Twinkling of stars is due to
options: reflection of starlight from the oceanic surface.
questions.solution:
- The twinkling of a star is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight. The starlight, on entering the earth's atmosphere, undergoes refraction continuously before it reaches the earth.
- As light from a star races through our atmosphere, it bounces and bumps through the different layers, bending the light before you see it. Since the hot and cold layers of air keep moving, the bending of the light changes too, which causes the star's appearance to wobble or twinkle.

questions.solution:

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Transformation of meristematic cells into specific permanent tissues occurs by the process of
questions.solution:
- The permanent tissues always differentiate from the meristematic cells, during the process of growth. These meristematic cells lose the ability to divide and take up a specific role. This process of taking up a permanent shape, size and a function is called cellular differentiation.
- The cells derived from root apical and shoot-apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions.
- This act leading to maturation is termed as differentiation. During differentiation, cells undergo few to major structural changes both in their cell walls and protoplasm.
- The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation.
- For example, formation of meristems - interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells. While doing so, such meristems / tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform specific functions, i.e., get redifferentiated.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: During seed germination, the part of the embryo which grows into root is
questions.solution: The primary root, or radicle, is the first organ to appear when a seed germinates. It grows downward into the soil, anchoring the seedling. In gymnosperms and dicotyledons (angiosperms with two seed leaves), the radicle becomes a taproot. The tip of the root is covered by a mass of loose cells called the root cap.

questions.subject: General Ability

ATP synthase uses this concentration gradient to synthesize the energy rich molecule ATP.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A liquid is kept in a glass beaker. Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the pressure exerted by the liquid column at the base of the beaker?
options: The pressure depends on the area of the base of the beaker
The pressure depends on the height of liquid column
The pressure does not depend on the density of the liquid
The pressure neither depends on the area of the base of the beaker nor on the height of liquid column
questions.solution: The pressure of liquid kept in a glass beaker depends upon the height of liquid column inside the beaker. Pressure at different heights from the surface of liquid is given by formula, $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}+\rho \mathrm{gh}$ Where, $P$ is total pressure, $\rho=$ density of liquid, $g$ is acceleration due to gravity and h is height of the liquid from the surface.

questions.q:
Two equal resistors R are connected in parallel, and a battery of 12 V is connected across this combination. A dc current of 100 mA flows through the circuit as shown below:
The value of $R$ is
questions.solution:
Let R' be the equivalent resistance of two resistors.
As they are connected in parallel
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{R}+\frac{1}{R} \\
& R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2} (i)
\end{aligned}$
Using ohm's law
$V=I R^{\prime}\begin{aligned}
& R^{\prime}=\frac{V}{I}=\frac{12}{100 \times 10^{-3}} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}^{\prime}=120 \Omega
\end{aligned}$
But, $R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2}\therefore \quad \mathrm{R}=2 \times \mathrm{R}^{\prime}=2 \times 120=240 \Omega$

questions.solution:
According to Kepler's law of planetary motion, $\mathrm{T}^2 \propto \mathrm{R}^3$
Therefore, the ratio of the time period is given by,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{T_1^2}{T_2^2}=\frac{R^3}{(4 R)^3}=\frac{1}{64} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{T_1}{T_2}=\frac{1}{8}
\end{aligned}$
i.e., $T_1: T_2$ is $1: 8$

questions.solution: When the light enters the human eye through the cornea; it then passes through the aqueous humor, the lens and the vitreous humor. questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about sound is NOT correct?
options: Sound travels at a speed slower than the speed of light
Sound travels faster in moist air than in dry air
questions.solution:
The sensation felt by our ears is called sound. It is a form of energy which makes us hear. Sound travels in the form of wave.
Longitudinal Waves: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth in the 'same direction' in which the wave is moving. Medium can be solid, liquid or gases. Therefore, sound waves are longitudinal waves. Sound is a longitudinal wave which consists of compressions and rarefactions travelling through a medium.
Transverse Waves: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate up and down 'at right angles' to the direction in which the wave is moving. These waves are produced only in a solids and liquids but not in gases.

questions.q: A lens has a power of +2.0 Dioptre. Which one of the following statements about the lens is true?
options: The lens is concave and has a focal length of 0.5 metre
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 2.0 metre
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 0.5 metre
The lens is concave and has a focal length of 2.0 metre
questions.solution:
A dioptre, is a unit of measurement of the optical power of a lens, which is equal to the reciprocal of the focal length measured in meters (that is, $1 / \mathrm{f}$ metres). It is thus a unit of reciprocal length.
Hence, $\mathrm{P}=1 / \mathrm{f} \Rightarrow 2=1 / \mathrm{f} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=0.5$ meter.
As the value is positive, it is a positive lens, that is, convex. Hence, the option (c) is true.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT the unit of energy?
questions.solution:
A watt-hour $(\mathrm{Wh})$ is a unit of energy; it's a way to measure the amount of work performed or generated. Household appliances and other electrical devices perform "work" and that requires energy in the form of electricity. The joule (symbol J) is the SI unit of energy-a measure of the capacity to do work or generate heat. Newton-Meter $(\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m})$ is a unit of energy. One joule equals the work done (or energy expended) by a force of one newton (N) acting over a distance of one meter (m).
SI unit for force is Newton (N).
$1 \mathrm{~N}=1 \mathrm{~kg} \cdot \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
Thus, $\mathrm{kg} \cdot \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ is the unit of Force not energy.

Thus, Force becomes half.

Graphite is a good conductor of electricity while diamond is not.

Water has a high heat of fusion
Water is a non polar molecule

questions.subject: General Ability

Mitochondria is a double-membrane-bound organelle found in most eukaryotic organisms.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: The filament is the part of the light bulb that produces light. Filaments in incandescent light bulbs are made of tungsten. For a typical incandescent light bulb, the Tungsten filament operates at approximately 2500 Celsius. Hence, the filaments are made of tungsten.

The simplest form of organic acids, such as acetic and formic, are typically used in stimulation treatments against corrosion for gas and oil, since these are less reactive compared to hydrochloric acid and other strong acids.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The equivalent weight of oxalic acid in $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is
questions.solution:
The equivalent weight of oxalic acid in $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is 63.
- The molecular weight of oxalic acid $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)$ is 90.
- But since Oxalic Acid exists with 2 molecules of water, hence molecular weight of Oxalic acid $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)=126$
- Now, Equivalent weight = Molecular weight/Basicity
- Therefore, Equivalent Weight $=126 / 2=63$ (As 2 is the basicity)
- Basicity here means Oxalic Acid release $2 \mathrm{H}^{+}$ ions

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Dinitrogen $\left(\mathrm{N}_2\right)$ and dioxygen $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$ are the main constituents of air but they do not react with each other to form oxides of nitrogen because
options: the reaction requires initiation by a catalyst
the reaction is endothermic and requires very high temperature
the stoichiometry of $\mathrm{N}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ in air is not ideal for the reaction to take place
questions.solution:
It is because:
(i) the reaction is endothermic and requires very high temperature.
(ii) the reaction can be initiated only in presence of a catalyst.
(iii) oxides of nitrogen are unstable.
(iv) $\mathrm{N}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ are unreactive.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Two metallic wires $A$ and $B$ are made using copper. The radius of wire $A$ is $r$ while its length is $l$. A dc voltage $V$ is applied across the wire $A$, causing power dissipation, $P$. The radius of wire $B$ is $2 r$, and its length is $2 l$ and the same dc voltage $V$ is applied across it causing power dissipation $P_1$. Which one of the following is the correct relationship between $P$ and $P_1$ ?
questions.solution:
Resis tance of wire $\mathrm{R}=\rho \frac{l}{\mathrm{~A}}=\rho \cdot \frac{l}{\pi \mathrm{r}^2}$
If $R_0$ is resistance of first wire, the resistance of second wire.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=\rho \cdot \frac{2 l}{\pi \cdot(2 \mathrm{r})^2}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \rho \frac{l}{\pi \mathrm{r}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_0}{2} \\ & \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{R}_0} \text { and } \mathrm{P}_1=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{R}_{0 / 2}}=2 \mathrm{P}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding Electrocardiogram is correct ?
options: Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of electrical activity of cornea
Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of activity of kidney
Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of activity of brain
Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of electrical activity of heart
questions.solution: An electrocardiogram (ECG or EKG) is a test that checks how your heart is functioning by measuring the electrical activity of the heart. With each heart beat, an electrical impulse (or wave) travels through your heart. This wave causes the muscle to squeeze and pump blood from the heart.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Tooth enamel is made up of which one of the following calcium compounds ?
questions.solution: Tooth enamel is the hardest, most highly mineralized substance in the body. It forms the outer, most visible layer of each tooth. Enamel is composed of hydroxyapatite, a mineral compound of calcium and phosphate Enamel plays a very important role in protecting teeth from decay. Tooth enamel forms a strong barrier that shields the inner layers of teeth from the effects of acids and plaque.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The atomic number of an element is 8 . How many electrons will it gain to form a compound with sodium?
questions.solution:
It will gain two electrons to form a compound with sodium. When the element with atomic number 8 that is oxygen reacts with sodium, each sodium atom loses an electron and sodium is oxidized, and each oxygen gains two electrons.

In path $A \rightarrow B$ velocity is decreasing with time, therefore $A B$ represents deceleration.
In path $B \rightarrow C$ velocity is constant with time.
In path $C \rightarrow D$ velocity is increasing with time, therefore $C D$ represents acceleration.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A sample of oxygen contains two isotopes of oxygen with masses 16 u and 18 u respectively. The proportion of these isotopes in the sample is $3: 1$. What will be the average atomic mass of oxygen in this sample?
questions.solution:
Isotope $1 \rightarrow 16 \mathrm{u}$
Isotope $2 \rightarrow 18 \mathrm{u}$
Proportion of Isotopes $=3: 1$
Now, Average atomic Oxygen $=(16 \times 3)+(18 \times 1) / 3+1=16.5 u$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is called syngas?
questions.solution: Syngas or synthesis gas is a mixture comprising of carbon monoxide $(\mathrm{CO})$, and hydrogen gas $\left(\mathrm{H}_2\right)$. It also contains little percentage of carbon dioxide $\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right), \mathrm{N}_2$, char, ashes, tars, and oils. Sound wave cannot propagate in vacuum.

options: Cholera is a disease that causes loss of memory
Cholera is a disease of muscles due to consumption of alcohol
Cholera is a disease due to consumption of contaminated food or water
questions.solution: Cholera is an infectious disease that causes severe watery diarrhea, which can lead to dehydration and even death if untreated. It is caused by eating food or drinking water contaminated with a bacterium called Vibrio cholerae.

Graphite is layered structure in which layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces.

Graphite layers are held together by carbon-carbon single bond.
questions.solution: In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms in the same plane giving a hexagonal array. 2. The focal length of the objective of a telescope is larger than the focal length of its eyepiece.
3. The magnification of a telescope increases with the increases in focal length of its objective.
4. The magnification of a microscope increases with the increases in focal length of its objective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
In case of compound microscope both the eyepiece and the objective of are made up of convex lenses. The focal length of the objective of a telescope is larger than the focal length of its eyepiece.
The magnification of a telescope increases with the increase in focal length of its objective since $m=\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}} / \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}$ while the magnification of microscope decreases with increase in focal length of its objective.

questions.q: A planet has a mass $M_1$ and radius $R_1$. The value of acceleration due to gravity on its surface is $g_1$. There is another planet 2 , whose mass and radius both are two times that of the first planet. Which one of the following is the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of planet 2 ?
questions.solution:
The acceleration experienced by the mass $\mathrm{M}_1$, on planet 1 is given by $\mathrm{g}_1=\mathrm{GM}_1 / \mathrm{R}_1^2$,
similarly the $\mathrm{g}_2=\mathrm{G}_2 \mathrm{M}_1 / 4 \mathrm{R}_1{ }^2$,
hence, $\mathrm{g}_1 / \mathrm{g}_2=2 / 1$ or
$\mathrm{g}_2=\mathrm{g}_1 / 2$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the law of conservation of mass is correct?
options: A given compound always contains exactly same proportion of elements.
When gases combine in a reaction, they do so in a simple ratio by volume, provided all gases are at room temperature.
Matter can neither be created nor destroyed.
Equal volumes of all gases at same temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.
questions.solution: The law of conservation of mass states that mass in an isolated system is neither created nor destroyed by chemical reactions or physical transformations. According to the law of conservation of mass, the mass of the products in a chemical reaction must equal the mass of the reactants. The law of conservation of mass is useful for a number of calculations and can be used to solve for unknown masses, such the amount of gas consumed or produced during a reaction.

In this reflex action brain is not involved.

questions.solution: Hearing is one of the five senses of the body. The ears help the body to pick up sound waves and vibrations. The number of vibrations that are produced per second is called frequency. Frequency varies for each sound and is measured in hertz. Humans cannot hear sounds of every frequency. The range of hearing for a healthy young person is 20 to 20,000 hertz.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about meristematic tissues in plants is correct?
options: These are dead tissues and form wood
They provide flexibility to plant due to their thickened walls
These are present in the bark of a tree only
Growth occurs in plants due to division of cells of these tissues
questions.solution: Meristematic tissues, or simply meristems, are tissues in which the cells remain forever young and divide actively throughout the life of the plant. Cells within the meristematic tissues are self-renewing, so that each time they divide, one cell remains identical to the parent while the other can specialize and become part of another plant structure. The meristematic tissue is therefore self-sustaining.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about classification of plants is correct?
options: Thallophytes have well differentiated body design
Vascular system is not found among Bryophytes
questions.solution:
Mosses and liverworts are lumped together as bryophytes, plants lacking true vascular tissues, and sharing a number of other primitive traits. They also lack true stems, roots, or leaves, though they have cells that perform these general functions.
Bryophytes do not have a true vascular system and are unable to pull water and nutrients up from the ground at any significant distance. Lacking this specialised system distinguishes bryophytes from ferns and flowering plants. It is for this reason that they are considered to be rather primitive plants.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is the value of 1 kWh of energy converted into joules?
questions.solution:
kWh (kilowatt-hour) and Joules are two energy units. 1 watt is defined as 1 joule/second. So if you multiply a watt times seconds, you get Ws which is also a joule.
So 1 kW is 1000 W , and an hour is 60 seconds x 60 minutes.
So $1 \mathrm{kWh}=3600 \mathrm{kWs}=3,600,000 \mathrm{Ws}=3,600,000 \mathrm{~J}$
So $1 \mathrm{kWh}=3.6 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.solution: Dengue virus (DENV) is the cause of dengue fever. It is a mosquito-borne single positive-stranded RNA virus of the family Flaviviridae; genus Flavivirus. This virus causes bone marrow suppression leading to reduction in number of blood platelets. A typical person has a platelet count of between 150,000 and 250,000 per microlitre of blood. About 80 to 90 per cent of patients with dengue will have levels below 100,000 , while 10 to 20 per cent of patients will see critically low levels of 20,000 or less.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following elements corrodes rapidly?
questions.solution: Iron corrodes rapidly, because of its non-stable corrosion products on the surface. Rust occurs when metals containing iron react with the oxygen in the air or in water and form a compound called iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide). This compound contains water molecules, so we call it a hydrated compound. Both oxygen gas and water must be present for the iron to rust. Chemically and very simply speaking, iron atoms lose a few electrons to oxygen atoms. This process by which electrons are removed from atoms is called oxidation. When oxidation occurs, it produces a chemical reaction that creates iron(III) oxide-or rust.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A circular coil of single turn has a resistance of $20 \Omega$. Which one of the following is the correct value for the resistance between the ends of any diameter of the coil?
questions.solution:
Each of the two semicircles between the two ends of the diameter has a resistence of $20 / 2=10$. These two resistors are in parallel between the 2 ends of the diameter. Thus the effective resistance
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_1 \times \mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1+\mathrm{R}_2}=\frac{10 \times 10}{10+10}=\frac{100}{20}=5$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The valency of an element depends upon the
options: total number of protons in an atom
total number of neutrons is an atom
total number of electrons in the outer most shell of an atom
questions.solution: Valency is the measure of the combining capacity of atoms or molecules. Therefore, it is the capacity of an atom of a single element to react and combine with particular numbers of atoms of another element. The electrons present in the outermost shell/orbit of an atom are called valence electrons. The valence electrons take part in any chemical reaction because the outermost orbit usually contains more energy than the electrons present in other orbits. The valency of an element depends upon the total number of electrons in the outer most shell of an atom.

questions.solution: Red blood cells (RBCs) are cells that circulate in the blood and carry oxygen throughout the body. It is also called erythrocytes. Red blood cells (RBCs) have no nucleus, no mitochondria and no endoplasmic reticulum. Hemoglobin is the protein inside red blood cells. It carries oxygen. Red blood cells also remove carbon dioxide from human body. Foods rich in iron help you maintain healthy red blood cells. Vitamins are also needed to build healthy red blood cells.

questions.solution: Cone cells, or cones, are photoreceptor cells in the retinas of vertebrate eyes (e.g. the human eye). They respond differently to light of different wavelengths, and are thus responsible for color vision and function best in relatively bright light, as opposed to rodcells, which work better in dim light.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: In a solenoid, the current flowing through the wire is I and number of turns per unit length is $n$. This gives a magnetic field $B$ inside the solenoid. If number of turn per unit length is increased to 2 n , what will be the value of magnetic field in the solenoid?
questions.solution:
A long solenoid is the one which has a larger length in comparison to the radius. It consists of a long wire wound in the form of a helix where the neighboring turns are closely spaced. So each turn can be regarded as a circular loop. The net magnetic field is the vector sum of the fields due to all the turns. Enamelled wires are used for winding so that turns are insulated from each other.
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is: $\mathrm{B}=\mu_0 \mathrm{nI}\ldots \ldots \ldots$. (1) where $\mathrm{n}=$ number of turns per unit length and $\mathrm{I}=$ current flowing through the solenoid. The magnetic field at a point on one end of the long solenoid is: $\mathrm{B}=\left(\mu_0 \mathrm{nI} / 2\right)$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A homogeneous mixture contains two liquids. How are they separated?
questions.solution: The homogeneous mixtures that are represented by a single uniform phase, throughout the entire mixture, can be separated using the properties of the components that participate in mixture. The method of separation of homogeneous mixtures is called distillation and it is based on the various boiling points of the component of mixture. Heating the mixture, the component that has the lowest boiling point will evaporate and the separation can be done.

Magnification does not depend upon the focal length of eyepiece
Magnification decreases with the increase in focal length of eyepiece
questions.solution: A telescope operates with an object at infinity (or close to it), and the angular magnification is given by the ratio between objective and eyepiece focal lengths. So increasing the objective focal length increases the magnification - but it also makes the telescope tube longer, which can be awkward. So, normally, you increase magnification by switching to a shorter focal length eyepiece, not a longer focal length objective and Vice versa.

questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mu g=3 / 2 \quad \mathrm{v}_\omega=4 / 3 \\
& \mu \mathrm{~g}=\mathrm{c} / \mathrm{vg} \quad \mu_\omega=\mathrm{c} / \mathrm{v}_\omega \\
& \mu \mathrm{g} / \mu_\omega=\mathrm{v}_\omega / \mathrm{vg} \quad 3 / 2 / 4 / 3=\mathrm{v}_\omega / \mathrm{vg} \\
& 9 / 8=\mathrm{v}_\omega / \mathrm{vg} \quad \text { or } \mathrm{vg} / \mathrm{v}_\omega=8 / 9 \\
& \mathrm{Vg}: \mathrm{v}_\omega=8: 9
\end{aligned}$

Statement I is true but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Mass is an invariant quantity. Acceleration due to gravity (g) decreases with altitude as one rises above the Earth's surface because greater altitude means greater distance from the Earth's centre.
Weight, $\mathrm{w}=$ mass $(\mathrm{m}) \times$ acc. due to gravity $(\mathrm{g})\mathrm{g}_{\text {height }}=\mathrm{g} /\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)^2$
Hence body weighs less on hill top than on earth's
surface.

questions.q: If radius of the earth were to shrink by $1 \%$, its mass remaining the same, g would decrease by nearly
questions.solution:
If the radius of the earth were to shrink by one percent, mass remaining the same, the value of $g$ will increase by $2 \%$.
$\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}^2}$
If mass remains constant, then $\mathrm{g} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{R}^2}\begin{aligned}
& \% ~\text { increase in } g=2(\% ~\text { decrease in } \mathrm{R}) \\
& =2 \times 1 \%=2 \%
\end{aligned}$
Therefore value of g will increase by $2 \%$.

the bottom, it exhibits a strongly convex meniscus,
whereas the meniscus of water is concave. Mercury will
not wet the glass, unlike water and many other liquids,
and if the glass is tipped, it will 'roll' around inside.

questions.q:
The sun is observed to be reddish when it is near the horizon,
i.e., in the morning and the evening. This is because
options: red light is least scattered by atmosphere
red light is most scattered by atmosphere
it is the colour of the Sun in the morning and evening
questions.solution:
Tiny molecules in our atmosphere cause light to scatter. That's why our sky looks blue: it's because the atmosphere scatters the bluish component of white sunlight. And it's why the sun looks reddish when it's near the horizon. Sunlight encounters more air molecules when the sun is low in the sky than when the sun is overhead. Even more blue light is scattered away, leaving mostly the reddish scattering
$\propto \frac{1}{\lambda^4}$ component of white sunlight to travel the straighter path to your eyes. So the setting and rising sun looks red.

questions.q:
When you walk on a woolen carpet and bring your finger
near the metallic handle of a door an electric shock is
produced. This is because
options: charge is transferred from your body to the handle
a chemical reaction occurs when you touch the handle
the temperature of the human body is higher than that of the handle
the human body and the handle arrive at thermal equilibrium by the process
questions.solution:
All materials are made up of negatively- and positivelycharged particles. These usually exist in equal amounts, balancing each other out. But when two materials come into contact, one may 'steal' negatively-charged
electrons from the other. One material ends up with more negative charges than positive ones, meaning that it becomes negatively-charged overall, whilst the other becomes positively-charged. If the charges cannot move away as they are produced, they accumulate in the material as static charge, or electricity. Once you have built up a big enough static charge, an electric shock is almost inevitable. The moment you touch a conducting material such as metal, the excess electrons jump between your hand and the conductor, giving you a shock.

questions.q: The pressure of an ideal gas undergoing isothermal change is increased by $10 \%$. The volume of the gas must decrease by about
questions.solution:
In isothermal process
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta \mathrm{T}=0 \\
& \therefore \quad P V=\text { Constant } \\
& \mathrm{P} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~V}}
\end{aligned}$
From $\quad \mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1=\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2$
here $\quad \mathrm{P}_2=\left(1+\frac{10}{100}\right) \mathrm{P}_1=1.1 \mathrm{P}_1\therefore$ Change in volume
$\frac{V_1-V_2}{V_1}=\frac{1}{11}$
Percentage decrease $=9.09 \%$.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding extratropical cyclones:
I. They usually develop in the mid and high latitudes.
II. They affect a much larger area as compared to tropical cyclone.
III. They move from east to west.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Extratropical cyclones develop in the mid and high latitudes, beyond the tropics. Hence, statement I is correct.

They have a clear frontal system and cover a much larger area compared to tropical cyclones. Hence, statement II is correct.

Extratropical cyclones move from west to east under the influence of westerly winds, whereas tropical cyclones generally move from east to west. Hence, statement III is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements I and II are correct.

Answer: I and II only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Loose sediments are transformed into sedimentary rocks by the process of
questions.solution:
Lithification is the process by which loose, unconsolidated sediments are transformed into solid sedimentary rocks. This occurs through compaction, where the weight of overlying materials compresses the sediments, and cementation, where minerals precipitate from groundwater and bind the sediment particles together.

Weathering is the breakdown of rocks into smaller particles.

Mass wasting is the downward movement of rock and soil under gravity.

Solifluction is a specific type of mass wasting common in permafrost areas.

Answer: lithification

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Earthquake waves are basically of two types, namely body waves and surface waves.
II. The body waves interact with the surface rocks and generate surface waves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Earthquake waves are broadly classified into two types: body waves and surface waves. Body waves are generated due to the release of energy at the focus and move in all directions travelling through the body of the Earth.

When these body waves interact with the surface rocks, they generate a new set of waves called surface waves, which move along the surface.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a strategy in the Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme of India?
questions.solution:
Rainfed Area Development (RAD) is a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).

The primary objective of RAD is to make rainfed agriculture more productive, sustainable, remunerative, and climate-resilient.

Key strategies of the RAD scheme include promoting Integrated Farming Systems (diversified farming), soil health management, and adopting a cluster-based approach to maximize the impact of interventions.

Since rainfed areas primarily depend on rainfall and lack assured irrigation, optimizing canal irrigation is not a strategy under the RAD scheme. It is typically a focus of command area development programs for irrigated regions.

Answer: Optimizing canal irrigation

questions.solution:
According to the land-use categories in the Land Revenue Records of India:

Current fallow is the land left uncultivated for one agricultural year or less.

Fallow other than current fallow is the cultivable land which is left uncultivated for more than a year but less than 5 years.

Culturable wasteland is the land left uncultivated for more than 5 years.

Barren and unculturable land is the land which cannot be brought under cultivation except at an exorbitant cost.

Therefore, the given description corresponds to fallow, other than current fallow.

Answer: fallow, other than current fallow

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about temperature inversion:
I. This happens when normal lapse rate gets inverted.
II. Winter nights with cloudy skies are conducive for temperature inversion.
III. Polar areas experience inversion throughout the year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Temperature inversion is a reversal of the normal behavior of temperature in the troposphere, where a layer of cool air at the surface is overlain by a layer of warmer air. Under normal conditions, temperature usually decreases with height, which is known as the normal lapse rate. When this is reversed, the normal lapse rate gets inverted. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Ideal conditions for temperature inversion include long winter nights, clear skies, calm air, and dry air. Cloudy skies prevent the rapid cooling of the earth's surface by trapping outgoing terrestrial radiation, which hinders the formation of a temperature inversion. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

In polar regions, due to the extremely cold surface, temperature inversion is a normal phenomenon that occurs throughout the year. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Therefore, only statements I and III are correct.

Answer: I and III only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Types of Chemical WeatheringCharacteristics
I. SolutionResults in leaching of minerals
II. CarbonationHelps in breaking down feldspars
III. HydrationCauses an increase in the volume of rocks
IV. OxidationChanges the colour of rocks

How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Chemical weathering processes include solution, carbonation, hydration, and oxidation.

I. Solution involves the dissolution of soluble minerals in water or weak acids, leading to the leaching of minerals from rocks. This pair is correctly matched.

II. Carbonation is the reaction of carbonates and bicarbonates with minerals. It is a common process that helps in the breaking down of feldspars and carbonate minerals. This pair is correctly matched.

III. Hydration is the chemical addition of water. Minerals absorb water and expand, causing an increase in the volume of the rocks, which leads to physical stress. This pair is correctly matched.

IV. Oxidation involves the reaction of minerals with oxygen to form oxides or hydroxides. This process often changes the colour of rocks, such as iron-bearing minerals turning red, brown, or yellow upon oxidation. This pair is correctly matched.

All four pairs are correctly matched.

Answer: All the four

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. In a seismograph, P waves are recorded earlier than S waves.
II. In P waves, the individual particles vibrate to and fro in the direction of wave propagation whereas in S waves, the particles vibrate up and down at right angles to the direction of wave propagation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
P waves are primary waves and travel faster than S waves. Thus, they reach the seismograph first and are recorded earlier. Statement I is correct.

P waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate to and fro parallel to the direction of wave propagation. S waves are transverse waves, meaning the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. Statement II is correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding hypocentre:
I. It is the point where the energy is released and is called the focus of an earthquake.
II. It is the point where the earthquake starts and may be many kilometers deep within the Earth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The hypocentre is the point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts. It is also commonly termed the focus.

It is the exact location where the strain energy stored in the rock is first released, marking the origin of the seismic waves.

This point can be located at various depths beneath the Earth's surface, ranging from near the surface to hundreds of kilometers deep.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

I. Neodymium
II. Tellurium
III. Dysprosium
IV. Gallium
Which of the above minerals are not used for the production of photovoltaic cells used in solar panels?
questions.solution:
Neodymium (I) and Dysprosium (III) are rare earth elements primarily used in the manufacturing of strong permanent magnets, which are essential for wind turbines and electric vehicle motors. They are not used in the production of photovoltaic cells.

Tellurium (II) is a key component in cadmium telluride (CdTe) thin-film solar cells.

Gallium (IV) is used in the production of copper indium gallium selenide (CIGS) and gallium arsenide (GaAs) solar cells.

Thus, Neodymium and Dysprosium are not used for the production of photovoltaic cells.

Answer: I and III

Santa Ana winds are strong, extremely dry down-slope winds that originate inland and affect coastal Southern California and northern Baja California. They are notorious for exacerbating regional wildfires due to their dry and warm nature.

Diablo winds and Jarbo Gap winds affect Northern California, while Chinook winds occur in the interior West of North America (Rocky Mountains).

Answer: Santa Ana wind

questions.solution:
Mount Ibu is a stratovolcano, which is also known as a composite volcano. It is located on the northwest coast of Halmahera island in Indonesia.

Composite volcanoes are conical volcanoes built up by many layers (strata) of hardened lava, tephra, pumice, and volcanic ash.

Answer: composite volcano

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in case of terrestrial planets:
I. Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are terrestrial planets having low densities as compared to other planets.
II. They lie between the Sun and the belt of asteroids.
III. Their lower gravity can hold the escaping gases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because terrestrial planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars) are primarily composed of rock and metal and have high densities compared to the Jovian planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune), which are gas giants with much lower densities.

Statement II is correct. The terrestrial planets are the inner planets, and their orbits lie between the Sun and the asteroid belt.

Statement III is correct. Because the terrestrial planets are smaller, they have lower gravity compared to the Jovian planets. This lower gravity is insufficient to hold escaping gases, which is why they do not possess thick, massive atmospheres of light gases like hydrogen and helium, unlike the giant outer planets.

Therefore, statements II and III are correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Rowlatt Act of 1919:
I. Gandhiji launched a nationwide Satyagraha against the proposed Rowlatt Act, 1919.
II. The Act had been hurriedly passed through the Imperial Legislative Council despite the opposition of Indian members.
III. The Act gave the Government enormous powers to repress political activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919) was hurriedly passed by the Imperial Legislative Council despite the united opposition of the Indian members. This makes Statement II correct.

The Act gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed the detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. This makes Statement III correct.

In response to this unjust law, Mahatma Gandhi decided to launch a nationwide Satyagraha, which started with a hartal on 6 April 1919. This makes Statement I correct.

Since all three statements are correct, the correct option includes I, II, and III.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Revolution in Britain:
I. There was availability of banks which could loan money to set up industries.
II. There was a good transport network.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Industrial Revolution in Britain was facilitated by several key factors.

Statement I is correct. Britain had a well-developed financial system. The Bank of England was established in 1694, and by the late eighteenth century, there were numerous provincial banks that provided the necessary capital and loans to entrepreneurs to set up industries.

Statement II is also correct. Britain possessed an excellent transport network. It had a long coastline and many navigable rivers, which made the transportation of raw materials and finished goods easier and cheaper. This was later enhanced by the construction of canals and railways.

Since both statements are correct, the correct option is Both I and II.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Russian Revolution:
I. The incident known as 'Bloody Sunday' started a series of events known as the 1905 Revolution.
II. Lawyers, doctors, engineers and other middle-class workers established the Union of Unions and demanded a Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The incident of 'Bloody Sunday' occurred in 1905 when a peaceful procession of workers led by Father Gapon was attacked by the police and the Cossacks, resulting in the death of over 100 workers. This event triggered a series of strikes and protests across the country, which came to be known as the 1905 Revolution.

During the 1905 Revolution, various sections of society, including lawyers, doctors, engineers, and other middle-class workers, formed the Union of Unions. They actively participated in the protests and demanded the establishment of a Constituent Assembly to draft a constitution for Russia.

Both statements are historically accurate.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Who among the following advocated the construction of initial railways in India for facilitating army movement?
questions.solution:
Lord Dalhousie, who served as the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, is widely regarded as the 'Father of Indian Railways'. In his famous Railway Minute of 1853, he strongly advocated for the construction of a network of railways in India. His primary motivations were to facilitate the rapid movement of the British army to maintain control over the vast Indian territory and to promote British commercial interests by enabling the easy transport of raw materials from the interior to the ports and manufactured goods from the ports to the interior markets.

Answer: Lord Dalhousie

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following are associated with composite volcanoes?
I. They result in explosive eruptions.
II. They eject pyroclastic materials.
III. Pyroclastic materials and ashes accumulate near the vent, forming layers.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Composite volcanoes are characterised by eruptions of cooler and more viscous lavas than basalt. These volcanoes often result in explosive eruptions.

Along with lava, large quantities of pyroclastic material and ashes find their way to the ground.

This material gathers near the vent openings leading to the creation of layers, which gives them the name composite volcanoes or stratovolcanoes.

Therefore, all three statements I, II, and III are correct.

Answer: I, II and III
