$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a-x & c & b \\
c & b-x & a \\
b & a & c-x
\end{array}\right|=0 \text { is }$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a-x & c & b \\
c & b-x & a \\
b & a & c-x
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
 -\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x-(a+b+c) & c & b \\
x-(a+b+c) & b-x & a \\
x-(a+b+c) & a & c-x
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
 \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x & c & b \\
x & b-x & a \\
x & a & c-x
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
 \left\{\text { Applying } \mathrm{C}_1 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2+\mathrm{C}_3\right. \text { \} } \\
 \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x & c & b \\
0 & c+x-b & b-a \\
0 & c-a & b+x-c
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
 \text { \{Applying } \mathrm{R}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_1-\mathrm{R}_2 \text { and } \mathrm{R}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_1-\mathrm{R}_3 \text { \} } \\
 x\{(c+x-b)(b+x-c)-(b-a)(c-a)\}=0 \\
 x\left\{\left(x^2-(b-c)^2-b c+a c+a b-a^2\right\}=0\right. \\
 x\left(x^2-a^2-b^2-c^2+a b+b c+c a\right)=0 \\
 x\left\{x^2-(a-b)^2-(b-c)^2-(c-a)^2\right\}=0 \\
 \begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & x=0 \\
\end{array}
\end{aligned}$

& =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For what values of $k$ is the system of equations $2 k^2 x+3 y-1=0,7 x-2 y+3=0,6 k x+y+1=0$ consistent?
questions.solution:
We know that three lines $a_1 x+b_1 y+c=0, a_2 x+b_2 y+c_2=0$ and $a_3 x+b_3 y+c_3=0$ are concurrerce if
$\begin{aligned}
& \left|\begin{array}{lll}
a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\
a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\
a_3 & b_3 & c_3
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \therefore\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
2 k^2 & 3 & -1 \\
7 & -2 & 3 \\
6 k & 1 & 1
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 k^2(-2-3)-7(3+1)+6 k(9-2)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 5 k^2-21 k+14=0 \\
& \therefore k=\frac{21 \mp \sqrt{161}}{10}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If $A, B$ and $C$ are the angles of a triangle and
$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 1 & 1 \\
1+\sin \mathrm{A} & 1+\sin \mathrm{B} & 1+\sin \mathrm{C} \\
\sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A} & \sin \mathrm{~B}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~B} & \sin \mathrm{C}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{C}
\end{array}\right|=0$
then which one of the following is correct?
options: No conclusion can be drawn with regard to the nature of the triangle
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1+\sin \mathrm{A} & 1+\sin \mathrm{B} & 1+\sin \mathrm{C} \\ \sin \mathrm{A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A} & \sin \mathrm{~B}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~B} & \sin \mathrm{C}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{C}\end{array}\right|\begin{aligned}
& \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 0 & 0 \\
1+\sin \mathrm{A} & \sin \mathrm{~A}-\sin \mathrm{B} & \sin \mathrm{~A}-\sin \mathrm{C} \\
\sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A} & \sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}-\sin ^2 \mathrm{~B} & \sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}-\sin ^2 \mathrm{C}
\end{array}\right|+0=0 \\
& \left\{\text { Applying } \mathrm{C}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_1-\mathrm{C}_2 \text { and } \mathrm{C}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_1-\mathrm{C}_3\right. \text { \} } \\
& =(\sin \mathrm{A}-\sin \mathrm{B}) \times(\sin \mathrm{A}-\sin \mathrm{C}) \\
& \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 0 & 0 \\
1+\sin \mathrm{A} & 1 & 1 \\
\sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A} & (\sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin \mathrm{B}) & (\sin \mathrm{A}+\sin \mathrm{C})
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& (\sin A-\sin B)(\sin A-\sin C)(\sin B-\sin C)=0 \\
& \therefore \sin \mathrm{~A}=\sin \mathrm{B} \text { or } \sin \mathrm{A}=\sin \mathrm{C} \text { or } \sin \mathrm{B}=\sin \mathrm{C} \text { either } \mathrm{A}= \\
& \mathrm{B} \text { or } \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{C} \text { or } \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{C} \text {. }
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, \mathrm{a}_9$ are in GP, then what is the value of the following determinant?
$\left|\begin{array}{lll}\ln a_1 & \ln a_2 & \ln a_3 \\\ln a_4 & \ln a_5 & \ln a_6 \\\ln a_7 & \ln a_8 & \ln a_9\end{array}\right|$
questions.solution:
As $a_1, a_2, a_3 \ldots \ldots a_9$ are in G.P.
$\therefore \frac{a_4}{a_1}=\frac{a_5}{a_2}=\frac{a_6}{a_3} \ldots . .=r^3 \quad(\text { where } r=\text { common ratio) }$
Now, $\left|\begin{array}{lll}\ln a_1 & \ln a_2 & \ln a_3 \\ \ln a_4 & \ln a_5 & \ln a_6 \\ \ln a_7 & \ln a_8 & \ln a_9\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\ln a_4-\ln a_1 & \ln a_5-\ln a_2 & \ln a_6-\ln a_3 \\ \ln a_7-\ln a_4 & \ln a_8-\ln a_5 & \ln a_9-\ln a_6 \\ \ln a_7 & \ln a_8 & \ln a_9\end{array}\right|$ 
(Applying $R_1 \rightarrow R_2-R_1$ and $R_2 \rightarrow R_3-R_2$ )
$=\left|\begin{array}{lll}\ln \frac{a_4}{a_1} & \ln \frac{a_5}{a_2} & \ln \frac{a_6}{a_3} \\ \ln \frac{a_7}{a_4} & \ln \frac{a_8}{a_5} & \ln \frac{a_9}{a_6} \\ \ln a_7 & \ln a_8 & \ln a_9\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{lll}\ln r^3 & \ln r^3 & \ln r^3 \\ \ln r^3 & \ln r^3 & \ln r^3 \\ \ln a_7 & \ln a_8 & \ln a_9\end{array}\right|=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $p+q+r=a+b+c=0$, then the determinant $\left|\begin{array}{lll}p a & q b & r c \\ q c & \text { ra } & p b \\ r b & p c & q a\end{array}\right|$ equals
questions.solution: $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\mathrm{pa} & \mathrm{qb} & \mathrm{rc} \\ \mathrm{qc} & \mathrm{ra} & \mathrm{pb} \\ \mathrm{rb} & \mathrm{pc} & \mathrm{qa}\end{array}\right|=\mathrm{pa}\left(\mathrm{rqa}^2-\mathrm{p}^2 \mathrm{bc}\right)-\mathrm{qb}\left(\mathrm{q}^2 \mathrm{ac}-\mathrm{prb}^2\right)+\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{rc}\left(q \mathrm{qcc}^2-\mathrm{r}^2 a b\right) \\ & =\mathrm{pqra}^3-\mathrm{p}^3 a b c-\mathrm{q}^3 a b c+\mathrm{pqrb}^3+\mathrm{pqrc}^3-\mathrm{r}^3 a b c \\ & =\mathrm{pqr}\left(\mathrm{a}^3+\mathrm{b}^3+\mathrm{c}^3\right)-\mathrm{abc}\left(\mathrm{p}^3+\mathrm{q}^3+\mathrm{r}^3\right) \\ & \text {Given, } \mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{p}^3+\mathrm{q}^3+\mathrm{r}^3=3 \mathrm{pqr} \text { and } \mathrm{a}^3+\mathrm{b}^3+\mathrm{c}^3=3 \mathrm{abc} . \\ & \therefore \operatorname{pqr}\left(\mathrm{a}^3+\mathrm{b}^3+\mathrm{c}^3\right)-\mathrm{abc}\left(\mathrm{p}^3+\mathrm{q}^3+\mathrm{r}^3\right) \\ & =\operatorname{pqr}(3 \mathrm{abc})-\mathrm{abc}(3 \mathrm{pqr}) \\ & =0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\mathrm{x} & \mathrm{y} & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{x} & \mathrm{y} \\ \mathrm{y} & 0 & \mathrm{x}\end{array}\right|=0$, then which one of the following is correct?
options: $\frac{x}{y}$ is one of the cube roots of unity
x is one of the cube roots of unity
y is one of the cube roots of unity
$\frac{x}{y}$ is one of the cube roots of -1
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \left|\begin{array}{lll}\mathrm{x} & \mathrm{y} & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{x} & \mathrm{y} \\ \mathrm{y} & 0 & \mathrm{x}\end{array}\right|=0 \Rightarrow x\left(\mathrm{x}^2-0\right)-\mathrm{y}\left(0-\mathrm{y}^2\right)+0=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^3+\mathrm{y}^3=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow x^3=-y^3 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x^3}{y^3}=-1 \Rightarrow\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^3=-1 \Rightarrow \frac{x}{y}=\sqrt[3]{-1}\end{aligned}$

Paragraph: For the system of linear equations $2 x+3 y+5 z=9,7 x+3 y-2 z=8$ and $2 x+3 y+\lambda z=\mu$
Question: Under what condition does the above system of equations have infinitely many solutions?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}

2 & 3 & \lambda
\end{array}\right] \text { and } B=\left[\begin{array}{l}
9 \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the function
$f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right|$, where $p$ is a constant.
What is the value of $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(0)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} f(x) & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right| \\ f^{\prime}(x)= & \left|\begin{array}{ccc}3 x^2 & \cos x & -\sin x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right| \\ & +\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right|\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} f^{\prime}(x) & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}3 x^2 & \cos x & -\sin x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right| \\ f^{\prime}(0) & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & \cos 0 & -\sin 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right| \\ & =-6 p^3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the function $f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right|$, where $p$ is a constant.
What is the value of $p$ for which $f^{\prime \prime}(0)=0$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}6 x & -\sin x & -\cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right| \\ & f^{\prime \prime}(0)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & 0 & -\cos 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3\end{array}\right| \\ & \quad=-1\left(6 p^2+p\right) \\ & f^{\prime \prime}(0)=0 \\ & \begin{array}{l}-\left(6 p^2+p\right)=0 \\ p(6 p+1)=0\end{array} \\ & p=0 \text { or } p=-\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The system of linear equations $\mathrm{kx}+\mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}=1, \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{ky}+\mathrm{z}=1$ and $x+y+k z=1$ has a unique solution under which one of the following conditions?
questions.solution:
Linear equations
$\begin{aligned}
& K x+y+z=1 \\
& x+K y+z=1 \\
& x+y+K z=1 \\
& {\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
K & 1 & 1 \\
1 & K & 1 \\
1 & 1 & K
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}
x \\
y \\
z
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l}
1 \\
1 \\
1
\end{array}\right]} \\
& \quad A X=B \\
& X=A^{-1} B
\end{aligned}$
Linear equation will have unique solution when $A^{-1}$ exist :
$\begin{aligned}
& |A| \neq 0 \\
& {\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
K & 1 & 1 \\
1 & K & 1 \\
1 & 1 & K
\end{array}\right] \neq 0} \\
& K\left(K^2-1\right)-1(K-1)+1(1-K) \neq 0 \\
& \Rightarrow K^3-K-K+1+1-K \neq 0 \\
& \Rightarrow K^3-3 K+2 \neq 0

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the determinant
$\left|\begin{array}{cc}
\cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} & \sin ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \\
\sin ^2 \frac{\beta}{2} & \cos ^2 \frac{\beta}{2}
\end{array}\right|$
where $\alpha, \beta$ are complementary angles
1. The value of the determinant is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \left(\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}\right)$.
2. The maximum value of the determinant is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
  
Which of the above statements is/ are correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha+\beta=90^{\circ} \\
& \left|\begin{array}{ll}
\cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} & \sin ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \\
\sin ^2 \frac{\beta}{2} & \cos ^2 \frac{\beta}{2}
\end{array}\right| \\
& =\cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \cos ^2 \frac{\beta}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \sin ^2 \frac{\beta}{2} \\
& = \\
& \left(\cos \frac{\alpha}{2} \cos \frac{\beta}{2}+\sin \frac{\alpha}{2} \sin \frac{\beta}{2}\right)\left(\cos \frac{\alpha}{2} \cos \frac{\beta}{2}-\sin \frac{\alpha}{2} \sin \frac{\beta}{2}\right) \\
& =\cos \frac{(\alpha-\beta)}{2} \times \cos \frac{(\alpha+\beta)}{2} \\
& =\cos \frac{(\alpha-\beta)}{2} \times \cos \frac{\left(90^{\circ}\right)}{2}=\cos \frac{(\alpha-\beta)}{2} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$
Maximum value of $\cos \left(\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}\right)$ is 1 . So maximum value of determinent is $\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
So both 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.q: The system of equations $k x+y+z=1, x+k y+z=k$ and $x+y+k z=k^2$ has no solution if $k$ equals
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & k x+y+z=1 \\ & x+k y+z=k \\ & x+y+k z=k^2\end{aligned}$
These equations will have no solution of $\left|\begin{array}{lll}\mathrm{k} & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \mathrm{k} & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \mathrm{k}\end{array}\right|=0$.
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}\left(\mathrm{k}^2-1\right)-1(\mathrm{k}-1)+(1-\mathrm{k})=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{k}+1)(\mathrm{k}-1)-1(\mathrm{k}-1)-(\mathrm{k}-1)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\mathrm{k}-1)[\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{k}+1)-1-1]=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}&\Rightarrow(\mathrm{k}-1)\left(\mathrm{k}^2+\mathrm{k}-2\right)=0 \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=1 \text { or }-2 \end{aligned}$
For $\mathrm{k}=1$, all equations are same and have infinite solution. So, for $\mathrm{k}=-2$, equations have no solution.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: One of the roots of $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x+a & b & c \\ a & x+b & c \\ a & b & x+c\end{array}\right|=0$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x+a & b & c \\
a & x+b & c \\
a & b & x+c
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& (x+a)[(x+b)(x+c)-b c]-b[a(x+c)-a c] \\
& +c[a b-a(x+b)] \\
& =(x+a)\left[x^2+x c+b x+b c-b c\right]-b[a x+a c-a c] \\
& +c[a b-a x-a b] \\
& =(x+a)\left[x^2+x c+b x\right]-a b x-a c x \\
& =x^3+x^2 c+b x^2+a x^2+a c x+a b x-a b x-a c x \\
& =x^3+x^2 c+b x^2+a x^2 \\
& =x^2(x+a+b+c)
\end{aligned}$
Now, $x^2(x+a+b+c)=0\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow x+a+b+c=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x=-a-b-c
\end{aligned}$
Hence, one of the root is $-(a+b+c)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The matrix $\left(\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 2 & 1 \\ a & 2 a & 1 \\ b & 2 b & 1\end{array}\right)$ is singular.
2. The matrix $\left(\begin{array}{ccc}c & 2 c & 1 \\ a & 2 a & 1 \\ b & 2 b & 1\end{array}\right)$ is non-singular.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A square matrix is said to be singular if its determinant is zero \& non-singular if its determinant is not equal to zero.
$\begin{aligned}
& \left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 1 \\
a & 2 a & 1 \\
b & 2 b & 1
\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 1 \\
a-b & 2(a-b) & 0 \\
1-b & 2(1-b) & 0
\end{array}\right| \\
& \left\{\text { Applying } \mathrm{R}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_2-\mathrm{R}_3 ; \mathrm{R}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_1-\mathrm{R}_3\right\} \\
& =(a-b)(1-b)\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 2 & 1 \\
1 & 2 & 0 \\
1 & 2 & 0
\end{array}\right| \\
& =(a-b)(1-b)(2-2)=0 \text { It is singular. }
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text { Again, }\left|\begin{array}{lll}
c & 2 c & 1 \\
a & 2 a & 1 \\
b & 2 b & 1
\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
c & 2 c & 1 \\
a-b & 2(a-b) & 0 \\
b-c & 2(b-c) & 0
\end{array}\right| \\
& \quad\left\{\text { Applying } \mathrm{R}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_2-\mathrm{R}_3 ; \mathrm{R}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_3-\mathrm{R}_2\right\} \\
& =(a-b)(b-c)\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
c & 2 c & 1 \\
1 & 2 & 0 \\
1 & 2 & 0
\end{array}\right| \\
& =(a-b)(b-c)(2-2)=0
\end{aligned}$
It is singular.

questions.q: What are the order and degree respectively of the differential equation $\left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{0.6}=\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$ ?
questions.solution:
$\left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{0.6}=\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$
Removing decimal power/fraction power both sides
$\left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{3 / 5}=\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^5$
Raise power of 5 both sides
$\begin{aligned}
& \left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{\frac{3}{5} \times 5}=\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^5 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^3=\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^5
\end{aligned}$
Hence,
$\begin{aligned}
\text { Order } & =2 \\
\text { Power } & =5
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the degree of the differential equation $\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}$?
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{\dfrac{5}{2}}$.

To find the degree of the differential equation, the powers of the derivatives must be made integers. Squaring both sides, we get:

$\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^5$

The highest order derivative is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which has an order of $2$.

The power of the highest order derivative is $3$.

Therefore, the degree of the differential equation is $3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $k$ is an arbitrary constant, then what is the general solution of the equation $(x + y)^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = k^2$?
questions.solution:
Let $x + y = v$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1$

Substituting in the given differential equation:

$v^2 \left( \dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1 \right) = k^2$

$v^2 \dfrac{dv}{dx} = v^2 + k^2$

$\dfrac{v^2}{v^2 + k^2} dv = dx$

$\left( 1 - \dfrac{k^2}{v^2 + k^2} \right) dv = dx$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \left( 1 - \dfrac{k^2}{v^2 + k^2} \right) dv = \int dx$

$v - k \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v}{k}\right) = x + c$

Substituting $v = x + y$:

$x + y - k \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{k}\right) = x + c$

$y - c = k \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{k}\right)$

$\dfrac{y - c}{k} = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{k}\right)$

$x + y = k \tan\left(\dfrac{y - c}{k}\right)$

Answer: $x + y = k\tan\left(\dfrac{y - c}{k}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Consider the differential equation $e^{x+y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{x-y}$.

Question: What is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\left(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right)^2$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Given the differential equation:

$e^{x+y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y}$

$e^x e^y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x e^{-y}$

Dividing both sides by $e^x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{e^{-y}}{e^y} = e^{-2y}$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{-2y}) = -2e^{-2y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Substituting $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{-2y}$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -2e^{-2y}(e^{-2y}) = -2e^{-4y}$

From $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{-2y}$, we get:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1}{e^{-2y}} = e^{2y}$

Squaring both sides:

$\left(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right)^2 = (e^{2y})^2 = e^{4y}$

Now, multiplying the two results:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\left(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right)^2 = (-2e^{-4y})(e^{4y}) = -2e^0 = -2$

Answer: $-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. $y = xe^{2x}$ is the solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)$.
II. $y = x\ln|x| + cx$ is the solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y}{x}$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
For Statement I:

Given $y = xe^{2x}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2x} + 2xe^{2x} = e^{2x}(1 + 2x)$

Also, $y\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) = xe^{2x}\left(\dfrac{2x + 1}{x}\right) = e^{2x}(2x + 1)$

Since $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)$, Statement I is correct.

For Statement II:

Given $y = x\ln|x| + cx$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \ln|x| + x\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + c = \ln|x| + 1 + c$

Also, $\dfrac{x + y}{x} = 1 + \dfrac{y}{x} = 1 + \dfrac{x\ln|x| + cx}{x} = 1 + \ln|x| + c$

Since $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y}{x}$, Statement II is correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.q: What is the solution of the differential equation $\cos\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)=p$ when $y(0)=q$ ?
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\cos\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)=p$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos^{-1}(p)$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$y = x \cos^{-1}(p) + C$

Given $y(0) = q$, substituting $x = 0$ and $y = q$:

$q = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = q$

Substituting the value of $C$ in the equation:

$y = x \cos^{-1}(p) + q$

$\Rightarrow y - q = x \cos^{-1}(p)$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{y - q}{x} = \cos^{-1}(p)$

$\Rightarrow \cos\left(\dfrac{y - q}{x}\right) = p$

Answer: $\cos\left(\dfrac{y-q}{x}\right)=p$

Passage: Consider the differential equation $e^{x+y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{x-y}$.

The given differential equation is $e^{x+y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{x-y}$

$e^x e^y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x e^{-y}$

$e^y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{-y}$

$e^{2y} dy = dx$

Integrating both sides:

$\int e^{2y} dy = \int dx$

$\dfrac{e^{2y}}{2} = x + C$

Given $y(0)=0$, substituting $x=0$ and $y=0$:

$\dfrac{e^0}{2} = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Substituting $C$ back into the equation:

$\dfrac{e^{2y}}{2} = x + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$e^{2y} = 2x + 1$

$2y = \ln(2x+1)$

questions.q: Let $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ be two solutions of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=x$. If $y_1(0)=0$ and $y_2(0)=4$, then what is the number of points of intersection of curves $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ ?

Given, D.E. $\frac{d y}{d x}=x\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \int d y & =\int x d x \\ \Rightarrow & y & =\frac{x^2}{2}+c\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad y_1(x)=\frac{x^2}{2}+c_1$ ...(i)
and $\quad y_2(x)=\frac{x^2}{2}+c_2$  ...(ii)
For $y_1(0)=0$ in equation (i)
$0=0+c_1\Rightarrow \quad c_1=0\Rightarrow \quad y_1(x)=\frac{x^2}{2} \quad$ ...(iii)
For $\quad y_2(0)=0\Rightarrow \quad 4=0+c_2 \quad[$ From (iii) $]$
For, $\quad c_2=4\Rightarrow \quad y_2(x)=\frac{x^2}{2}+4 \quad$  ...(iv)
For number of points of intersection for $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ solving (iii) and (iv)
$\frac{x^2}{2}=\frac{x^2}{2}+4 \text { (not possible) }$
as
$0 \neq 4$
Hence, no point of intersection.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $k \frac{d y}{d x}=\int\left[1+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right]^{\frac{2}{3}} d x$ are respectively
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
$k \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}=\int\left[1+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right]^{2 / 3} \cdot d x$
On differentiating both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned} & k \cdot \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\left[1+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right]^{2 / 3} \\ & \Rightarrow\left(k \cdot \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^3=\left[1+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right]^2\end{aligned}$
Now, order of the D.E. $=2$ Degree of the D.E. $=3$.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the differential equation that represents the family of curves $y=\frac{1}{2 x^2-c}$ where $c$ is an arbitrary constant?

questions.q: The differential equation which represents the family of curves given by $\tan y=c\left(1-e^x\right)$ is
options: $e^x \tan y d x+\left(1-e^x\right) \sec ^2 y d y=0$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \tan y=c\left(1-e^x\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=c\left(-e^x\right) \\ & \Rightarrow c=\frac{1}{e^x} \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x} \\ & \therefore \tan y=\frac{-1}{e^x} \sec ^2 y \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}\left(1-e^x\right) \\ & \Rightarrow e^x \cdot \tan y=\sec ^2 y\left(1-e^x\right) \frac{d y}{d x} \\ & \Rightarrow e^x \tan y d x+\left(1-e^x\right) \sec ^2 y d y=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=\cos (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x})+1$ is
questions.solution:
$\frac{d y}{d x}=\cos (y-x)+1$...(1)
Let $\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}-1=\frac{d t}{d x}\therefore(1) \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d x}+1=\cos t+1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d x}=\cos t \\ & \Rightarrow \sec t \cdot \mathrm{dt}=1 \cdot \mathrm{dx} \\ & \Rightarrow \int \sec t \cdot d t=\int 1 \cdot d x \\ & \Rightarrow \log |\operatorname{sect}+\tan t|=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow-\log |\sec t-\tan t|=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \log |\sec t-\tan t|=-\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \log (\sec (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x})-\tan (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x})=-\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \sec (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x})-\tan (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{x}} \cdot \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{c}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}(\sec (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x})-\tan (\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x}))=\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}$

Differentiating, $1+\frac{x \cdot 2 y \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}-y^2}{x^2}=0\Rightarrow x^2+2 x y \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}-y^2=0$

questions.q: What is the general solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{x}{y}=0$ ?
questions.solution: $\frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{x}{y}=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-x}{y} \\ & \Rightarrow y d y+x d x=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{y^2}{2}+\frac{x^2}{2}+c=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y^2+x^2+2 c=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2+y^2=c\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is the solution of the differential equation $(d y-d x)+\cos x(d y+d x)=0 ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (d y-d x)+\cos x(d y+d x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(1+\cos x) d y=(1-\cos x) d x \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x}=\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}=\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}-1 \\ & \int d y=\int\left(\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}-1\right) d x \\ & \Rightarrow y=2 \tan \frac{x}{2}-x+C\end{aligned}$

General solution, $y=A-\frac{B}{x}\begin{aligned}

& x^2 y_1=B \\
& x^2 y_2+y_1 \times 2 x=0 \\
& \therefore \quad x\left(x y_2+2 y_1\right)=0

Differential Equation : $x y_2+2 y_1=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the solution of the differential equation
$\frac{d x}{d y}=\frac{x+y+1}{x+y-1} ?$
questions.solution:
Let $t=x+y \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d y}=\frac{d x}{d y}+1$
So, $\frac{d t}{d y}-1=\frac{t+1}{t-1}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d t}{d y}=\frac{t+1+t-1}{t-1}=\frac{2 t}{t-1} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{t-1}{t} d t=2 \int d y \\
& \Rightarrow \quad t-\log t=2 y+\mathrm{C}_1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x+y-\log (x+y)-2 y=\mathrm{C}_1 \\
& \Rightarrow y-x+\log (x+y)=-\mathrm{C}_1=\mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The general solution of $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{a x+h}{b y+k}$ represents a circle only when
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{a x+h}{b y+k} \\ & \Rightarrow(b y+k) d y=(a x+h) d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{by}^2}{2}+\mathrm{ky}=\frac{\mathrm{ax}^2}{2}+\mathrm{hx} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{by}^2+2 \mathrm{ky}=\mathrm{ax}^2+2 \mathrm{hx}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \mathrm{ax}^2-\mathrm{by}^2+2 \mathrm{hx}-2 \mathrm{ky}=0$

Integrating

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y \phi^{\prime}(x)-y^2}{\phi(x)}$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y \phi^{\prime}(x)-y^2}{\phi(x)}=\frac{y \phi^{\prime}(x)}{\phi(x)}-\frac{y^2}{\phi(x)} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y^2 \cdot \phi^{\prime}(x)}{y \cdot \phi(x)}-\frac{y^2}{\phi(x)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^2}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)=\frac{\phi^{\prime}(x)}{y \cdot \phi(x)}-\frac{1}{\phi(x)} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^2}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)-\frac{1}{y} \cdot \frac{\phi^{\prime}(x)}{\phi(x)}=\frac{-1}{\phi(x)}\end{aligned}$
Let $\mathrm{t}=\frac{-1}{\mathrm{y}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{y}^2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right)\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\mathrm{t} \cdot \frac{\phi^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})}{\phi(\mathrm{x})}=\frac{-1}{\phi(\mathrm{x})}I . F=e^{\int \frac{\phi^{\prime}(x)}{\phi(x)} \cdot d x}=e^{\log \phi(x)}=\phi(x)$
Solution of differential equation is
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{t} \cdot \phi(\mathrm{x}) & =\int \frac{-1}{\phi(\mathrm{x})} \times \phi(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{dx} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{-1}{\mathrm{y}} \phi(\mathrm{x}) & =-\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \frac{\phi(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=\frac{\phi(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x d y=y(d x+y d y) ; y(1)=1$ and $y(x) \gt 0$, then what is $y(-3)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& x d y=y d x+y^2 d y \\
& \Rightarrow x \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}=y+y^2 \cdot \frac{d y}{d x} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{y-x \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}}{y^2}=\frac{-d y}{d x}
\end{aligned}$
Integrating both sides
$\frac{x}{y}=-y+c$
Given, $\mathrm{x}=1, \mathrm{y}=1\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{1}=-1+\mathrm{c} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=2 \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{y}}+\mathrm{y}=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}^2=2 \mathrm{y} \\
& \Rightarrow-3+\mathrm{y}^2-2 \mathrm{y}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}^2-2 \mathrm{y}-3=0 \\
& \mathrm{y}=3,-1 \\
& \therefore \mathrm{y}=3
\end{aligned}$

On integration
$\begin{aligned}

questions.q: If $x d y=y d x+y^2 d y, y \gt 0$ and $y(1)=1$, then what is $y(-3)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } x d y=y d x+y^2 d y \\ & \Rightarrow 1=\frac{y}{x} \frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{y^2}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d y}+y=\frac{x}{y}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d y}-\frac{x}{y}=-y$  ...(1)
$\begin{aligned}
& P=-\frac{1}{y}, Q=-y \\

\end{aligned}$
Now, Solution of d.E.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{I} . \mathrm{F})=\int(\mathrm{Q} . \mathrm{I} . \mathrm{F} .) \mathrm{dy} \\
& \frac{x}{y}=\int \frac{1}{y}(-y) d y+C \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{x}{y}=\int-1 d y+C \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{x}{y}=-y+C \\
& y(1)=1
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{1}=-1+C \Rightarrow C=2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{y}=-y+2 \Rightarrow x=-y^2+2 y \\ & \Rightarrow y(-3) \Rightarrow-3=-y^2+2 y \\ & \Rightarrow y^2-2 y-3=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=\frac{+2 \pm \sqrt{4+12}}{2}=\frac{2 \pm 4}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow y=3,-1 \\ & \text {Since } y \gt 0 \text { so } y=3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What are the order and degree respectively of the differential equation whose solution is $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{cx}+\mathrm{c}^2-3 \mathrm{c}^{3 / 2}+2$, where c is a parameter?
questions.solution:
Given :
Solution of differential equation is
$y=c x+c^2-3 c^{\frac{3}{2}}+2$...(1)
To find order and degree of differential equation, we will find differential equation first.
Now differentiating equation (1) w.r.t. $x$ and putting value of $c$ to remove it, we get
$\frac{d y}{d x}=c\begin{aligned} & y=x \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2-3\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+2 \\ & \Rightarrow(y-2)^2+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^4+(2 x-9)\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^3\end{aligned}+\left(x^2-2 y+4\right)\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2+(-2 x y+4 x) \frac{d y}{d x}=0$
Hence order of differential equation is 1 and degree is 4 .

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the solution of the differential equation $\frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{x}{y}-y^2=0$ ?
where $c$ is an arbitrary constant.
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{x}{y}-y^2=0 \\
& \frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{x}{y}=y^2
\end{aligned}$
This is a linear differential equation of the form
$\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dy}}+\mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{Q}_1$
Here, $\mathrm{P}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{y}}$ and $\mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{y}^2\therefore \quad \text { I.F. }=\mathrm{e}^{\int P d y}=\mathrm{e}^{\int \frac{1}{y} d y}=\mathrm{e}^{\log y}=y$
So, required solution is
$\begin{aligned}
& x \cdot y=\int y^2 \cdot y d y+c \\
& x y=\int y^3 d y+c \\
& x y=\frac{y^4}{4}+c \\
& 4 x y=y^4+c
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (C) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The general solution of $\frac{d y}{d x}=f(x)+x$ is of the form $y=g(x)+c$, where $c$ is an arbitrary constant.
2. The degree of $\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=f(x)$ is 2 .
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement 1:
The general solution of $\frac{d y}{d x}=f(x)+x$ 
Now integrating on both side
$\int \frac{d y}{d x}=\int[f(x)+x] d x\therefore \quad y=f(x)+C\therefore \quad$ Statement 1 is correct.
Statement 2:
$\frac{d y}{d x}=f(x)+c$
Squaring both sides,
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=(f(x)+c)^2 \\
& \left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=\left[f(x)^2+2 \mathrm{cf}(x)+c^2\right]
\end{aligned}$
Hence, the differential equation is of order -1 and degree -2 .
$\therefore \quad$ both Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
$\therefore \quad$ Option (C) is correct.

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& y^2-2 a y+x^2=a^2 \\
& \Rightarrow y^2-2(y)(a)+a^2+x^2=a^2+a^2 \\
& \Rightarrow(y-a)^2+x^2=2 a^2...(i)
\end{aligned}$
Dift w.r.t $x\begin{aligned}
& 2(y-a) \cdot y^1+2 x=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(y-a) \cdot p=-x \\
& \Rightarrow y-a=\frac{-x}{p}...(ii) \\
& \Rightarrow a=y+\frac{x}{p}...(iii)
\end{aligned}\text { (i) } \Rightarrow\left(\frac{-x}{p}\right)^2+x^2=2\left(y+\frac{x}{p}\right)^2\begin{aligned}
& =2\left(\frac{(\mathrm{py}+\mathrm{x})^2}{\mathrm{p} 2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{p}^2 \mathrm{x}^2}{\mathrm{p}^2}=\frac{2\left(\mathrm{p}^2 \mathrm{y}^2+\mathrm{x}^2+2 \mathrm{pxy}\right)}{\mathrm{p}^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{p}^2 \mathrm{x}^2-2 \mathrm{p}^2 \mathrm{y}^2-2 \mathrm{x}^2-4 \mathrm{pxy}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow\left(\mathrm{x}^2-2 \mathrm{y}^2\right) \mathrm{p}^2-4 \mathrm{pxy}-\mathrm{x}^2=0
\end{aligned}$

$\therefore \frac{|m(0)-(0)+c|}{\sqrt{m^2+(-1)^2}}=1 \Rightarrow c=\sqrt{1+m^2}$
Now:
$\left[y-x \frac{d y}{d x}\right]^2=[m x+c-x m]^2 \Rightarrow c^2=1+m^2$
also,
$\left[y+x \frac{d y}{d x}\right]^2=[m x+c+m x]^2=\left[2 m x+\sqrt{1+m^2}\right]^2$
also, $1-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=1-m^2$ and $1+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=1+m^2\Rightarrow\left[y-x \frac{d y}{d x}\right]^2=1+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2$

For the following two (02) items:
Consider the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 4(5^x), & x \lt 0 \\ 8k + x, & x \geq 0 \end{cases}$.

What is $f'(-1)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
For $x \lt 0$, the function is given by $f(x) = 4(5^x)$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 4(5^x \ln 5)$

To find $f'(-1)$, substitute $x = -1$ into the derivative:

$f'(-1) = 4(5^{-1} \ln 5)$

$f'(-1) = \dfrac{4}{5}\ln 5$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{5}\ln 5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $x = \sec\theta - \cos\theta$ and $y = \sec^4\theta - \cos^4\theta$.

What is $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $x = \sec\theta - \cos\theta$ and $y = \sec^4\theta - \cos^4\theta$.

Differentiating $x$ with respect to $\theta$:
$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = \sec\theta \tan\theta + \sin\theta$
$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = \tan\theta (\sec\theta + \cos\theta)$

Differentiating $y$ with respect to $\theta$:
$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = 4\sec^3\theta (\sec\theta \tan\theta) - 4\cos^3\theta (-\sin\theta)$
$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = 4\sec^4\theta \tan\theta + 4\cos^3\theta \sin\theta$
$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = 4\tan\theta (\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)$

Now, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}}{\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}} = \dfrac{4\tan\theta (\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)}{\tan\theta (\sec\theta + \cos\theta)} = \dfrac{4(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)}{\sec\theta + \cos\theta}$

Squaring both sides:
$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)^2}{(\sec\theta + \cos\theta)^2}$

Using the algebraic identity $(a+b)^2 = (a-b)^2 + 4ab$, we can rewrite the numerator and denominator:
$(\sec\theta + \cos\theta)^2 = (\sec\theta - \cos\theta)^2 + 4\sec\theta\cos\theta = x^2 + 4$
$(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)^2 = (\sec^4\theta - \cos^4\theta)^2 + 4\sec^4\theta\cos^4\theta = y^2 + 4$

Substituting these values, we get:
$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16(y^2 + 4)}{x^2 + 4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{16(y^2+4)}{(x^2+4)}$

$(p+q) \ln(x+y) = p \ln x + q \ln y$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{p+q}{x+y} \left(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{p}{x} + \dfrac{q}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$\dfrac{p+q}{x+y} - \dfrac{p}{x} = \left( \dfrac{q}{y} - \dfrac{p+q}{x+y} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Simplifying the left side:

$\dfrac{x(p+q) - p(x+y)}{x(x+y)} = \dfrac{px + qx - px - py}{x(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx - py}{x(x+y)}$

Simplifying the right side:

$\dfrac{q(x+y) - y(p+q)}{y(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx + qy - py - qy}{y(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx - py}{y(x+y)}$

Equating the two sides:

$\dfrac{qx - py}{x(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx - py}{y(x+y)} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Canceling the common terms from both sides:

$\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}$

The derivative $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is $\dfrac{y}{x}$, which is independent of both $p$ and $q$.

Answer: is independent of both $p$ and $q$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\left(e^y\right)^x-y=0$, where $y$ is a function of $x$ whose domain is $(0,10]$.

Question: What is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to, given that $y=y_0$ when $x=1$ ?
questions.solution:
Given the equation $(e^y)^x - y = 0$, we can rewrite it as:

$e^{xy} = y$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$xy = \ln y$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$ using the product rule and chain rule:

$y + x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$y = \left( \dfrac{1}{y} - x \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$y = \left( \dfrac{1 - xy}{y} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^2}{1 - xy}$

We are given that at $x = 1$, $y = y_0$. Substituting these values into the derivative:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y_0^2}{1 - y_0}$

From the original equation $e^{xy} = y$, substituting $x = 1$ and $y = y_0$ gives:

$e^{y_0} = y_0$

To match the given options, we substitute $y_0 = e^{y_0}$ for one $y_0$ in the numerator and the $y_0$ in the denominator:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y_0 e^{y_0}}{1 - e^{y_0}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{y_0 e^{y_0}}{1-e^{y_0}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $y = \sin^{-1}\left(x - \dfrac{4x^3}{27}\right)$.

What is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $x = 3\sin\theta$. Then $\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$.

Substituting $x = 3\sin\theta$ into the given expression:

$y = \sin^{-1}\left(3\sin\theta - \dfrac{4(3\sin\theta)^3}{27}\right)$

$y = \sin^{-1}\left(3\sin\theta - \dfrac{4(27\sin^3\theta)}{27}\right)$

$y = \sin^{-1}(3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta)$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(3\theta) = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$:

$y = \sin^{-1}(\sin 3\theta)$

Assuming principal values, we get:

$y = 3\theta$

$y = 3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2}} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{x^2}{9}}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{9 - x^2}{9}}}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{9 - x^2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{9-x^2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following three (03) items:
Let $y = f(x) = \dfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + \ln\sqrt{1 - x^2}$.

If $x = \sin\theta$, then what is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $y = \dfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + \ln\sqrt{1 - x^2}$

Substitute $x = \sin\theta$ into the expression for $y$:

$y = \dfrac{\sin\theta \cdot \theta}{\sqrt{1 - \sin^2\theta}} + \ln\sqrt{1 - \sin^2\theta}$

$y = \dfrac{\theta\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} + \ln(\cos\theta)$

$y = \theta\tan\theta + \ln(\cos\theta)$

Differentiating $y$ with respect to $\theta$:

$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = \dfrac{d}{d\theta}(\theta\tan\theta) + \dfrac{d}{d\theta}(\ln(\cos\theta))$

$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = \left(\tan\theta + \theta\sec^2\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}(-\sin\theta)$

$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = \tan\theta + \theta\sec^2\theta - \tan\theta = \theta\sec^2\theta$

Differentiating $x = \sin\theta$ with respect to $\theta$:

$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = \cos\theta$

Using the chain rule to find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}}{\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}} = \dfrac{\theta\sec^2\theta}{\cos\theta}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \theta\sec^3\theta$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sqrt[4]{y}=x+\sqrt{x^2+4}$, then what is $\sqrt{x^2+4}\,\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Given $y^{1/4} = x + \sqrt{x^2+4}$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{1}{4} y^{-3/4} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x^2+4}} (2x)$

$\dfrac{1}{4} y^{-3/4} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+4}}$

$\dfrac{1}{4} y^{-3/4} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+4} + x}{\sqrt{x^2+4}}$

Substituting $x + \sqrt{x^2+4} = y^{1/4}$:

$\dfrac{1}{4} y^{-3/4} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^{1/4}}{\sqrt{x^2+4}}$

$\sqrt{x^2+4} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4 y^{1/4} y^{3/4}$

$\sqrt{x^2+4} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4y$

Answer: $4y$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $f:(-1,1) \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a differentiable function with $f(0)=-1$ and $f^{\prime}(0)=1$. Let $h(x)=f(2 f(x)+2)$ and $g(x)=(h(x))^2$.
Question: What is $g^{\prime}(0)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{f}:(-1,1) \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a differentiable function with $\mathrm{f}(0)=-1$ and $f^{\prime}(0)=1\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{n})=(\mathrm{h}(\mathrm{x}))^2$
Differentiate both side w.r.t $x\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=2(\mathrm{~h}(\mathrm{x})) \cdot \mathrm{h}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})\begin{aligned} & g^{\prime}(0)=2(h(0)) \cdot h^{\prime}(0) \\ & {\left[\because h^{\prime}(0)=2\right]} \\ & {\left[\because f^{\prime}(0)=-1\right]} \\ & =2 f(2+10)+2) \cdot 2 \\ & =2 f(2(-1)+2)=2 f(0) \cdot 2=(-2) \cdot 2=-4 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let a function f be defined on $\mathbb{R}-\{0\}$ and $2 f(x)+f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=x+3$
If f is differentiable, then what is $\quad(0.5)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Since, } 2 \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=\mathrm{x}+3 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{f}^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)=1 \\
& \text { Put } \mathrm{x}=2, \frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(2)-\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{f}^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1...(i) \\
& \text { and, } 2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-4 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(2)=1...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
after solving (i) \& (ii), we get
$\mathrm{f}^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=2, \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(2)=\frac{3}{4}$
So, $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(0.5)=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be two functions such that $g(x)=x-\frac{1}{x}$ and $f$ o $g(x)=x^3-\frac{1}{x^3}$.
What is $f^{\prime}(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\because f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are two functions
$\begin{aligned}
g(x) & =x-\frac{1}{x} \text { and } f o g(x)=x^3-\frac{1}{x^3} \\
f\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right) & =x^3-\frac{1}{x^3} \\
\Rightarrow f\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right) & =\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right)^3+3\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right)
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} f^{\prime}(x) & =3 x^2+3 \\ f^{\prime \prime}(x) & =6 x\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=|\ln | x| |$ where $0 \lt \mathrm{x} \lt 1$, then what is $f^{\prime}(0.5)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=|\ln | \mathrm{x}| | ; 0 \lt \mathrm{x} \lt 1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=-\ln \mathrm{x}$
Now, $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{-1}{x} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(0.5)=-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f^{\prime}(x)=\cos (\ln x)$ and $y \quad f\left(\begin{array}{ll}2 & 3\end{array}\right)$, then what is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Since, $y=f\left(\frac{2 x-3}{x}\right)\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\mathrm{f}^{\prime}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{x}-3}{\mathrm{x}}\right) \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{x}-3}{\mathrm{x}}\right)\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=f^{\prime}\left(\frac{2 x-3}{x}\right) \cdot\left(\frac{3}{x^2}\right) ...(i)\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3}{x^2} \cos \left(\ln \left(\frac{2 x-3}{x}\right)\right)
\end{aligned}$

Since, $1 \lt x \lt 2 \Rightarrow|\ln x|=\ln x$
and $0 \lt \ln x \lt \ln 2 \Rightarrow|\ln x|=-\ln x$
Hence $\mathrm{y}=$ fof $(x)=|\ln ||\ln x|=-\ln (\ln x)$,
for $\mid \lt x \lt 2y^{\prime}=\frac{-1}{\ln x} \times \frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow y^{\prime}=\frac{-1}{x \ln x}$

questions.q: What is the derivative of $\operatorname{cosec}\left(x^{\circ}\right)$ ?
questions.solution: $\frac{d}{d x} \operatorname{cosec}\left(x^{\circ}\right)=\frac{d}{d x} \operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{x \pi}{180}\right)=\frac{-\pi}{180} \operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right) \cdot \cot \left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right)=\frac{-\pi}{180} \operatorname{cosec}\left(x^{\circ}\right) \cdot \cot \left(x^{\circ}\right)$

questions.q: What is the derivative of $\sin ^2 x$ with respect to $\cos ^2 x$ ?
questions.solution: $\frac{d\left(\sin ^2 x\right)}{d\left(\cos ^2 x\right)}=\frac{\frac{d}{d x} \sin ^2 x}{\frac{d}{d} \cos ^2 x}=\frac{2 \sin x \cos x}{-2 \sin x \cos x}=-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y=\left(x^{\mathrm{x}}\right)^{\mathrm{x}}$ then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$y=\left(x^x\right)^x=x^{x^2}$
Taking $\ln$ both sides, we get $\ln y=x^2 \ln x$
Differentiate w.r.t to $x$.
$\frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x \ln x+x^2 \cdot \frac{1}{x}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=(x+2 x \ln x) \quad \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=x y(1+2 \ln x) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}-x y(1+2 \ln x)=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $y=\ln ^2\left(\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}\right)$, then what is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ at $x=0$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} y= & {\left[\ln \left(\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}\right)\right]^2 } \\ \frac{d y}{d x}= & 2 \ln \left(\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}\right) \times \frac{x^2+x+1}{x^2-x+1} \\ & \times \frac{(2 x-1)\left(x^2+x+1\right)-(2 x+1)\left(x^2-x+1\right)}{\left(x^2+x-1\right)^2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Put } x=0 \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{1+x^4+x^8}{1-x^2+x^4}\right)=a x+b x^3$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } f(x)=\frac{x^8+x^4+1}{x^4-x^2+1} \\ & =\frac{x^8+2 x^4+1-x^4}{x^4-x^2+1}=\frac{\left(x^4+1\right)^2-\left(x^2\right)^2}{\left(x^4-x^2+1\right)} \\ & =\frac{\left(x^4-x^2+1\right)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right)}{x^4-x^2+1} \\ & f(x)=x^4+x^2+1 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=4 x^3+2 x=a x+b x^3 \\ & \Rightarrow a=2, b=4 \Rightarrow b=2 \mathrm{a}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x^y y^x=1$, then what is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ at $(1,1)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{y}} \mathrm{y}^{\mathrm{x}}=1$
Taking log both sides
$\begin{aligned} & y \log x+x \log y=0 \\ & y^{\prime} \log x+\frac{y}{x}+\log y+\frac{x}{y} y^{\prime}=0\end{aligned}$
put $\mathrm{x}=1, \mathrm{y}=1\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{y}^{\prime} \log (1)+1+\log (1)+\mathrm{y}^{\prime}=0 \\ & 0+1+0+\mathrm{y}^{\prime}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}^1=-1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y=\left(x^x\right)^x$, then what is the value of $\frac{d y}{d x}$ at $x=1$ ?
questions.solution:
$y=\left(x^x\right)^x=(x)^{x^2}$
Taking log both side
$\log y=x^2 \log x\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x \cdot \log x+x^2 \cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ & \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x \log x+x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { put } x=1, y=1 \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=2 \log (1)+1=1\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Let $e^x=t$
Hence $e^{e^x}=e^t\frac{d}{d t} e^t=e^t=e^{e^x}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y=(1+x)\left(1+x^2\right)\left(1+x^4\right)\left(1+x^8\right)\left(1+x^{16}\right)$ then what is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ at $x=0$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& y=(1+x)(1+x)^2\left(1+x^4\right)\left(1+x^8\right)\left(1+x^{16}\right) \\
& \ln y=\ln (1+x)+\ln \left(1+x^2\right)+\ln \left(1+x^4\right)+\ln \left(1+x^8\right) \\
& +\ln \left(1+x^{16}\right) \\
& \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{1-x}+\frac{2 x}{1+x^2}+\frac{4 x^3}{1+x^4}+\frac{8 x^7}{1+x^8}+\frac{16 x^{15}}{1+x^{16}} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}=y\left[\frac{1}{1+x}+\frac{2 x}{1+x^2}+\frac{4 x^3}{1+x^4}+\frac{8 x^7}{1+x^8}+\frac{16 x^{15}}{1+x^{16}}\right]
\end{aligned}$
Put $x=0\frac{d y}{d x}=1[1+0+0+0+0]=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\left(e^y\right)^x-y=0$, where $y$ is a function of $x$ whose domain is $(0,10]$.

Question: What is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Given equation is $(e^y)^x - y = 0$

$e^{xy} = y$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides:

$xy = \ln(y)$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$y + x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$y = \left( \dfrac{1}{y} - x \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$y = \left( \dfrac{1 - xy}{y} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^2}{1 - xy}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $(x+y)^{p+q} = x^p y^q$, where $p$, $q$ are positive integers.

If $p + q = 10$, then what is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $(x+y)^{p+q} = x^p y^q$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides:

$(p+q) \ln(x+y) = p \ln x + q \ln y$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{p+q}{x+y} \left(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{p}{x} + \dfrac{q}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$\dfrac{p+q}{x+y} - \dfrac{p}{x} = \left( \dfrac{q}{y} - \dfrac{p+q}{x+y} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{x(p+q) - p(x+y)}{x(x+y)} = \left( \dfrac{q(x+y) - y(p+q)}{y(x+y)} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{qx - py}{x(x+y)} = \left( \dfrac{qx - py}{y(x+y)} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}$

The result is independent of the value of $p+q$.

Answer: $\dfrac{y}{x}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following three (03) items:
Let $y = f(x) = \dfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + \ln\sqrt{1 - x^2}$.

What is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $x = 0$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $y = \dfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + \ln\sqrt{1 - x^2}$

We can rewrite the function as:
$y = \dfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1 - x^2)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the quotient and chain rules:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left(\sin^{-1} x + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right)\sqrt{1 - x^2} - x\sin^{-1} x \left(\dfrac{-x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right)}{1 - x^2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{-2x}{1 - x^2}\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - x^2}\sin^{-1} x + x + \dfrac{x^2\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}}{1 - x^2} - \dfrac{x}{1 - x^2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{(1 - x^2)\sin^{-1} x + x\sqrt{1 - x^2} + x^2\sin^{-1} x}{(1 - x^2)^{3/2}} - \dfrac{x}{1 - x^2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sin^{-1} x + x\sqrt{1 - x^2}}{(1 - x^2)^{3/2}} - \dfrac{x}{1 - x^2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sin^{-1} x}{(1 - x^2)^{3/2}} + \dfrac{x}{1 - x^2} - \dfrac{x}{1 - x^2} = \dfrac{\sin^{-1} x}{(1 - x^2)^{3/2}}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} (1 - x^2)^{3/2} - \sin^{-1} x \cdot \dfrac{3}{2}(1 - x^2)^{1/2}(-2x)}{(1 - x^2)^3}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{(1 - x^2) + 3x\sqrt{1 - x^2}\sin^{-1} x}{(1 - x^2)^3}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{1}{(1 - x^2)^2} + \dfrac{3x\sin^{-1} x}{(1 - x^2)^{5/2}}$

Substituting $x = 0$ into the second derivative:
$\left. \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \right|_{x=0} = \dfrac{1}{(1 - 0)^2} + 0 = 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y=\cos x \cdot \cos 4 x \cdot \cos 8 x$, then what is $\frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}$ at $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& y=\cos x \cdot \cos 4 x \cdot \cos 8 x \\
& \ln y=\ln (\cos x)+\ln (\cos 4 x)+\ln (\cos 8 x) \\
& \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=-\tan x-4 \tan 4 x-8 \tan 8 x
\end{aligned}$
Put $x=\frac{\pi}{4}\frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=-1-4(0)-8(0)-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial function such that $f \circ f(x)=x^4$. What is $f^{\prime}(1)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \text { Let } f(x)=x^2 \\ & \therefore f[f(x)]=\left(x^2\right)^2=x^4 \\ & \therefore f^{\prime}(x)=2 x \\ & f^{\prime}(1)=2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the derivative of $\sin (\ln x)+\cos (\ln x)$ with respect to $x$ at $x=e$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} y & =\sin (\ln x)+\cos (\ln x) \\ \frac{d y}{d x} & =\frac{d}{d x}(\sin (\ln x))+\frac{d}{d x}(\cos (\ln x)) \\ & =\cos (\ln x) \cdot \frac{1}{x}+\{-\sin (\ln x)\} \cdot \frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} &= \frac{\cos (\ln x)-\sin (\ln x)}{x} \\ &\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{x=e}=\frac{\cos (\ln e)-\sin (\ln e)}{e}=\frac{\cos (1)-\sin (1)}{e}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $x = \sec\theta - \cos\theta$ and $y = \sec^4\theta - \cos^4\theta$.

What is $\left(\dfrac{x^2+4}{y^2+4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\left[(x^2+4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 16y\right]$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $x = \sec\theta - \cos\theta$ and $y = \sec^4\theta - \cos^4\theta$.

First, we simplify $x^2 + 4$ and $y^2 + 4$:
$x^2 + 4 = (\sec\theta - \cos\theta)^2 + 4 = \sec^2\theta + \cos^2\theta - 2 + 4 = (\sec\theta + \cos\theta)^2$
$y^2 + 4 = (\sec^4\theta - \cos^4\theta)^2 + 4 = \sec^8\theta + \cos^8\theta - 2 + 4 = (\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)^2$

Differentiating $x$ and $y$ with respect to $\theta$:
$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = \sec\theta\tan\theta + \sin\theta = \tan\theta(\sec\theta + \cos\theta)$
$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = 4\sec^3\theta(\sec\theta\tan\theta) - 4\cos^3\theta(-\sin\theta) = 4\tan\theta(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)$

Now, finding $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}}{\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}} = \dfrac{4\tan\theta(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)}{\tan\theta(\sec\theta + \cos\theta)} = \dfrac{4(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)}{\sec\theta + \cos\theta}$

Squaring both sides:
$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16(\sec^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)^2}{(\sec\theta + \cos\theta)^2} = \dfrac{16(y^2+4)}{x^2+4}$

Rearranging the equation:
$(x^2+4)\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 16(y^2+4)$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:
$2x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + (x^2+4) \cdot 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} \cdot \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 16 \cdot 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Dividing the entire equation by $2\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x^2+4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 16y$
$\Rightarrow (x^2+4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 16y = -x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Substituting this into the given expression:
$\left(\dfrac{x^2+4}{y^2+4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\left[(x^2+4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 16y\right] = \left(\dfrac{x^2+4}{y^2+4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\left(-x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)$

This simplifies to:
$-x\left(\dfrac{x^2+4}{y^2+4}\right)\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$

Substituting $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16(y^2+4)}{x^2+4}$ into the expression:
$-x\left(\dfrac{x^2+4}{y^2+4}\right)\left(\dfrac{16(y^2+4)}{x^2+4}\right) = -16x$

Answer: $-16x$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the derivative of $e^x$ with respect to $x^e$ ?
questions.solution: Let $y=e^x, \frac{d y}{d x}=e^x\begin{aligned} & \text { and } z=x^e \Rightarrow \frac{d z}{d x}=e \cdot x^{(e-1)} \\ & \text {Now, } \frac{d y}{d z}=\frac{d y / d x}{d z / d x}=\frac{e^x}{e \cdot x^{(e-1)}}=\frac{x \cdot e^x}{e \cdot x^e}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x=e^t \cos t$ and $y=e^t \sin t$, then what is $\frac{d x}{d y}$ at $t=0$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & x=e^t \cdot \cos t \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d t}=e^t \cdot \cos t-e^t \cdot \sin t \\ & y=e^t \cdot \sin t \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d t}=e^t \cdot \sin t+e^t \cdot \cos t\end{aligned}\frac{d x}{d y}=\frac{\frac{d x}{d t}}{\frac{d y}{d t}}=\frac{e^t(\cos t-\sin t)}{e^t(\sin t+\cos t)}=\frac{\cos t-\sin t}{\sin t+\cos t}\left.\frac{d x}{d y}\right|_{t=0}=\frac{\cos 0-\sin 0}{\sin 0+\cos 0}=\frac{1-0}{0+1}=1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the derivative of $\tan ^{-1} x$ with respect to $\cot ^{-1} x$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $y=\tan ^{-1} x$; and $z=\cot ^{-1} x$
Then, $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{1+x^2}$ and $\frac{d z}{d x}=-\frac{1}{1+x^2}$
Now, $\frac{d y}{d z}=\frac{\frac{d y}{d x}}{\frac{d z}{d x}}=\frac{\frac{1}{1+x^2}}{-\left(\frac{1}{1+x^2}\right)}=-1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $e^{\theta \varphi}=c+4 \theta \varphi$, where $c$ is an arbitrary constant and $\varphi$ is a function of $\theta$, then what is $\varphi \mathrm{d} \theta$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  e^{\theta \phi}=C+4 \theta \cdot \phi \\
& \text { ( } \theta \cdot \phi) \ln e=\ln (C+4 \theta \cdot \phi) \\
& \theta \cdot \phi=\ln (C+4 \theta \cdot \phi) \\
& \Rightarrow \theta \cdot g \phi=4\{\ln (\theta)+\ln (\phi)\}+\ln C
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating both sides with respect to ' $\theta$ '.
$\begin{aligned} & \phi+\theta \cdot \frac{d \phi}{d \theta}=4\left(\frac{1}{\theta}+\frac{1}{\phi} \cdot \frac{d \phi}{d \theta}\right) \\ & \phi \cdot d \theta+\theta \cdot d \phi=4 \phi \cdot d \theta+4 \cdot \theta \cdot d \phi\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3 \theta \cdot d \phi=-3 \phi \cdot d \theta \\ & \therefore \phi \cdot d \theta=-\theta \cdot d \phi\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x^m y^n=a^{m+n}$, then what is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$x^m y^n=a^{m+n}\frac{x^m}{a^m}=\frac{a^n}{y^n}$ (i)
Differentiating equation (i) w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{m \cdot x^{(m-1)}}{a^m}=\frac{a^n \cdot(-n)}{y^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{m \cdot y^{(n+1)} \cdot(x)^{(m-1)}}{-n \cdot a^m \cdot a^n}=-\frac{m y}{n \cdot x} \cdot\left(\frac{x^m \cdot y^n}{a^{m+n}}\right)=-\frac{m y}{n x}(1)=-\frac{m y}{n x}$

Paragraph: Consider the equation $x^y=e^{x-y}$
Question: What is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ at $x=1$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  x^y=e^{x-y} \\
& \left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{x=1}=? \\
& \text { at } x=1 ; x^y=e^{x-y} \\
& \Rightarrow 1=e^{1-y} \\
& \Rightarrow y=1 \\
& \because x^y=e^{x-y} \\
& \Rightarrow y, \ln x=x-y
\end{aligned}$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow y \cdot \frac{1}{x}=1-y^1-\ln x \cdot y^1 \\
& \Rightarrow 1-\frac{y}{x}=y^1(1+\ln x) \\
& \Rightarrow y^1=\frac{x-y}{x(1+\ell \mathrm{n} x)} \\
& \therefore y^1 \text { at } x=1 \\
& =\frac{1-1}{1(1+0)}=0
\end{aligned}$

for $x=0.5, f(x)=-\ln xf^{\prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{x}f^{\prime}(0.5)=-\frac{1}{0.5}=-2$

questions.solution: Let $\mathrm{y}=\sec ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } \tan ^{-1} x=\theta \Rightarrow x=\tan \theta \\ & y=\sec ^2 \theta=1+\tan ^2 \theta=1+x^2 \\ & \therefore \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d}{d x}\left(1+x^2\right)=2 x\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{5-2 \tan \sqrt{x}}{2+5 \tan \sqrt{x}}\right)$, then what is $\frac{d y}{d x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{5-2 \tan \sqrt{x}}{2+5 \tan \sqrt{x}}\right) \\ & =\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{5}{2}-\tan \sqrt{x}}{1+\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) \tan \sqrt{x}}\right) \\ & =\tan ^{-1} \frac{5}{2}-\tan ^{-1} \tan \sqrt{x} \\ & =\tan ^{-1} \frac{5}{2}-\sqrt{x} \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the derivative of the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{e}^{\tan \mathrm{x}}+\ln (\sec \mathrm{x})-\mathrm{e}^{\ln \mathrm{x}} \text { at } \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{4} ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(x)=e^{\tan x}+\ln (\sec x)-e^{\ln x} \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=e^{\tan x} \cdot \sec ^2 x+\frac{1}{\sec x} \cdot \sec x \tan x-1 \\ & \qquad\left(\because e^{\ln x}=x \text { and } \frac{d}{d x}(x)=1\right) \\ & f^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=e^{\tan \frac{\pi}{4}} \cdot \sec ^2 \frac{\pi}{4}+\tan \frac{\pi}{4}-1=2 \mathrm{e}+1-1 \\ & =2 \mathrm{e}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is an even function, where $f(x) \neq 0$, then which one of the following is correct?
options: $f^{\prime}(x)$ may be an even or odd function depending on the type of function
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is an even function.
Let's see some examples
(1) If $f(x)=\cos x$, which is even function, $f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-\sin \mathrm{x}$, which is odd function.
(2) If $f(x)=x^2$, which is even function, $f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=2 \mathrm{x}$, which is odd function.

questions.q: If $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}^2} \sin 2 \mathrm{x}$, then what is $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}$ at $\mathrm{x}=\pi$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & y=e^{x^2} \cdot \sin 2 x \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=2 \cdot e^{x^2} \cdot \cos 2 x+2 x e^{x^2} \cdot \sin 2 x \\ & =2 e^{x^2}(\cos 2 x+x \sin 2 x) \\ & \left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{x=\pi}=2 e^{\pi^2}(\cos 2 \pi+\pi \cdot \sin 2 \pi) \\ & =2 e^{\pi^2}(1+0)=2 \cdot e^{\pi^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{y}=(\cos \mathrm{x})^{(\cos \mathrm{x})^{(\cos x)^{\frac{\infty}{x}}}}$, then $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & y=(\cos x)^{(\cos x)^{\cos x \cdots}} \\ & \Rightarrow y=(\cos x)^y\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \log y=y \cdot \log \cos x$
Differentiating on both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{y} \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}=y(-\tan x)+\log \cos x \cdot \frac{d y}{d x} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}\left(\frac{1}{y}-\log \cos x\right)=-y \tan x\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-y \tan x}{\frac{1}{y}-\log \cos x}=\frac{-y^2 \tan x}{1-y \log \cos x}$

If $l_1=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}\right)\begin{aligned} & l_2=\lim _{\mathrm{h} \rightarrow 0} \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\sin (\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{h})}-\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{h}} \\ & l_3=\int \mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}} \cos \mathrm{xdx}\end{aligned}$
then which one of the following is correct?

$\begin{aligned} & l_1=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}\right) \\ & l_2=\lim _{\mathrm{h} \rightarrow 0} \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\sin (\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{h})}-\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{h}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & l_3=\int \mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}} \cdot \cos \mathrm{xdx} \\ & l_2=\lim _{\mathrm{h} \rightarrow 0} \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\sin (\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{h})}-\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{h}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}\right)=l_1\end{aligned}l_3=\int \mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}} \cdot \cos \mathrm{xdx}$
Let $\sin \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \cos \mathrm{xdx}=\mathrm{dt}l_3=\int \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \mathrm{dt}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{c}=\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{c}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(l_3\right)=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{c}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\mathrm{e}^{\sin \mathrm{x}}\right)=l_1=l_2$

Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a function such that
$f(x)=x^3+x^2 f^{\prime}(1)+x f f^{\prime \prime}(2)+f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)$
for $\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$
What is $\mathrm{f}(1)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=x^3+x^2 f^{\prime}(1)+\mathrm{x} f^{\prime \prime}(2)+f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)...(1) \\
& f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2+2 x f^{\prime}(1)+f^{\prime \prime}(2)...(2) \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(x)=6 \mathrm{x}+2 f^{\prime}(1)...(3) \\
& f^{\prime \prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=6...(4) \\
& f^{\prime}(1)=3+2 f^{\prime}(1)+f^{\prime \prime}(2)...(5) \\
& f^{\prime}(2)=12+2 f^{\prime}(1)...(6)
\end{aligned}$
Using (6) in (5), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(1)=3+2 f^{\prime}(1)+12+2 f^{\prime \prime}(1)-3 f^{\prime}(1)=15 \\
& f^{\prime}(1)=-5
\end{aligned}$
Using this value in eqn (6) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(2)=12+2 \times(-5) \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(2)=2
\end{aligned}$
Using $x=3$ in eqn (4),
$f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)=6$
Putting value of $f^{\prime}(1)+f^{\prime \prime}(2)$ and $f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)$ in eqn (1) We get
$\begin{aligned}
f(x) & =x^3+x^2(-5)+x(2)+6 \\
& =x^3-5 x^2+2 x+6
\end{aligned}$
Putting $x=1\begin{aligned}
& f(1)=(1)^3-5(1)^2+2(1)+6 \\
& f(1)=4
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $x^a y^b=(x-y)^{a+b}$, then the value of $\frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$x^a y^b=(x-y)^{a+b}$
taking log both the sides.
$\begin{aligned}
& \log \left(x^a y^b\right)=\log (x-y)^{(a+b)} \\
& \text { a logx }+b \operatorname{logy}=(a+b) \log (x-y) \\
& \text { differentiating both sides w.r. }{ }^{\prime} x^{\prime} . \\
& \frac{a}{x}+\frac{b}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(a+b)}{(x-y)}\left[1-\frac{d y}{d x}\right] \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{b}{y}+\frac{a+b}{x-y}\right]=\frac{a+b}{x-y}-\frac{a}{x} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{b x-b y+a y+b y}{y(x-y)}\right]=\frac{a x+b x-a x+}{x(x-y)} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{b x+a y}{y}\right]=\frac{b x+a y}{x} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{x} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x}=0
\end{aligned}$

Let equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{b^2}+\frac{y^2}{a^2}=1\therefore \quad$ It passes through $(3,2)$ and $(1,6)\therefore \frac{9}{b^2}+\frac{4}{a^2}=1$ ...(i)

questions.q:
Passage: The foci of the ellipse $px^2+16y^2=16p$ and the foci of the hyperbola $25(81x^2-144y^2)=11664$ coincide (assume $p\lt 16$).

Question: What is the value of $p$ ?
questions.solution:
The equation of the ellipse is $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{p} = 1$.

Since $p \lt 16$, the major axis is along the x-axis. The foci are given by $(\pm \sqrt{a^2 - b^2}, 0) = (\pm \sqrt{16 - p}, 0)$.

The equation of the hyperbola is $25(81x^2 - 144y^2) = 11664$, which can be rewritten as $\dfrac{x^2}{144/25} - \dfrac{y^2}{81/25} = 1$.

For the hyperbola, $a^2 = \dfrac{144}{25}$ and $b^2 = \dfrac{81}{25}$. The foci are given by $(\pm \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}, 0) = \left(\pm \sqrt{\dfrac{144}{25} + \dfrac{81}{25}}, 0\right) = \left(\pm \sqrt{\dfrac{225}{25}}, 0\right) = (\pm 3, 0)$.

Since the foci of the ellipse and the hyperbola coincide, we have $\sqrt{16 - p} = 3$.

Squaring both sides, we get $16 - p = 9 \Rightarrow p = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.q: If any point on an ellipse is $(3\sin\alpha, 5\cos\alpha)$, then what is the eccentricity of the ellipse?
questions.solution:
Let $x = 3\sin\alpha$ and $y = 5\cos\alpha$.

$\dfrac{x}{3} = \sin\alpha$ and $\dfrac{y}{5} = \cos\alpha$

Squaring and adding both equations:

$\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{25} = \sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1$

This represents an ellipse with $a^2 = 9$ and $b^2 = 25$.

Since $b \gt a$, the eccentricity $e$ is given by $a^2 = b^2(1 - e^2)$.

$9 = 25(1 - e^2)$

$1 - e^2 = \dfrac{9}{25}$

$e^2 = \dfrac{16}{25}$

$e = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{5}$

It's foci are $\mathrm{S}_1(a e, o)$ and $\mathrm{S}_2(-a e, o)$ and the extremity of the minor axis is $\mathrm{B}(o, b)$ Then, slope of $\mathrm{BS}_2=\frac{b-o}{o-(-a e)}=\frac{b}{a e}$ and $\quad$ slope of $\mathrm{BS}_1=\frac{b-o}{o-a e}=-\frac{b}{a e}$ The product of slopes $=\frac{b}{a e} \times-\frac{b}{a e}=-1\Rightarrow \quad b^2=a^2 e^2\Rightarrow \quad e^2=\frac{b^2}{a^2} \qquad$ ....(i) We have,$e=\frac{c}{a}\Rightarrow \quad c=\sqrt{a^2-b^2}\Rightarrow \quad e^2=1-\frac{b^2}{a^2}=1-e^2 \quad[$ from $(i)]\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & 2 e^2 & =1 \\ \Rightarrow & & e^2 & =\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

Passage: The foci of the ellipse $px^2+16y^2=16p$ and the foci of the hyperbola $25(81x^2-144y^2)=11664$ coincide (assume $p\lt 16$).

Question: What is the difference between the eccentricities of the hyperbola and the ellipse ?
questions.solution:
The equation of the ellipse can be written as $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{p} = 1$.

Since $p \lt 16$, the major axis is along the x-axis. The eccentricity $e_1$ of the ellipse is given by $e_1 = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{p}{16}}$.

The foci of the ellipse are $(\pm 4e_1, 0) = \left(\pm 4\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{p}{16}}, 0\right) = (\pm \sqrt{16 - p}, 0)$.

The equation of the hyperbola is $25(81x^2 - 144y^2) = 11664$.

Dividing by $11664$, we get $\dfrac{25x^2}{144} - \dfrac{25y^2}{81} = 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2}{144/25} - \dfrac{y^2}{81/25} = 1$.

The eccentricity $e_2$ of the hyperbola is $e_2 = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{81/25}{144/25}} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{81}{144}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{225}{144}} = \dfrac{15}{12} = \dfrac{5}{4} = 1.25$.

The foci of the hyperbola are $(\pm A e_2, 0) = \left(\pm \dfrac{12}{5} \times \dfrac{5}{4}, 0\right) = (\pm 3, 0)$.

Since the foci of the ellipse and the hyperbola coincide, we have $\sqrt{16 - p} = 3 \Rightarrow 16 - p = 9 \Rightarrow p = 7$.

The eccentricity of the ellipse is $e_1 = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{7}{16}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{16}} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$.

The difference between the eccentricities is $e_2 - e_1 = 1.25 - 0.75 = 0.5$.

Answer: $0\cdot5$

What is the domain of the function?
questions.solution:
The given function is $f(x) = 1 - \sqrt[3]{(x-1)^2}$.

The expression inside the cube root is $(x-1)^2$, which is a polynomial and is defined for all real values of $x$.

Since the cube root of any real number is well-defined for all real numbers, the function $f(x)$ is defined for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Therefore, the domain of the function is $(-\infty, \infty)$.

Answer: $(-\infty, \infty)$

Let the function $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$, where $x \neq 2n\pi$ and $n$ is an integer.

What is the range of the function?
questions.solution:
Given function is $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x}$

The range of $\cos x$ is $[-1, 1]$.

Since $x \neq 2n\pi$, $\cos x \neq 1$.

Therefore, $-1 \le \cos x \lt 1$

Multiplying by $-1$, we get $-1 \lt -\cos x \le 1$

Adding $1$, we get $0 \lt 1 - \cos x \le 2$

Taking the reciprocal, we get $\dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x} \ge \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $y \ge 0.5$

The range of the function is $[0.5, \infty)$.

Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{10^x - 10^{-x}}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$.

What is $f \circ f \circ f \circ f \circ f(0)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given the function $f(x) = \dfrac{10^x - 10^{-x}}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$

Substituting $x = 0$ into the function:

$f(0) = \dfrac{10^0 - 10^{-0}}{10^0 + 10^{-0}}$

$f(0) = \dfrac{1 - 1}{1 + 1} = 0$

Since $f(0) = 0$, applying the function $f$ repeatedly to $0$ will always result in $0$.

$f(f(0)) = f(0) = 0$

$f(f(f(0))) = f(0) = 0$

$f(f(f(f(0)))) = f(0) = 0$

$f(f(f(f(f(0))))) = f(0) = 0$

Therefore, $f \circ f \circ f \circ f \circ f(0) = 0$

Answer: $0$

Consider the following statements in respect of the function $f(x)=x$ in the interval $(-1,1)$ :
I. The function attains maximum value.
II. The function attains minimum value.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.solution:
Given the function $f(x) = x$ defined on the open interval $(-1, 1)$.

For any $x \in (-1, 1)$, we have $-1 \lt f(x) \lt 1$.

Since the interval is open, $x$ can be arbitrarily close to $1$ but never equals $1$. Thus, $f(x)$ does not attain a maximum value in the given interval.

Similarly, $x$ can be arbitrarily close to $-1$ but never equals $-1$. Thus, $f(x)$ does not attain a minimum value in the given interval.

Therefore, neither statement I nor statement II is correct.

Answer: Neither I nor II

Question: What is the number of points of intersection of the curves ?
questions.solution:
Equating the two given curves $y = x^2$ and $y = 2|x|$:

$x^2 = 2|x|$

Since $x^2 = |x|^2$, the equation becomes:

$|x|^2 - 2|x| = 0$

$|x|(|x| - 2) = 0$

This gives $|x| = 0$ or $|x| = 2$.

Solving for $x$, we get $x = 0$, $x = 2$, and $x = -2$.

The corresponding points of intersection are $(0, 0)$, $(2, 4)$, and $(-2, 4)$.

The number of points of intersection is $3$.

Answer: $3$

Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{1 - x}$ ($x \gt 0$, $x \neq 1$).

What is $(1 - x)f(\sqrt{x}) + xf(\sqrt{x} + 1)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{1 - x}$

Substitute $\sqrt{x}$ in $f(x)$:

$f(\sqrt{x}) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 - \sqrt{x}}$

Substitute $\sqrt{x} + 1$ in $f(x)$:

$f(\sqrt{x} + 1) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{1 - (\sqrt{x} + 1)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{-\sqrt{x}}$

Now, evaluate the given expression:

$(1 - x)f(\sqrt{x}) + xf(\sqrt{x} + 1) = (1 - x)\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 - \sqrt{x}}\right) + x\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{-\sqrt{x}}\right)$

Using $1 - x = (1 - \sqrt{x})(1 + \sqrt{x})$:

$= (1 - \sqrt{x})(1 + \sqrt{x})\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 - \sqrt{x}}\right) - \sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} + 1)$

$= \sqrt{x}(1 + \sqrt{x}) - \sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} + 1)$

$= 0$

Answer: $0$

What is $f(16)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $f\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = \dfrac{f(x)}{f(y)}$

Substituting $x = 1$ and $y = 1$, we get $f(1) = 1$

Substituting $x = 1$, we get $f\left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) = \dfrac{f(1)}{f(y)} = \dfrac{1}{f(y)}$

Replacing $y$ with $\dfrac{1}{y}$ in the given equation, we get:

$f(xy) = \dfrac{f(x)}{f\left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right)} = f(x)f(y)$

Using this property, $f(16) = f(2^4) = (f(2))^4$

Given $f(2) = 3$, we have $f(16) = 3^4 = 81$

Answer: $81$

questions.solution:
Given $f(xy) = f(x+y)$ for all real values of $x$ and $y$.

Substituting $y = 0$, we get $f(x \cdot 0) = f(x + 0)$, which simplifies to $f(0) = f(x)$ for all real $x$.

This implies that $f(x)$ is a constant function for all real values of $x$.

Since $f(5) = 10$, the constant value of the function is $10$. Thus, $f(x) = 10$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

We need to find the value of $f(20) + f(-20)$.

questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{1 - x}$ ($x \gt 0$, $x \neq 1$).

What is $\dfrac{f(x)}{f(x+1)}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{1 - x}$

Substitute $x+1$ for $x$ to find $f(x+1)$:

$f(x+1) = \dfrac{x+1}{1 - (x+1)} = \dfrac{x+1}{-x}$

Now, calculate the ratio $\dfrac{f(x)}{f(x+1)}$:

$\dfrac{f(x)}{f(x+1)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{1 - x}}{\dfrac{x+1}{-x}}$

$\dfrac{f(x)}{f(x+1)} = \dfrac{x}{1 - x} \times \dfrac{-x}{x+1} = \dfrac{-x^2}{1 - x^2}$

Since $f(x^2) = \dfrac{x^2}{1 - x^2}$, we get:

$\dfrac{f(x)}{f(x+1)} = -f(x^2)$

Answer: $-f(x^2)$

questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{10^x - 10^{-x}}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$.

What is the inverse of the function?
questions.solution:
Let $y = f(x) = \dfrac{10^x - 10^{-x}}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$

Multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $10^x$, we get:

$y = \dfrac{10^{2x} - 1}{10^{2x} + 1}$

Applying componendo and dividendo:

$\dfrac{1 + y}{1 - y} = \dfrac{10^{2x} + 1 + 10^{2x} - 1}{10^{2x} + 1 - (10^{2x} - 1)}$

$\dfrac{1 + y}{1 - y} = \dfrac{2 \cdot 10^{2x}}{2}$

$10^{2x} = \dfrac{1 + y}{1 - y}$

Taking logarithm to the base $10$ on both sides:

$2x = \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{1 + y}{1 - y}\right)$

$x = \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{1 + y}{1 - y}\right)$

Replacing $y$ with $x$ to find the inverse function:

$f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right)$

Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $f = \{(1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 7), (4, 10)\}$.

Consider the following statements:
I. $f$ is one-one function.
II. $f$ is onto function if the codomain is the set of natural numbers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The given function is $f = \{(1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 7), (4, 10)\}$.

The domain of $f$ is $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and the range of $f$ is $\{1, 4, 7, 10\}$.

Since each element in the domain has a distinct image in the range, $f$ is a one-one function. Statement I is correct.

If the codomain is the set of natural numbers, the range $\{1, 4, 7, 10\}$ is a proper subset of the codomain. Since the range is not equal to the codomain, $f$ is not an onto function. Statement II is incorrect.

Therefore, only Statement I is correct.

Answer: I only

&  f(x)=2 x-x^2 \\

questions.q: A function satisfies $f(x-y)=\frac{f(x)}{f(y)}$, where $f(y) \neq 0$. If $f(1)=0.5$, then what is $f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5)+f(6)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Since, } \mathrm{f}(2-1)=\mathrm{f}(1)=\frac{\mathrm{f}(2)}{\mathrm{f}(1)} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(2)=(\mathrm{f}(1))^2=\frac{5}{10} \times \frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{4} \\ & \mathrm{f}(3-2)=\mathrm{f}(1)=\frac{\mathrm{f}(3)}{\mathrm{f}(2)} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{f}(3)}{\frac{1}{4}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(3)=\frac{1}{8} \\ & \text {Similarly we get } \mathrm{f}(4)=\frac{1}{16}, \mathrm{f}(5)=\frac{1}{32}, \mathrm{f}(6)=\frac{1}{64} \\ & \text {Now, } \mathrm{f}(2)+\mathrm{f}(3)+\mathrm{f}(4)+\mathrm{f}(5)+\mathrm{f}(6) \\ & \quad=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{32}+\frac{1}{64}=\frac{31}{64}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A function f defined by $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)$ is
questions.solution:
$f(x)=\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)\begin{aligned} & f(-x)=\ln \left(\sqrt{(-x)^2+1}-(-x)\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\frac{\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x\right)\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\frac{x^2+1-x^2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\right) \\ & =\ln \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\right) \\ & =-\ln \left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right) \\ & =-\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})\end{aligned}$
So, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is odd function.

Given, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=|\mathrm{x}+1|$.

$\begin{aligned}

$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{f}(|\mathrm{x}|)=\| \mathrm{x}|+1| \\
& |\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})|=|\mathrm{x}+1||=|\mathrm{x}+1| \\
& \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \neq|\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})|
\end{aligned}$
(c)
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})=|\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+1| \\
& \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{y})=|\mathrm{x}+1|+|\mathrm{y}+1| \\
& \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}) \neq \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{y}))
\end{aligned}$

Given internal, $[0,2]$

roots are $\frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16-4}}{2}=\frac{4 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2}=2 \pm \sqrt{3}$

questions.solution:
$f(x)=4 \sin x-3 \cos x+1$
To find range of this function, we have to find maximum and minimum values.
We know, for a $\sin \theta+\mathrm{b} \cos \theta+\mathrm{c}$, max value is $\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}+\mathrm{c}$ and minimum value is $-\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}+\mathrm{c}$.
$\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}$
Minimum value $=-\sqrt{16+9+1}=-5+1=-4\therefore$ Range, $\mathrm{S} \in[-4,6]$

questions.q:
Consider the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{27\left(\mathrm{x}^{2 / 3}-\mathrm{x}\right)}{4}$
How many solutions does the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=1$ have?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} f(x) & =\frac{27}{4}\left(x^{2 / 3}-x\right) \\ & =\frac{27}{4}\left(\left(x^2\right)^{1 / 3}-x\right)\end{aligned}$ For $f(x)=1\begin{aligned} & \frac{27}{4}\left(\left(x^2\right)^{1 / 3}-x\right)=1 \\ & \left(x^{1 / 3}\right)^2-x=\frac{4}{27} \end{aligned}$ Put $x^{1 / 3}=yx=y^3\begin{aligned} & y^2-y^3=\frac{4}{27} \\ & \Rightarrow y^3-y^2+\frac{4}{27}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 27 y^3-27 y^2+4=0 \end{aligned}$ This is a cubic equation. If we put $y=-\frac{1}{3}$ then $(3 y+1)=0$ is a factor of cubic equation.
$\begin{aligned} & (3 y+1)\left(9 y^2-12 y+4\right)=0 \\ & (3 y+1)(3 y-2)^2=0 \end{aligned}$ Hence $y=-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{3}$ Thus $f(x)=1$ has two solutions.

questions.solution:
$f(x) \rightarrow$ greatest integer function
$f(x)=[x]g(x) \rightarrow$ modulus function
$g(x)=|x|\begin{aligned}
& g \circ f(x)=g(f(x)) \quad f o g(x)=f(g(x)) \\

& =|-2| \quad ; \quad=\left[\frac{5}{3}\right] \\
& =2 \quad ; \quad=1 \\
& \operatorname{gof}\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)-f o g\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)=2-1=1
\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}

& 2 y-y=x \\
& \text { [for } y \geq 0 \text { ] } \\
& y=x \\
& 2 y+y=x \quad for[y \geq 0]\\
& 3 y=x \\
& y=\frac{1}{3} x \\
& y=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
x & y \geq 0 \\
\frac{1}{3} x & y \lt 0
\end{array} \text { function is defined for all value of } \mathrm{x} .\right. \\
& \text { or } \mathrm{y}=\left\{\begin{array}{lll}
x ; & x \geq 0 \\
\frac{1}{3} x & ; & x \lt 0

$y$ as a function of $x$ is continuous at $x=0$, but not differentiable at $x=0$.
