questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
The top ($M$) of a tower is observed from three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lying in a horizontal straight line which passes directly along the foot ($N$) of the tower. The angles of elevations of $M$ from $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are $30°$, $45°$ and $60°$ respectively. Let $PQ = a$ and $QR = b$.

What is $PN$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $h$ be the height of the tower $MN$.

In $\triangle MNP$, $\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{PN} \Rightarrow PN = h\sqrt{3}$

In $\triangle MNQ$, $\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{h}{QN} \Rightarrow QN = h$

In $\triangle MNR$, $\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{RN} \Rightarrow RN = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$

Since the angles of elevation increase as we move closer to the tower, the points $P, Q, R$ lie on the same side of $N$ in the order $P, Q, R, N$.

Given $PQ = a$, we have $PN - QN = a$.

$h\sqrt{3} - h = a \Rightarrow h(\sqrt{3} - 1) = a$

$h = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$

Rationalizing the denominator, we get:

$h = \dfrac{a(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{(\sqrt{3} - 1)(\sqrt{3} + 1)} = \dfrac{a(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2}$

We need to find $PN$, which is $h\sqrt{3}$:

$PN = \dfrac{a(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} \times \sqrt{3} = \left(\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{2}\right)a$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: There are two points $P$ and $Q$ due south of a leaning tower, which leans towards north. $P$ is at a distance $x$ and $Q$ is at a distance $y$ from the foot of the tower $(x \gt y)$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$ respectively.
Question: What is the length of the tower?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Length of the tower, } A B=\sqrt{h^2+z^2} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{(x-y)^2}{12}+\left(\frac{2 \sqrt{3}(x-y)-3(x+y)}{6}\right)^2} \\ & =\frac{(x-y)}{2 \sqrt{3}} \sqrt{1+\left(2-\frac{\sqrt{3}(x+y)}{x-y}\right)^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A man at $M$, standing 100 m away from the base ($P$) of a chimney of height 50 m, observes the angle of elevation of the highest point ($Q$) of the smoke to be $45°$. The highest point of the chimney is at $R$. Further $P$, $R$ and $Q$ are in a straight line and the straight line is perpendicular to $PM$. What is the angle $RMQ$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $PM$ be the distance of the man from the base of the chimney, so $PM = 100$ m.

Let $PR$ be the height of the chimney, so $PR = 50$ m.

Let $Q$ be the highest point of the smoke. The angle of elevation of $Q$ from $M$ is $\angle PMQ = 45^\circ$.

In $\triangle PMQ$, $\tan(\angle PMQ) = \dfrac{PQ}{PM}$

$\tan(45^\circ) = \dfrac{PQ}{100} \Rightarrow PQ = 100$ m.

In $\triangle PMR$, $\tan(\angle PMR) = \dfrac{PR}{PM} = \dfrac{50}{100} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The required angle is $\angle RMQ = \angle PMQ - \angle PMR = 45^\circ - \angle PMR$.

Taking tangent on both sides:

$\tan(\angle RMQ) = \tan(45^\circ - \angle PMR) = \dfrac{\tan(45^\circ) - \tan(\angle PMR)}{1 + \tan(45^\circ)\tan(\angle PMR)}$

$\tan(\angle RMQ) = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$\angle RMQ = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

Answer: $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: There are two points $P$ and $Q$ due south of a leaning tower, which leans towards north. $P$ is at a distance $x$ and $Q$ is at a distance $y$ from the foot of the tower $(x \gt y)$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$ respectively.
Question: If $\theta$ is the inclination of the tower to the horizontal, then what is $\cot \theta$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad z=\frac{h}{\tan 75^{\circ}}-y=\frac{x-y}{2 \sqrt{3}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}-y \\ & =\frac{(x-y)}{2}\left[\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{3+\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{3-\sqrt{3}}\right]-y \\ & =\frac{x-y}{2}\left[\frac{3 \sqrt{3}-3-3+\sqrt{3}}{9-3}\right]-y \\ & =(x-y) \frac{[2 \sqrt{3}-3]}{6}-y=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}(x-y)-3(x+y)}{6} \\ & \cot \theta=\frac{z}{h}=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}(x-y)-3(x+y)}{6} \times \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{x-y} \\ & =2-\frac{\sqrt{3}(x+y)}{x-y}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A vertical tower stands on a horizontal plane and is surmounted by a vertical flagstaff of height $h$. At a point on the plane the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of the flagstaff are $\theta$ and $2 \theta$ respectively. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution: In $\triangle \mathrm{PBC}\tan \theta=\frac{B C}{P C}\Rightarrow \quad P C=B C \cot \theta...(i)$ In $\triangle P A C\begin{aligned} & \tan 2 \theta=\frac{h+B C}{P C} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & P C \tan 2 \theta=h+B C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad B C \cdot \cot \theta \cdot \frac{2 \tan \theta}{1-\tan ^2 \theta}=h+B C \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{2 B C}{1-\tan ^2 \theta}-B C=h \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{1-\tan ^2 \theta} B C=h \\ & \Rightarrow \quad B C=\frac{1-\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta} h=\cos 2 \theta \cdot h\end{aligned}$

The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$ respectively.
Question: At what height is the top of the tower above the ground level?
questions.solution: In $\triangle A C Q \tan 75^{\circ}=\frac{h}{z+y}\Rightarrow z=\frac{h}{\tan 75^{\circ}}-y$ ...(i) In $\triangle A C P \tan 15^{\circ}=\frac{h}{z+x}\Rightarrow z=\frac{h}{\tan 15^{\circ}}-x$ ...(ii) From (i) and (ii) $\begin{aligned} & \frac{h}{\tan 15^{\circ}}-\frac{h}{\tan 75^{\circ}}=x-y \\ & \Rightarrow h\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3-1}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}\right)=x-y \\ & {\left[\because\left[\begin{array}{l} \because \tan 75^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1} \\ \tan 75^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1} \end{array}\right]\right.} \\ & \Rightarrow h\left(\frac{3+1+2 \sqrt{3}-3-1+2 \sqrt{3}}{3-1}\right)=x-y \\ & \Rightarrow h(2 \sqrt{3})=x-y \Rightarrow h=\frac{x-y}{2 \sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A ladder 6 m long reaches a point 6 m below the top of a vertical flagstaff. From the foot of the ladder, the elevation of the top of the flagstaff is $75^{\circ}$. What is the height of the flagstaff?
questions.solution:
Let $A C$ is a flagstaff of length $h \mathrm{~m}$ and $B D$ is a ladder of length 6 m . Point $B$ is below the top of the flagstaff, such that $A B=6 \mathrm{~m}$. Then, $\angle A D C=75^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned} & \text { From } \triangle A C D, \angle C A D+\angle A D C+\angle A C D=180^{\circ} \\ & \therefore \angle C A D+75^{\circ}+90^{\circ}=180^{\circ} \\ & \therefore \angle C A D=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-75^{\circ}=15^{\circ}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { As, } A B=B D \text {. } \\ & \therefore \angle C A D=\angle B D A=15^{\circ} \text { and } \\ & \angle B D C=75^{\circ}-15^{\circ}=60^{\circ} \text {. }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { From } \triangle B C D, \sin \left(60^{\circ}\right)=\frac{B C}{B D}=\frac{B C}{6} \\ & \therefore B C=6 \cdot \sin \left(60^{\circ}\right)=6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=3 \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$ Hence, height of flagstaff $=(6+3 \sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A plane is observed to be approaching the airport. It is at a distance of $10$ km from the point of observation and makes an angle of elevation of $67\cdot5^\circ$. What is the height of the plane above the ground ?
questions.solution:
Let $h$ be the height of the plane above the ground.

The distance from the point of observation to the plane is $d = 10$ km.

The angle of elevation is $\theta = 67.5^\circ$.

From the right-angled triangle formed, $\sin \theta = \dfrac{h}{d}$.

$h = 10 \sin 67.5^\circ$

Using the half-angle formula, $\sin \theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}}$.

$\sin 67.5^\circ = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 135^\circ}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2}}}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator inside the square root by $\sqrt{2}$:

$\sin 67.5^\circ = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{2}}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2}$

Substituting this value into the equation for $h$:

$h = 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2} = 5\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}$ km

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: A flagstaff 20 m long standing on a pillar 10 m high subtends an angle $\tan ^{-1}(0.5)$ at a point $P$ on the ground. Let $\theta$ be the angle subtended by the pillar at this point $P$.
Question: What is a possible value of $\tan \theta$ ?
questions.solution: $\tan \theta=\frac{10}{x} \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{10}{10}$ or $\frac{10}{30}\tan \theta=1$ or $\frac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The shadow of a tower is found to be $x$ metre longer, when the angle of elevation of the sun changes from $60^{\circ}$ to $45^{\circ}$. If the height of the tower is $5(3+\sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}$, then what is $x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Shadow length when elevation of Sun is $60^{\circ}=B C$
From $\triangle A B C$, $B C=A B \cdot \cot \left(60^{\circ}\right)=5(3+\sqrt{3}) \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=5(\sqrt{3}+1) \mathrm{m}$ Shadow length when elevation of Sun is $45^{\circ}=B D$ From $\triangle A B D$, $B D=A B \cdot \cot 45^{\circ}=5(3+\sqrt{3}) \cdot 1=5(3+\sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}\therefore x=B D-B C=5(3+\sqrt{3})-5(\sqrt{3}+1)=10 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle of elevation of a tower of height $h$ from a point A due South of it is x and from a point B due East of A is y . If $\mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{z}$, then which one of the following is correct ?
questions.solution: from figure (iii), $\mathrm{h}^2 \cot ^2 y=\mathrm{z}^2+\mathrm{h}^2 \cot ^2 \mathrm{x}\Rightarrow \mathrm{z}^2=\mathrm{h}^2\left(\cot ^2 \mathrm{y}-\cot ^2 \mathrm{x}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A ladder 9 m long reaches a point 9 m below the top of a vertical flagstaff. From the foot of the ladder, the elevation of the flagstaff is $60^{\circ}$. What is the height of the flagstaff?
questions.solution: $\triangle P A B$ is isosceles $\triangle\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \theta=30^{\circ} \\ & \text { In } \triangle A B D \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \tan 30^{\circ}=\frac{h}{x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \Rightarrow x=h \sqrt{3} \end{aligned}\text { In } \triangle P B O \text {, }\begin{aligned} & \tan 60^{\circ}=\sqrt{3}=\frac{9+h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{3}=\frac{9+h}{h \sqrt{3}} \\ & \Rightarrow 3 h=q+h \\ & \Rightarrow h=\frac{9}{2} m \end{aligned}\therefore$ Total height $=13.5 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A balloon is directly above one end of a bridge. The angle of depression of the other end of the bridge from the balloon is $48^{\circ}$. If the height of the balloon above the bridge is 122 m , then what is the length of the bridge?
questions.solution:
Let the bridge is BC and height above the bridge $\mathrm{AB}=122 \mathrm{~m}$.
From $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$, $\begin{aligned} & \cot 48^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{BC}}{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{\mathrm{BC}}{122} \\ & \mathrm{BC}=122 \cdot \cot \left(48^{\circ}\right) \\ &= 122 \cdot \cot \left(90^{\circ}-42^{\circ}\right) \\ &= 122 \cdot \tan 42^{\circ} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The top of a hill observed from the top and bottom of a building of height h is at angles of elevation $\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{\pi}{3}$ respectively. What is the height of the hill?
questions.solution: From question, In $\triangle \mathrm{PQR}$ and $\triangle \mathrm{PST}$. $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}=\frac{\mathrm{H}}{\tan \frac{\pi}{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{H}-h}{\tan \frac{\pi}{6}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \frac{\mathrm{H}}{3}=\mathrm{H}-h \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{H}=h \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{H}=\frac{3}{2} h \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from the top and foot of a pole are respectively $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. If $\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the height of the tower and $h_p$ is the height of the pole, then which of the following are correct?
1. $\frac{2 \mathrm{~h}_{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}}{3+\sqrt{3}}=\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}^2$
2. $\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}}{2}$
3. $\frac{2\left(\mathrm{~h}_{\mathrm{P}}+\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{P}}}=4+\sqrt{3}$
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Let the distance between tower and pole be ' $x$ '.
$\begin{aligned} & \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{x}}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~h}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{x} .\end{aligned}$ Now, $\tan 30^{\circ}=\frac{h_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{x}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}-1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\left(\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}\right)}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{2}$\ldots(1) So, statement ' 2 ' is correct. Now, $\frac{h_t-h_p}{h_p}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{h_t-h_p+2 h_p}{h_p}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1+4}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{5+\sqrt{3}}{2}$\ldots(2) So, statement ‘3’ is incorrect.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a flag-staff of 6 m height placed on the top of a tower throws a shadow of $2 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}$ along the ground, then what is the angle that the sun makes with the ground?
questions.solution: $A B$ is the tower. $B C$ is flag staff. The angles made by the shadows of tower and flag staff are same. $\begin{aligned} & \text { In } \triangle A B E, \tan \theta=\frac{h}{x}...(1) \\ & \text { In } \triangle A C D, \tan \theta=\frac{h+6}{x+2 \sqrt{3}}...(2)\\ & \text { from (1), (2), } \frac{h}{x}=\frac{h+6}{x+2 \sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow h x+2 \sqrt{3} h=h x+6 x \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{h}{x}=\frac{6}{2 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3} \end{aligned}$ from(1), $\tan \theta=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{x}}=\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta=60^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A spherical balloon of radius $r$ subtends an angle $\alpha$ at the eye of an observer, while the angle of elevation of its centre is $\beta$. What is the height of the centre of the balloon (neglecting the height of the observer)?
questions.solution:
Let ' $A$ ' be the position of eye. Let ' $O$ ' be the centre of spherical balloon. Let ' $h$ ' be the height of centre of balloon.
From figure, in $\triangle \mathrm{OAD}, \sin \frac{\alpha}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{OD}}{\mathrm{OA}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{OA}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{OA}=\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\sin \frac{\alpha}{2}}...(1) \\ & \text { In } \triangle \mathrm{OAB}, \sin \beta=\frac{\mathrm{OB}}{\mathrm{OA}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{OA}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~h}=\mathrm{OA} \cdot \sin \beta \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{r} \cdot \sin \beta}{\sin \frac{\alpha}{2}}...from (1) \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the top of a lighthouse, 100 m high, the angle of depression of a boat is $\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)$. What is the distance between the boat and the lighthouse?
questions.solution:
Given, angle of depression, $\theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{5}{12} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{100}{x}=\frac{5}{12} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{100 \times 12}{5}=240 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A moving boat is observed from the top of a cliff of 150 m height. The angle of depression of the boat changes from $60^{\circ}$ to $45^{\circ}$ in 2 minutes. What is the speed of the boat in metres per hour?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan 60^{\circ}=\frac{150}{x} \Rightarrow x=\frac{150}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \text {Also, } \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{150}{x+y} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x+y=150 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=150-x=150-\frac{150}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=150\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\text { distance travelled } \\ & \quad \text { Speed }(\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{hr})=\frac{150(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{60}{2}=4500 \frac{(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two poles are 10 m and 20 m high. The line joining their tops makes an angle of $15^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The distance between the poles is approximately equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \tan 15^{\circ}=\mathrm{DE} / \mathrm{AE} \\ & \mathrm{AE}=10 \cot 15^{\circ} ....(1)\\ & \cot \left(15^{\circ}\right)=\cot \left(45-30^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\frac{\cot 45^{\circ} \cot 30^{\circ}+1}{\cot 30^{\circ}-\cot 45^{\circ}} \end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \cot 15^{\circ}=\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}=2+\sqrt{3} \\ & \text { Putting } \cot 15^{\circ} \text { in eq (1) } \\ & \mathrm{AE}=10 \cot 15^{\circ} \\ & =10(2+\sqrt{3}) \\ & =10(3.73)=37.3 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A lamp post stands on a horizontal plane. From a point situated at a distance 150 m from its foot, the angle of elevation of the top is $30^{\circ}$. What is the height of the lamp post?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \tan 30^{\circ} & =\frac{h}{150} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & =\frac{h}{150}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad h=\frac{150}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}=50 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}\therefore$ Height of the lamp post $=50 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower standing on a horizontal plane from two points on a line passing through the foot of the tower at distances 49 m and 36 m are $43^{\circ}$ and $47^{\circ}$ respectively. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{h} \text { (height of the tower) } \\ & \mathrm{BD}=36 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \mathrm{BC}=49 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \angle \mathrm{D}=47^{\circ} \\ & \angle \mathrm{C}=43^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Now, in $\triangle A B D$, $\tan 47^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{36 \mathrm{~m}}...(i)$ and in $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$, $\begin{aligned} & \tan 43^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{49 \mathrm{~m}} \\ & \tan \left(90^{\circ}-47^{\circ}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{49} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad \cot 47^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{49}...(ii)$ Multiplying equations (i) and (ii) $\begin{aligned} & \tan 47^{\circ} \cdot \cot 47^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{36} \times \frac{\mathrm{h}}{49}=1=\frac{\mathrm{h}^2}{36 \times 49} \\ & \mathrm{~h}=6 \times 7=42 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (B) is correct

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 20 $m$ away from its base is $45^{\circ}$. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$, $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{h} \\ & \mathrm{BC}=20 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \angle \mathrm{C}=45^{\circ} \end{aligned}$
$\therefore \quad \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{\mathrm{BC}}1=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{20} \quad\left[\because \tan 45^{\circ}=1\right]\begin{array}{ll} & \mathrm{h}=20 \mathrm{~m} \\ \therefore & \text { Height of the tower }=20 \mathrm{~m} \\ \therefore \quad & \text { Option (B) is correct. }\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From an aeroplane above a straight road the angles of depression of two positions at a distance 20 m apart on the road are observed to be $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. The height of the aeroplane above the ground is:
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{ll}\text { In } \triangle \mathrm{ABD}, & \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{h}{x} \\ \Rightarrow & 1=\frac{h}{x} \Rightarrow h=x\end{array} In $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$, $\begin{array}{rlrl} & & \tan 30^{\circ} & =\frac{h}{x+20} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & =\frac{h}{x+20}=\frac{h}{h+20} \quad(\because x=h) \\ \Rightarrow & \quad \sqrt{3} h & =h+20=(\sqrt{3} h-h)=20 \\ \Rightarrow & h(\sqrt{3}-1) & =20 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & h & =\frac{20}{\sqrt{3}-1} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{20(\sqrt{3}+1)}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & h & =10(\sqrt{3}+1) \end{array} Hence, height of the aeroplane above the ground $=10(\sqrt{3}+1) \mathrm{m}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
The top ($M$) of a tower is observed from three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lying in a horizontal straight line which passes directly along the foot ($N$) of the tower. The angles of elevations of $M$ from $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are $30°$, $45°$ and $60°$ respectively. Let $PQ = a$ and $QR = b$.

What is $MN$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $MN = h$ be the height of the tower.

The distances of points $P$, $Q$, and $R$ from the foot of the tower $N$ are given by:

$PN = h \cot 30^{\circ} = h\sqrt{3}$

$QN = h \cot 45^{\circ} = h$

$RN = h \cot 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$

Given that $P$, $Q$, $R$ lie on a straight line passing through $N$, the distance $QR$ is:

$QR = QN - RN$

$b = h - \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$

$b = h\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$h = \dfrac{b\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-1}$

Rationalizing the denominator:

$h = \dfrac{b\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}{(\sqrt{3}-1)(\sqrt{3}+1)}$

$h = \dfrac{b(3+\sqrt{3})}{3-1}$

$h = \left(\dfrac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)b$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)b$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two places situated at distances 21 m and $x \mathrm{~m}$ from the base of the tower are $45^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ respectively. What is the value of $x$ ?
questions.solution: Let $A B$ is a tower, Given that $\mathrm{AC}=21 \mathrm{~m}$ and $\mathrm{AD}=x \mathrm{~m}$ From $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}, \tan \left(45^{\circ}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{\mathrm{AC}}1=\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{21}\therefore A B=21 \mathrm{~m}$ Again, from $\triangle \mathrm{ABD}$, $\begin{aligned} \tan \left(60^{\circ}\right) & =\frac{\mathrm{AB}}{\mathrm{AD}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{3}=\frac{21}{x} \\ x & =7 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation $2 x^2-3 y^2-6=0$ represents
questions.solution:
Given equation, $2 x^2-3 y^2-6=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2 x^2-3 y^2=6 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{3}-\frac{y^2}{2}=1\end{aligned}$
This equation represents hyperbola.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If any point on a hyperbola is $(3 \tan \theta, 2 \sec \theta)$, then what is the eccentricity of the hyperbola?
questions.solution:
Let equation of hyperbola is $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
then eccentricity $e=\sqrt{1+\frac{a^2}{b^2}}$
Now, as point $(3 \tan \theta, 2 \sec \theta)$ lies on hyperbola then, $\frac{3^2 \tan ^2 \theta}{a^2}-\frac{2^2 \sec ^2 \theta}{b^2}=1\frac{9 \tan ^2 \theta}{a^2}-\frac{4 \sec ^2 \theta}{b^2}=1$
This is true for $a^2=9$ and $b^2=4\therefore \text { eccentricity }(e)=\sqrt{1+\frac{9}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{13}}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the distance between the foci of the hyperbola $x^2 - 4y^2 = 1$?
questions.solution:
The given equation of the hyperbola is $x^2 - 4y^2 = 1$.

This can be rewritten in the standard form as $\dfrac{x^2}{1} - \dfrac{y^2}{1/4} = 1$.

Comparing with $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$, we get $a^2 = 1$ and $b^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

The eccentricity $e$ of the hyperbola is given by $e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{b^2}{a^2}}$.

$e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1/4}{1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$

The distance between the foci of the hyperbola is $2ae$.

$2ae = 2 \times 1 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2} = \sqrt{5}$

Answer: $\sqrt{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the equation of the hyperbola having latus rectum and eccentrieity 8 and $\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}$ respectively?
questions.solution:
Let the equation of hyperbola be $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
Latus rectum $=8=\frac{2 b^2}{a} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~b}^2=4 \mathrm{a}$  ...(i)
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Also, } \mathrm{b}^2=\mathrm{a}^2\left(\mathrm{e}^2-1\right) \\
\Rightarrow & 4 \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{a}^2\left(\mathrm{e}^2-1\right) \\
\Rightarrow & 4 \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{a}^2\left[\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\right)^2-1\right] \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{a}=5 \& \mathrm{~b}^2=20 \\
\therefore & \text { Equation is } \frac{x^2}{25}-\frac{y^2}{20}=1
\end{aligned}$
[From(i)]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The eccentricity of the hyperbola $16 x^2-9 y^2=1$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \because 16 x^2-9 y^2=1 \\
& \text { or } \frac{x^2}{\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2}-\frac{y^2}{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2}=1
\end{aligned}$
Comparing with $\frac{\mathrm{x}^2}{\mathrm{a}^2}-\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{\mathrm{~b}^2}=1\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \mathrm{a}^2=\frac{1}{16} \\
& \& \mathrm{~b}^2=\frac{1}{9} \\
& \because \mathrm{e}=\sqrt{1+\frac{\mathrm{b}^2}{\mathrm{a}^2}} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{e}=\sqrt{1+\frac{1 / 9}{1 / 16}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{e}=\frac{5}{3}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the distance between the two foci of the hyperbola $25x^2 - 75y^2 = 225$?
questions.solution:
The given equation of the hyperbola is $25x^2 - 75y^2 = 225$.

Dividing the entire equation by $225$, we get:

$\dfrac{x^2}{9} - \dfrac{y^2}{3} = 1$

Comparing this with the standard equation of a hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$, we have $a^2 = 9$ and $b^2 = 3$.

The relation between $a$, $b$, and the distance from the center to a focus $c$ is given by $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$.

Substituting the values, we get:

$c^2 = 9 + 3 = 12$

$c = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$

The distance between the two foci is $2c$.

Distance $= 2(2\sqrt{3}) = 4\sqrt{3}$ units.

Answer: $4\sqrt{3}$ units

questions.solution: The correct answer is option C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the locus of points, the difference of whose distances from two points being constant?
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ passes through the point $(3 \sqrt{5}, 1)$ and the length of its latus rectum is $\frac{4}{3}$ units. The length of the conjugate axis is
questions.solution:
$\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
Hyperbola passes through $(3 \sqrt{5}, 1)\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & \frac{(3 \sqrt{5})^2}{\mathrm{a}^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}^2}=1 \\
& \frac{45}{\mathrm{a}^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}^2}=1...(i)
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text { Now length of latus rectum }=\frac{2 b^2}{a} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{4}{3}=\frac{2 b^2}{\mathrm{a}} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{2}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{b}^2}{\mathrm{a}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\frac{3 \mathrm{~b}^2}{2}...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Putting the value of ‘a’ from equation (ii) in equation (i),
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{45 \times 4}{9 b^4}-\frac{1}{b^2}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{20}{b^4}-\frac{1}{b^2}=1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& 20-b^2=b^4 \\
& b^4+b^2-20=0 \\
& b^4+5 b^2-4 b^2-20=0 \\
& b^2\left(b^2+5\right)-4\left(b^2+5\right)=0 \\
& \left(b^2-4\right)\left(b^2+5\right)=0 \\
& b^2=4, b^2=-5 \\
& \therefore \quad b^2=4 \Rightarrow b=2
\end{aligned}$
Now length of conjugate axis
$=2 b=2(2)=4\therefore \quad$ Option (C) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of hyperbola
$\frac{x^2}{\cos ^2 \theta}-\frac{y^2}{\sin ^2 \theta}=1$
1. The two foci are independent of 0 .
2. The eccentricity is $\sec \theta$.
3. The distance between the two foci is 2 units.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Given the equation
$\frac{x^2}{\cos ^2 \theta}-\frac{y^2}{\sin ^2 \theta}=1$
Since $C^2=\cos ^2 \theta+\sin ^2 \theta=1$
So focus $=(0 \pm 1,0)=( \pm 1,0)e=\frac{c}{a}=\frac{1}{\cos \theta}=\sec \theta$
Distance between the two foci $=1+1=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The foci of the hyperbola $4 x^2-9 y^2-1=0$ are
questions.solution:
Standard equation of hyperbola
$\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
with foci $S(a e, 0)$ and $S^{\prime}(-a e, 0)$
Given equation is
$4 x^2-9 y^2=1$
or, $\quad \frac{x^2}{\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)}-\frac{y^2}{\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)}=1$
Here, $\quad a^2=\frac{1}{4}, \quad b^2=\frac{1}{9}$
From hyperbola properties, or,
$\begin{aligned}
b^2 & =a^2 e^2-a^2 \\
a^2 e^2 & =b^2+a^2 \\
& =\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{13}{36}
\end{aligned}\text { or, } \quad a e= \pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{6}$
Hence, foci : $\left( \pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{6}, 0\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the eccentricity of rectangular hyperbola?
questions.solution:
Here, $b^2=a^2\left(e^2-1\right)$
For rectangular hyperbola : $a=b\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow b^2=b^2\left(e^2-1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow e^2-1=1 \\
& \Rightarrow e^2=2 \Rightarrow e= \pm \sqrt{2}
\end{aligned}$
For hyperbola, $\mathrm{e} \gt 1$.
Hence, $\mathrm{e}=\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \dfrac{dx}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{dx}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$

$I = \int \dfrac{10^x}{10^{2x} + 1} dx$

Let $10^x = t$

$10^x \ln 10 \, dx = dt \Rightarrow 10^x \, dx = \dfrac{dt}{\ln 10}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10} \int \dfrac{dt}{t^2 + 1}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10} \tan^{-1}(t) + c$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10} \tan^{-1}(10^x) + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\ln 10}\tan^{-1}(10^x) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$, where $x \neq 2n\pi$ and $n$ is an integer.

What is $\int y \, dx$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$

$y = \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x}$

Using the half-angle formula $1 - \cos x = 2 \sin^2(x/2)$

$y = \dfrac{1}{2 \sin^2(x/2)} = \dfrac{1}{2} \csc^2(x/2)$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$\int y \, dx = \int \dfrac{1}{2} \csc^2(x/2) \, dx$

$\int y \, dx = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{-\cot(x/2)}{1/2} \right) + c$

$\int y \, dx = -\cot(x/2) + c$

Answer: $-\cot(x/2) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$
What is the value of $\beta$ ?
questions.solution:
Given,
$\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c\qquad ....(i)$
Let, $\quad \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}) d x}{(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1})(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1})} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{(x+1)} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{x-1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+\frac{\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii) we get
$\beta=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=\mathrm{U}(x) \mathrm{V}(x)-3 \ln \{\mathrm{U}(x)+\mathrm{V}(x)\}+c$
Question: What is $\mathrm{U}(x) \mathrm{V}(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=2 \int\left(\frac{x^2+1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2 \int\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-2 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c\right. \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}+\ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-4 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right) \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}-3 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c \\ & =U(x) \cdot V(x)-3 \ln \{U(x)+V(x)\}+c \\ & \therefore U(x)=x \text { and } V(x)=\sqrt{x^2+1}\end{aligned}\therefore \mathrm{U}(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{V}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x} \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+1}=\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^4+\mathrm{x}^2}=\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}^4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}=A\ln|2+\cos\theta|+B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$.

Question: What is the value of $A$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}$

Substitute $\cos\theta = t$, which gives $-\sin\theta\,d\theta = dt \Rightarrow \sin\theta\,d\theta = -dt$

$I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{-dt}{(2+t)(3+4t)}$

Using partial fractions:

$\dfrac{-1}{(t+2)(4t+3)} = \dfrac{P}{t+2} + \dfrac{Q}{4t+3}$

$-1 = P(4t+3) + Q(t+2)$

Substituting $t = -2$, we get $-1 = P(-8+3) \Rightarrow P = \dfrac{1}{5}$

Substituting $t = -\dfrac{3}{4}$, we get $-1 = Q\left(-\dfrac{3}{4}+2\right) \Rightarrow Q = -\dfrac{4}{5}$

Therefore, the integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int \left( \dfrac{1/5}{t+2} - \dfrac{4/5}{4t+3} \right) dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|t+2| - \dfrac{4}{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{4} \ln|4t+3| + C$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|t+2| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|4t+3| + C$

Substituting back $t = \cos\theta$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+\cos\theta| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|3+4\cos\theta| + C$

Comparing this with $A\ln|2+\cos\theta| + B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$, we get $A = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=\mathrm{U}(x) \mathrm{V}(x)-3 \ln \{\mathrm{U}(x)+\mathrm{V}(x)\}+c$
Question: What is $\left|\mathrm{U}^2(x)-\mathrm{V}^2(x)\right|$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=2 \int\left(\frac{x^2+1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2 \int\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-2 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c\right. \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}+\ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-4 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right) \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}-3 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c \\ & =U(x) \cdot V(x)-3 \ln \{U(x)+V(x)\}+c \\ & \therefore U(x)=x \text { and } V(x)=\sqrt{x^2+1}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Now, }\left|\mathrm{U}^2(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{V}^2(\mathrm{x})\right| \\ & =\left|\mathrm{x}^2-\left(\mathrm{x}^2+1\right)\right|=\left|\mathrm{x}^2-\mathrm{x}^2-1\right|=|-1|=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Given that $\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x=\frac{\alpha x}{29}+\frac{\beta}{29} \ln |2 \cos x+5 \sin x|+c$
What is the value of $\beta$ ?
questions.solution:
Let,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}\left[\frac{d}{d x}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)\right] \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)
\end{aligned}$
Comparing co-efficient of $\sin x$ and $\cos x\begin{aligned}
& 3=2 A+5 B \qquad ....(i)\\
& 4=5 A-2 B \qquad ....(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Solving (i) and (ii) then we get,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A}=\frac{26}{29}, \mathrm{~B}=\frac{7}{29} \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\int \frac{26}{29}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+\frac{7}{29}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\int \frac{26}{29} d x+\frac{7}{29} \int \frac{(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\frac{26}{29} x+\frac{7}{29} \text { In }(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+c \\
& \alpha=26, \beta=7[\text { [on comparing] }
\end{aligned}\beta=7$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$.

Consider the following:
I. $\dfrac{du}{dx} = -v$
II. $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -u$
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Given $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:
$\dfrac{du}{dx} = e^x \cos x$
$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = e^x \sin x$

Evaluating the integrals, we have:
$u = \dfrac{e^x}{2}(\cos x + \sin x) + C_1$
$v = \dfrac{e^x}{2}(\sin x - \cos x) + C_2$

Comparing the derivatives with $u$ and $v$, it is clear that:
$\dfrac{du}{dx} \neq -v$
$\dfrac{dv}{dx} \neq -u$

Therefore, neither statement I nor statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int\left(x^x\right)^2(1+\ln x) d x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$I=\int\left(x^x\right)^2\left(1+\int \ln x\right) d x$
Let $x^{\mathrm{x}}=t\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \ln t=x \ln x \Rightarrow d t=x^{\mathrm{x}}(1+\ln x) d x \\
& I=\int t d t=\frac{-}{2}+C=-(x)+C \\
& \frac{1}{2} x^{2 \mathrm{x}}+C
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $f(x)=P e^x+Q e^{2 x}+R e^{3 x}$, where $P, Q, R$ are real numbers. Further $f(0)=6, f^{\prime}(\ln 3)=282$ and $\int_0^{\ln 2} f(x) d x=11$
Question: What is the value of R ?
questions.solution: $\because Q=2\therefore \quad R=\frac{30-3 Q}{8}=\frac{30-6}{8}=3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $f(x)=P e^x+Q e^{2 x}+R e^{3 x}$, where $P, Q, R$ are real numbers. Further $f(0)=6, f^{\prime}(\ln 3)=282$ and $\int_0^{\ln 2} f(x) d x=11$
Question: What is the value of Q ?
questions.solution:
$f(x)=P e^x+Q e^{2 x}+R e^{J x}f(0)=P+Q+R=6$  ....(1)
$f^{\prime}(x)=P e^x+2 Q e^{2 x}+3 R e^{3 x}f^{\prime}(\ln 3)=P e^{\ln 3}+2 Q e^{2 \ln 3}+3 R e^{3 \ln 3}\Rightarrow \quad 3 P+18 Q+81 R=282\Rightarrow P+6 Q+27 R=94$  ....(2)
Since $\int f(x) d x=P e^x+\frac{Q}{2} e^{2 x}+\frac{R}{3} e^{3 x}\Rightarrow \int_0^{\ln } f(x) d x=11\left(P e^{\operatorname{In} 2}+\frac{Q}{2} e^2 \operatorname{In} 2+\frac{R}{3} e^3 \operatorname{In} 2-P-\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{R}{3}\right)=11\Rightarrow \quad 2 P+2 Q+\frac{8 R}{3}-P-\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{R}{3}=11\Rightarrow \quad P+\frac{3 Q}{2}+\frac{7 R}{3}=11$  ....(3)
(2) - (1) and (3) - (1),
$5 Q+26 R=88$  ....(4)
and, $\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{4 R}{3}=53 Q+8 R=30$  ....(5)
From (5), $R=\frac{30-3 Q}{8}$
From (4), $5 Q+26\left(\frac{30-3 Q}{8}\right)=88\Rightarrow 20 Q+390-39 Q=352\Rightarrow \quad 19 Q=38\Rightarrow \quad Q=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int e^{\mathrm{x}}(1+\ln x+x \ln x) d x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \frac{d(x \ln x)}{d x}=1+\ln x \\ & \therefore I=\int e^x\{1+\ln x+x \ln x\} d x \\ & =x \ln x e^{\mathrm{x}}+c\left[\because \int e^x\left(f(x)+f^{\prime}(x) d x=e^x f(x)+c\right)\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^2+1\right)}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^2+1\right)} \\ & =\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^2+1\right)} \\ & \text {Let } x^2+1=t \Rightarrow x^2=t-1 \\ & 2 x d s=d t \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d t}{t(t-1)} \\ & =\frac{-1}{2} \int\left[\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{(t-1)}\right] d t \\ & =\frac{-1}{2}\left[\int \frac{1}{t} d t-\int \frac{1}{(t-1)} d t\right] \\ & =\frac{-1}{2}[\log (t)-\log (t-1)]+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2}[\log (t-1)-\log t]+C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} \log \left(\frac{t-1}{t}\right)+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \log \left(\frac{x^2}{x^2+1}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the integral of $f(x)=1+x^2+x^4$ with respect to $x^2 ?$
questions.solution:
Let $x^2=t\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=1+x^2+x^4 \\
& \mathrm{I}=\int f(x) d x^2=\int\left(1+x^2+x^4\right) d x^2 \\
& =\int\left(1+t+t^2\right) d t=t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+c \\
& \mathrm{I}=x^2+\frac{x^4}{2}+\frac{x^6}{3}+C
\end{aligned}
$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{d x}{\sec x+\tan x}$ equal to ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{d x}{\sec x+\tan x}=\int \frac{(\sec x-\tan x) \cdot d x}{\left(\sec ^2 x-\tan ^2 x\right)} \\ & =\int \sec x \cdot d x-\int \tan x \cdot d x \\ & =l n|(\sec x+\tan x)|-(-\operatorname{nn}|\cos x|)+C \\ & =l n|\sec x+\tan x|-l \operatorname{n}|\cos x|^{-1}+C \\ & =l n|\sec x+\tan x|-l \operatorname{n}|\sec x|+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \sqrt{1-\sin 2 x} d x=A \sin x+B \cos x+C$, where $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4}$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\int \sqrt{1-\sin ^2 x} d x, 0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4} \\
& =\int \sqrt{\sin ^2 x-2 \sin x \cos x+\cos ^2 x} d x \\
& =\int \sqrt{(\sin x-\cos x)^2} d x
\end{aligned}$
(i.e. $\sin x-\cos x \lt 0$ when $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4}$ )
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \mathrm{I}=-\int(\sin x-\cos x) d x=\int(\cos x-\sin x) d x \\
& \mathrm{I}=\sin x-\cos x+c=\mathrm{A} \sin x+\mathrm{B} \cos x+\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$
Thus, $A+B=1-1=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{d x}{\sec ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} x\right)}$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$\int \frac{d x}{\sec ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} x\right)}$
Let $\tan ^{-1} x=y \Rightarrow \tan y=x$ and
$\begin{aligned} & \sec ^2 y=1+\tan ^2 y=1+x^2 \\ & \therefore \int \frac{d x}{\sec ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} x\right)}=\int \frac{d x}{1+x^2}=\tan ^{-1} x+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int e^{\left(2 \ln x+\ln x^2\right)} d x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int e^{\left(2 \ln x+\ln x^2\right)} \cdot d x \\ & =\int e^{\left(\ln x+\ln x^2\right)} \cdot d x=\int e^{\left(2 \cdot \ln x^2\right)} \cdot d x\end{aligned}=\int e^{\left(\ln x^4\right)} \cdot d x=\int x^4 \cdot d x=\frac{x^5}{5}+c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $p(x)=(4 e)^{2 x}$, then what is $\int p(x) d x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\int P(x) \cdot d x=\int(4 \cdot e)^{2 x} \cdot d x=\int e^{2 x(\ln e+\ln 4)} \cdot d x=\int e^{2 x(1+\ln 4)} \cdot d x=\frac{e^{2 x(1+\ln 4)}}{2(1+\ln 4)}+C \quad$ where $C=$ constant
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(4 e)^{2 x}}{2(1+2 \ln 2)}+C \\ & \therefore \int P(x) \cdot d x=\frac{P(x)}{2(1+2 \ln (2))}+C .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int\left(e^{\log x}+\sin x\right) \cos x d x$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} &  \int\left(e^{\log x}+\sin x\right) \cdot \cos x \cdot d x=\int(x+\sin x) \cdot \cos x \cdot d x \\ & =\int(x \cdot \cos x+\sin x \cdot \cos x) \cdot d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\int x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x+\int \sin x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x \\ & =x \cdot \int \cos x \cdot d x-\int\left(\frac{d x}{d x} \cdot \int(\cos x) \cdot d x\right) \cdot d x \\ & \quad+\int \sin x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =x \cdot \sin x-\int \sin x \cdot d x+\int \sin x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x \\ & =x \cdot \sin x-(-\cos x)+\int \sin x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x\end{aligned}=x \sin x+\cos x+\int \sin x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x$
Now, $\int \sin x \cdot \cos x \cdot d x$
Let $\sin x=z, d z=\cos x \cdot d x\int \sin x \cdot \cos x d x=\int z \cdot d z=\frac{z^2}{2}=\frac{\sin ^2 x}{2}\therefore I=x \cdot \sin x+\cos x+\frac{\sin ^2 x}{2}+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^n+1\right)}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^n+1\right)}=\int \frac{x^{n-1}}{x^n\left(x^n+1\right)} \cdot d x$
Let $z=x^n \Rightarrow d z=n x^{n-1} d x\therefore \int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^n+1\right)}=\int \frac{x^{n-1}}{x^n\left(x^n+1\right)} \cdot d x=\int \frac{1}{z(z+1)} \cdot \frac{d z}{n}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{n}\left[\int \frac{1}{z} \cdot d z-\int \frac{d z}{z+1}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{n}[\ln z-\ln (z+1)]+C \quad \text { where } C=\text { constant }\end{aligned}=\frac{1}{n} \cdot \ln \left(\frac{z}{z+1}\right)+C=\frac{1}{n} \ln \left(\frac{x^n}{x^n+1}\right)+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $k$ such that integration of $\frac{3 x^2+8-4 k}{x}$ with respect to $x$, may be a rational function?
questions.solution:
$I=\int\left(\frac{3 x^2+8-4 k}{x}\right) \cdot d x\begin{aligned}
& =\int 3 x d x+\int \frac{8-4 k}{x} \cdot d x \\
& =\frac{3}{2} x^2+(8-4 k) \cdot \ln (x)+C
\end{aligned}$
where $C=$ constant
To get integration as rational function,
$(8-4 k) \cdot \ln (x)=0 \Rightarrow 8-4 k=0 \Rightarrow k=\frac{8}{4}=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$.

What is $u + v$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$

Adding $u$ and $v$:

$u + v = \int e^x (\cos x + \sin x)\, dx$

Using the standard integral $\int e^x (f(x) + f'(x))\, dx = e^x f(x)$, where $f(x) = \sin x$ and $f'(x) = \cos x$:

$u + v = e^x \sin x$

From the given expression for $v$, differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \int e^x \sin x\, dx \right) = e^x \sin x$

Therefore, $u + v = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

Answer: $\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}=A\ln|2+\cos\theta|+B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$.

Question: What is the value of $B$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}$.

Substitute $t = \cos\theta$, which gives $dt = -\sin\theta\,d\theta$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{-dt}{(2+t)(3+4t)}$

Using partial fractions, we can write:

$\dfrac{-1}{(2+t)(3+4t)} = \dfrac{A'}{2+t} + \dfrac{B'}{3+4t}$

$-1 = A'(3+4t) + B'(2+t)$

Putting $t = -2$, we get $-1 = A'(3 - 8) \Rightarrow A' = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Putting $t = -\dfrac{3}{4}$, we get $-1 = B'\left(2 - \dfrac{3}{4}\right) \Rightarrow -1 = B'\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right) \Rightarrow B' = -\dfrac{4}{5}$.

So, the integral is:

$I = \displaystyle\int \left( \dfrac{1/5}{2+t} - \dfrac{4/5}{3+4t} \right) dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+t| - \dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{4}\ln|3+4t| + C$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+t| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|3+4t| + C$

Substituting back $t = \cos\theta$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+\cos\theta| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|3+4\cos\theta| + C$

Comparing this with the given expression $A\ln|2+\cos\theta| + B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$, we get:

$B = -\dfrac{1}{5}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{1}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Given that $\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x=\frac{\alpha x}{29}+\frac{\beta}{29} \ln |2 \cos x+5 \sin x|+c$
What is the value of $\alpha$ ?
questions.solution:
Let,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}\left[\frac{d}{d x}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)\right] \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)
\end{aligned}$
Comparing co-efficient of $\sin x$ and $\cos x\begin{aligned}
& 3=2 A+5 B \qquad ....(i)\\
& 4=5 A-2 B \qquad ....(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Solving (i) and (ii) then we get,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A}=\frac{26}{29}, \mathrm{~B}=\frac{7}{29} \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\int \frac{26}{29}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+\frac{7}{29}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\int \frac{26}{29} d x+\frac{7}{29} \int \frac{(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\frac{26}{29} x+\frac{7}{29} \text { In }(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+c \\
& \alpha=26, \beta=7[\text { [on comparing] }
\end{aligned}\alpha=26$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{d x}{x(1+\ln x)^n}$ equal to $\left(n^1 1\right)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{d x}{x(1+\ell \mathrm{n} x)^n} \\ & \text {Let } 1+\ell \mathrm{n} x=t \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} d x=d t \\ & \Rightarrow \int \frac{d t}{t^n}=\frac{t^{-n}+1}{-n+1}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(1+\ell n x)^{-n+1}}{1-n} \\ & =\frac{1}{(n-1)(1+\ell \mathrm{n} x)^{n-1}}+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{d x}{2 x^2-2 x+1}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  \int \frac{d x}{2 x^2-2 x+1}=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d x}{x^2-x+\frac{1}{2}} \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d x}{\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2} \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x-\frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right]+C \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2: \tan ^{-1}(2 x-1)+C \\
& =\tan ^{-1}(2 x-1)+C
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$
What is the value of $\alpha$ ?
questions.solution:
Given,
$\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c\qquad ....(i)$
Let, $\quad \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}) d x}{(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1})(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1})} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{(x+1)} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{x-1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+\frac{\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii) we get
$\alpha=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.solution: $\int \ln (x) \cdot d x \quad 2 \cdot \int \ln x \cdot d x\begin{aligned} & =2 \int 1 \cdot \ln x \cdot d x \\ & =2\left[\ln x \cdot x-\int \frac{1}{x} \cdot x \cdot d x\right. \\ & =2(x \cdot \ln x-x)+c \\ & =2 x \ln x-2 x+c\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}\left(\mathrm{x}^7+1\right)}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}\left(\mathrm{x}^7+1\right)}=\int \frac{\mathrm{x}^6}{\mathrm{x}^7\left(\mathrm{x}^7+1\right)} \cdot \mathrm{dx}$
Let $\mathrm{x}^7=\mathrm{t}\Rightarrow 7 x^6 . d x=\mathrm{dt} \Rightarrow x^6 d x=\frac{d t}{7}$
Then $\int \frac{x^6 d x}{x^7\left(x^7+1\right)}=\frac{1}{7} \int \frac{d t}{t(t+1)}\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1}{7}\left[\int \frac{1}{t} \mathrm{dt}-\int \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}+1} \mathrm{dt}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{7}[\ln |\mathrm{t}|-\ln |\mathrm{t}+1|]+\mathrm{c} \\
& =\frac{1}{7} \ln \left|\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{t}+1}\right|+\mathrm{c} \\
& =\frac{1}{7} \ln \left|\frac{\mathrm{x}^7}{\mathrm{x}^7+1}\right|+\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{\left(\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}-1}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}-1}\right) \mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{\left(\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}-1}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}-1}\right) \mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}} \\ & \text {Put } \mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \mathrm{ex} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{e}-1}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}=\frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{dx}} \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\mathrm{ex} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{e}-1}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}\right) \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dt} \\ & \therefore \int \frac{\left(\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}-1}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}-1}\right) \mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}} \int \frac{\mathrm{e} \cdot \mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}-1}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}} \cdot \mathrm{dx} \\ & =\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}} \int \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}} \cdot \ln \mathrm{t}+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}} \cdot \ln \left(\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{e}}+\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}\right)+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $f(\mathrm{x})$ be an indefinite integral of $\sin ^2 \mathrm{x}$. Consider the following statements :
Statement 1 : The function $f(\mathrm{x})$ satisfies $f(\mathrm{x}+\pi)=f(\mathrm{x})$ for all real x .
Statement $2: \sin ^2(x+\pi)=\sin ^2 x$ for all real $x$.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both the statements are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1
Both the statements are true but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1
Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false
Statement 1 is false but Statement 2 is false
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\int \sin ^2 x \cdot d x=\int \frac{1-\cos 2 x}{2} \cdot d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{\sin 2 x}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}+c=\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{1}{4} \sin 2 x+c\end{aligned}$
(i)
$\begin{aligned}
& f(\pi+x)=\frac{1}{2}(\pi+x)-\frac{1}{4} \sin 2(\pi+x) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \pi+\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{1}{2} \sin (2 \pi+2 x)+c \\
& =\frac{x}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \sin 2 x+c=f(x)
\end{aligned}$
So, statement 1 is true.
(ii)
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin ^2(\pi+x)=\sin ^2 x \\
& (-\sin x)^2=\sin ^2 x \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^2 x=\sin ^2 x
\end{aligned}$
So, statement 2 is true

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}} d x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Take option (1)
$I_1=\sqrt{\frac{x^4+x^3+1}{x}}+C\begin{aligned}
\frac{d I_1}{d x} & =\frac{d}{d x}\left[\left(x^3+x^2+x^{-1}\right)^{1 / 2}+C\right] \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(x^3+x^2+x^{-1}\right)^{-1 / 2}\left(3 x^2+2 x-x^{-2}\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3 x^2+2 x-\frac{1}{x^2}}{\sqrt{x^3+x^2+\frac{1}{x}}}\right] \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3 x^4+2 x^3-1}{\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{x}} \sqrt{x^4+x^3+1}}\right]
\end{aligned}$
Take option (b) :
$\begin{aligned}
I_2 & =\sqrt{x^4+2-\frac{1}{x^2}}+C \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[x^4+2-x^{-2}\right]^{-1 / 2}\left[4 x^3+0+2 x^{-3}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{4 x^3+\frac{2}{x^3}}{\sqrt{x^4+2-\frac{1}{x^2}}}\right]=\frac{2 x^6+1}{\frac{x^3}{x} \sqrt{x^6+2 x^2-1}} \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{2 x^6+1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^6+2 x-1}}
\end{aligned}$
Take option (3) :
$\begin{aligned}
& I_3=\sqrt{x^2+x^{-2}+1}+C \\
& \frac{d I_3}{d x}=\frac{1}{2}\left[x^2+x^{-2}+1\right]^{-1 / 2}\left[2 x-2 x^{-3}+0\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{2 x-\frac{2}{x^3}}{\sqrt{x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}+1}}\right]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{2\left(x^4-1\right)}{x^3 \sqrt{\frac{x^4+1+x^2}{x^2}}}\right] \\
& \frac{d I_3}{d x}=\frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (3) is correct answer.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $I_1=\int \frac{e^x d x}{e^x+e^{-x}}$ and $I_2=\int \frac{d x}{e^{2 x}+1}$, then what is $I_1+I_2$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I_1=\int \frac{e^x}{e^x+e^{-x}} d x=\int \frac{e^x}{e^x+\frac{1}{e^x}} d x \\ & =\int \frac{e^{2 x}}{e^{2 x+1}} d x \\ & \therefore I_1+I_2=\int \frac{e^{2 x}+1}{e^{2 x}+1} d x=\int 1 d x \\ & =x+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{(\cos x)^{1.5}-(\sin x)^{1.5}}{\sqrt{\sin x \cdot \cos x}} d x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int \frac{\cos ^{3 / 2} x-\sin ^{3 / 2} x}{\sin ^{1 / 2} x \cdot \cos ^{1 / 2} x} d x \\ & \int\left(\sin ^{-1 / 2} x \cdot \cos x-\cos ^{-1 / 2} x \cdot \sin x\right) d x \\ & =2 \cdot \sin ^{1 / 2} x+2 \cdot \cos ^{1 / 2} x+C=2 \sqrt{\sin x}+2 \sqrt{\cos x}+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int e^{\sin x} \frac{x \cos ^3 x-\sin x}{\cos ^2 x} d x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let us differentiate all the options one by one to get the expression in the question whose integral is to be found.
Here $x e^{\sin x}$ is the common term in all the options. So, let us differentiate it first.
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Let } l=x e^{\sin x} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d l}{d x}=e^{\sin x}[x \cos x+1] \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d l}{d x}=\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x\right]
\end{aligned}$
Let $m=\sec x e^{\sin x}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{d m}{d x}=\sec x e^{\sin x} \cdot \cos x+e^{\sin x} \sec x \tan x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d m}{d x}=e^{\sin x}\left[1+\frac{\sin x}{\cos ^2 x}\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d m}{d x}=\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[\cos ^2 x+\sin x\right]
\end{aligned}$
Differentiation of option (a) is
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x+\cos ^2 x+\sin x\right] \\
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+2 \cos ^2 x+\sin x\right]
\end{aligned}$
Differentiation of option (b) is
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x-\cos ^2 x-\sin x\right] \\
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x-\sin x\right]
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (2) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=(\mathrm{x}-1)^2(\mathrm{x}+1)(\mathrm{x}-2)^3$.
Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be twice differentiable functions on $[0,2]$ satisfying $\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x}), \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)=4, \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}(1)=6, f(2)=3$ and $g(2)=9$. Then what is $f(x)-g(x)$ at $x=4$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$f^{\prime \prime}(x)=g^{\prime \prime}(x)$
integrate b|s w.r.t. (x)
$f^{\prime}(x)+C_1=g^{\prime}(x)+C_2$  ...(1)
Putting $x=1\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(1)+C_1=g^{\prime}(1)+C_2 \\
& \Rightarrow C_1-C_2=g^{\prime}(1)-f^{\prime}(1) \\
& \Rightarrow C_1-C_2=6-4=2
\end{aligned}$
again integrating equation (1)
$f(x)+C_1 x+a_1=g(x)+C_2 x+a_2$  ...(3)
Putting $x=2\begin{aligned}
& f(2)+C_1 \times 2+a_1=g(2)+2 C_2+a_2 \\
& \Rightarrow a_1-a_2=g(2)+2 C_2-2 C_1-f(2) \\
& \quad=9-3-2\left(C_1-C_2\right) \\
& \quad=6-2 \times 2=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}_1-\mathrm{a}_2=2
\end{aligned}$
Rearranging equation (3) again, we get
$f(x)-g(x)=-x\left(C_1-C_2\right)-\left(a_1-a_2\right)$
Putting $x=4$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
{[f(x)-g(x)]_{x=4} } & =-4\left(C_1-C_2\right)-\left(a_1-a_2\right) \\
& =-4 \times(2)-2 \\
{[f(x)-g(x)]_{x=4} } & =-10
\end{aligned}$

$\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{1+\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{x}}}$ is equal to
where $c$ is the constant of integration
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{1+\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{x}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \int \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1} \mathrm{dx} \\ & \text {Let } \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1=\mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dt} \\ & =\int \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{t}} \\ & \Rightarrow \log \mathrm{t}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \log \left(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1\right)+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The integral $\int \frac{d x}{a \cos x+b \sin x}$ is of the form $\frac{1}{r} \operatorname{In}\left[\tan \left(\frac{x+\alpha}{2}\right)\right]$.
What is $r$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given that, $\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{a} \cos \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{b} \sin \mathrm{x}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}} \ln \left[\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\alpha}{2}\right)\right]$
Let $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{r} \sin \alpha, \mathrm{b}=\mathrm{r} \cos \alpha\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{d x}{r \sin \alpha \cos x+r \cos \alpha \sin x}=\frac{1}{r} \int \frac{1}{\sin (x+\alpha)} \\
& =\frac{1}{r} \int \operatorname{cosec}(x+\alpha) d x=\frac{1}{r} \ln \left[\tan \left(\frac{x+\alpha}{2}\right)\right]
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& a=r \sin \alpha \Rightarrow a^2=r^2 \sin ^2 \alpha ...(i)\\
& b=r \cos \alpha \Rightarrow b^2=r^2 \cos ^2 \alpha...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Adding (i) and (ii), we get
$\Rightarrow \quad \begin{aligned}
\mathrm{r}^2 & =\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{r} & =\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x^2+a^2}}$ equal to?
where $c$ is the constant of integration.
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x^2+a^2}} \\ & \text {Let } x=a \tan u \\ & \quad d x=a \sec ^2 u d u \\ & =\int \frac{a \sec ^2 u d u}{\sqrt{a^2 \tan ^2 u+a^2}} \\ & =a \int \frac{\sec ^2 u d u}{\sqrt{a^2\left(1+\tan ^2 u\right)}} \Rightarrow \frac{a}{a} \int \frac{\sec ^2 u d u}{\sec u}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{\sec ^2 u d u}{\sec u}=\int \sec u d u \\ & =\ln [\tan (u)+\sec (u)]+c \quad\left[\because \int \sec x d x=\tan x\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =\ln \left[\frac{x}{\sqrt{a^2}}+\sqrt{1+\frac{x^2}{a^2}}\right]+c \\
& =\ln \left[\frac{x}{a}+\frac{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}{a}\right]+c \\
& =\ln \left[\frac{x+\sqrt{x^2+a^2}}{a}\right]+c
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (A) is correct.

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& a=r \sin \alpha \\
& b=r \cos \alpha

Dividing (i) from (ii),
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{~b}}=\tan \alpha \\
& \alpha=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{~b}}\right) .

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider $\int x \tan ^{-1} x d x=\mathrm{A}\left(x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} x+\mathrm{C}$, where C is the constant of integration.
What is the value of A ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \int x \cdot \tan ^{-1} x d x=\mathrm{A}\left(x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} x+\mathrm{C} \\ & \text {Let } \mathrm{I}=\int x \cdot \tan ^{-1} x d x \\ &=\tan ^{-1} x \cdot\left(\frac{x^2}{2}\right)-\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{x^2}{1+x^2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\left(1+x^2\right)-1}{1+x^2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2}\left[\int 1 d x-\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} d x\right] \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2}\left[x-\tan ^{-1} x\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} x+\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{C} \\ &=\left(\frac{x^2+1}{2}\right) \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{x}{2}+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
Value of $\mathrm{A}=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider $\int x \tan ^{-1} x d x=\mathrm{A}\left(x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} x+\mathrm{C}$, where C is the constant of integration.
What is the value of B?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \int x \cdot \tan ^{-1} x d x=\mathrm{A}\left(x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} x+\mathrm{C} \\ & \text {Let } \mathrm{I}=\int x \cdot \tan ^{-1} x d x \\ &=\tan ^{-1} x \cdot\left(\frac{x^2}{2}\right)-\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{x^2}{1+x^2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\left(1+x^2\right)-1}{1+x^2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2}\left[\int 1 d x-\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} d x\right] \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2}\left[x-\tan ^{-1} x\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} x+\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{C} \\ &=\left(\frac{x^2+1}{2}\right) \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{x}{2}+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
Value of $\mathrm{B}=-\frac{1}{2}$

questions.q: $\int(\operatorname{In} x)^{-1} d x-\int(\operatorname{In} x)^{-2} d x$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int(\ln x)^{-1} d x-\int(\ln x)^{-2} d x \\ & =\int\left[\frac{1}{\ln x}-\frac{1}{(\ln x)^2}\right] d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Put } \ell \mathrm{n} \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \\ & \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} . \mathrm{dt} .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \int\left[\frac{1}{\ln \mathrm{x}}-\frac{1}{(\ln \mathrm{x})^2}\right] \mathrm{dx}=\int\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\int \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{dt}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\int \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{c}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\ln \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}=x(\ln x)^{-1}+c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is $\int \sqrt{x} e^{\sqrt{x}} d x$ equal to?
where $c$ is a constant of integration.
questions.solution:
$\int \sqrt{x} e^{\sqrt{x}} d x$
Put $\sqrt{x}=u\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}=d u \\ & \therefore d x=2 \sqrt{x} d u \\ &= \int u^2 e^u d u \times 2 \\ &= 2\left[u^2 \int e^u d u-\int 2 u e^u d u\right] \\ &= 2\left[u^2 \cdot e^u-2\left\{e^u \cdot u-e^u\right\}\right] \\ &= 2 u^2 e^u-4 u e^u+4 e^u \\ &= 2 x e^{\sqrt{x}}-4 \sqrt{x} e^{\sqrt{x}}+4 e^{\sqrt{x}} \\ &= 2 e^{\sqrt{x}}(x-2 \sqrt{x}+2)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following in respect of inverse circular functions :
I. $\sin^{-1}(-x)=-\sin^{-1}x$
II. $\cos^{-1}(-x)=\cos^{-1}x$
III. $\tan^{-1}(-x)=\pi-\tan^{-1}x$
IV. $\cot^{-1}(-x)=\pi-\cot^{-1}x$
How many of the above are correct ?
questions.solution:
Statement I: $\sin^{-1}(-x) = -\sin^{-1}x$ is a standard property of inverse trigonometric functions and is correct.

Statement II: The correct property is $\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cos^{-1}x$. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Statement III: The correct property is $\tan^{-1}(-x) = -\tan^{-1}x$. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Statement IV: $\cot^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cot^{-1}x$ is a standard property and is correct.

Exactly two of the given statements are correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then what is the value of $k$?
questions.solution:
Given $\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Using the formula $\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+y}{1-xy}\right)$, we get:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{k + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - \dfrac{k}{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$\dfrac{2k + 1}{2 - k} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$\dfrac{2k + 1}{2 - k} = 1$

$2k + 1 = 2 - k$

$3k = 1$

$k = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\tan\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\right]$?
questions.solution:
Let $\theta = \sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$\Rightarrow \sec \theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

The given expression becomes $\tan\left(\dfrac{1}{2} \theta\right) = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$

$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) = \tan(15^{\circ}) = \tan(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ})$

Using the formula $\tan(A - B) = \dfrac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A \tan B}$

$\tan(15^{\circ}) = \dfrac{\tan 45^{\circ} - \tan 30^{\circ}}{1 + \tan 45^{\circ} \tan 30^{\circ}}$

$\tan(15^{\circ}) = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

Rationalizing the denominator:

$\tan(15^{\circ}) = \dfrac{(\sqrt{3} - 1)^2}{(\sqrt{3} + 1)(\sqrt{3} - 1)} = \dfrac{3 + 1 - 2\sqrt{3}}{3 - 1}$

$\tan(15^{\circ}) = \dfrac{4 - 2\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2 - \sqrt{3}$

Answer: $2 - \sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $y = \sin^{-1}\left(x - \dfrac{4x^3}{27}\right)$.

What is $y$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sin^{-1}\left(x - \dfrac{4x^3}{27}\right)$

Substitute $x = 3\sin\theta$, which gives $\sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{3}$ or $\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

The expression becomes:

$y = \sin^{-1}\left(3\sin\theta - \dfrac{4(3\sin\theta)^3}{27}\right)$

$y = \sin^{-1}\left(3\sin\theta - \dfrac{4(27\sin^3\theta)}{27}\right)$

$y = \sin^{-1}(3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta)$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(3\theta) = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$:

$y = \sin^{-1}(\sin(3\theta))$

$y = 3\theta$

Substituting back the value of $\theta$:

$y = 3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

Answer: $3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $k$ is a root of $x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$, then what is $\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{k}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
The given equation is $x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$.

The roots of the equation are given by $x = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - 4}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{3}$.

Since $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$, both roots $2 + \sqrt{3}$ and $2 - \sqrt{3}$ are positive. Therefore, $k \gt 0$.

Using the standard inverse trigonometric identity for $x \gt 0$:

$\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Substituting $x = k$, we get:

$\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\tan\left[2\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Let $\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}$, which implies $\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

We need to evaluate $\tan\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

First, calculate $\tan(2\theta)$ using the double angle formula:

$\tan(2\theta) = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta} = \dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Now, apply the tangent subtraction formula:

$\tan\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\tan(2\theta) - \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}{1 + \tan(2\theta)\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}$

Substitute $\tan(2\theta) = \dfrac{4}{3}$ and $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$:

$\tan\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{3} - 1}{1 + \dfrac{4}{3}(1)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{\dfrac{7}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{7}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{7}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cot ^2\left(\sec ^{-1} 2\right)+\tan ^2\left(\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} 3\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Suppose } \mathrm{I}=\cot ^2\left(\sec ^{-1} 2\right)+\tan ^2\left(\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} 3\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\cot ^2\left(60^{\circ}\right)+\tan ^2+\left(\cot ^{-1} \sqrt{9-1}\right) \\ & \left\{\therefore \operatorname{cosec}^{-1} \mathrm{t}=\cot ^{-1} \sqrt{\mathrm{t}^2-1}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}+\tan ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{8}}\right)=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{8}=\frac{11}{24}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos ^{-1} x=\sin ^{-1} x$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: $\cos ^{-1} x=\sin ^{-1} x\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow & \frac{\pi}{2}-\sin ^{-1} x & =\sin ^{-1} x \\ & \Rightarrow & 2 \sin ^{-1} x & =\frac{\pi}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow & & \sin ^{-1} x\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sqrt{15+\cot ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-2 \cot ^{-1} 3\right)}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} 2 \cot ^{-1} 3 & =2 \tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{3}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{\frac{2}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{9}} \\ & =\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{8}\right)=\tan ^{-1} \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}$
So,
$\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{15+\cot ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right.}- & \left.2 \cot ^{-1} 3\right) \\
& =\sqrt{15+\cot ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} 1-\tan ^{-1} \frac{3}{4}\right)} \\
& =\sqrt{15+\cot ^2\left(\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\left.1-\frac{3}{4}\right)}{1+\frac{3}{4}}\right)\right]} \\
& =\sqrt{15+\cot ^2\left(\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{7}\right)} \\
& =\sqrt{15+7^2} \\
& =\sqrt{15+\cot ^2\left(\cot ^{-1} 7\right)} \\
& =\sqrt{15+49}=8
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $2 \cot \left(\frac{1}{2} \cos ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let, $\frac{1}{2} \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right)=\theta \Rightarrow \cos 2 \theta=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$
Now, $2 \cot \theta=2 \sqrt{\frac{1+\cos 2 \theta}{1-\cos 2 \theta}}2 \sqrt{\frac{1+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}}{1-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}}}=2 \sqrt{\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{3-\sqrt{5}}}=3+\sqrt{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sec ^{-1} p-\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} q=0$, where $\mathrm{p} \gt 0, \mathrm{q} \gt 0$; then what is the value of $\mathrm{p}^{-2}+\mathrm{q}^{-2}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } \sec ^{-1} \mathrm{p}-\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} \mathrm{q}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{p}}\right)=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{q}}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{p}}\right)^2+\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{q}}\right)^2=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{p}^{-2}+\mathrm{q}^{-2}=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $1+\sin ^2\left(\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{17}}\right)\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } 1+\sin ^2\left(\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{17}}\right)\right) \\ & =1+1-\left(\cos \left(\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{17}}\right)\right)\right)^2 \\ & =2-\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{17}}\right)^2=2-\frac{9}{17}=\frac{25}{17}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\tan ^{-1} \cot \left(\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} 2\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan ^{-1} \cot \left(\operatorname{cosec}^{-1} 2\right) \\ & =\tan ^{-1}\left(\cot \frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $3 \sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x=\pi$, then what is $x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 3 \sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x=\pi \\ \Rightarrow \quad & 2 \sin ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x=\pi\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin ^{-1} x+\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \sin ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x=\sin \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}$, where $0 \lt x \lt 6$, then what is $x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \quad \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ \Rightarrow & \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)=\tan ^{-1} 1-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow & \tan ^{-1} \frac{x}{3}=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-\frac{1}{2}}{1+\frac{1}{2}}\right) \\ \Rightarrow & \tan ^{-1} \frac{x}{3}=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{x}{3}=\frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow x=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of the following?
$\cot \left[\sin ^{-1} \frac{3}{5}+\cot ^{-1} \frac{3}{2}\right]$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Let } \sin ^{-1} \frac{3}{5}=\theta \Rightarrow \sin \theta=\frac{3}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{3}{\sqrt{5^2-3^2}}=\frac{3}{4} \\
& \therefore \cot =\left[\tan ^{-1} \frac{3}{4}+\tan ^{-1} \frac{2}{3}\right] \\
& =\cot \left[\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{2}{3}}{1-\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{2}{3}}\right)\right] \\
& =\cot \left[\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)\right]=\cot \left[\cot ^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{17}\right)\right]=\frac{6}{17}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the slope of the tangent of $y=\cos ^{-1}(\cos x)$ at $x=-\frac{\pi}{4} ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Slope of the tangent }=\frac{d y}{d x} \\ & \text {At } x=\frac{-\pi}{4}, \frac{d y}{d x}\left(\cos ^{-1}(\cos x)\right)=\frac{d}{d x}(-x)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore-\pi \leq x \leq 0 \\ & =\frac{d y}{d x}-1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\sin ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} y+\sin ^{-1} z=\frac{3 \pi}{2}$ for $0 \leq x, y, z \leq 1$. What is the value of $x^{1000}+y^{1001}+z^{1002}$ ?
questions.solution: $\sin ^{-1}(x)+\sin ^{-1}(y)+\sin ^{-1}(z)=\frac{3 \pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{2}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \sin ^{-1}(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}, \sin ^{-1}(y)=\frac{\pi}{2}, \sin ^{-1}(z)=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & x=y=z=1\left[\text { as } \sin ^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}\right] \\ & \text {So, } x^{1000}+y^{1001}+z^{1002} \\ & \Rightarrow 1+1+1=3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cot^{-1} 9 + \text{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $A = \cot^{-1} 9 \Rightarrow \cot A = 9 \Rightarrow \tan A = \dfrac{1}{9}$

Let $B = \text{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4}\right) \Rightarrow \text{cosec} B = \dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4} \Rightarrow \sin B = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{41}}$

From this, $\tan B = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{(\sqrt{41})^2 - 4^2}} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{41 - 16}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Using the formula $\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$:

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{4}{5}}{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)}$

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\dfrac{5 + 36}{45}}{\dfrac{45 - 4}{45}}$

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{41}{41} = 1$

Since $A, B \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, we have $A + B = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin ^{-1} \frac{2 p}{1+p^2}-\cos ^{-1} \frac{1-q^2}{1+q^2}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{2 x}{1-x^2}$, then what is $x$ equal to ?
questions.solution: $\sin ^{-1} \frac{2 p}{1+p^2}-\cos ^{-1} \frac{1-q^2}{1+q^2}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{2 x}{1-x^2}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2 \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{p}-2 \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{q}=2 \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{p}-\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{q}=\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1} \frac{p-q}{1+p q}=\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{p-q}{1+p q}\end{aligned}$

4. $-\frac{1}{4}$
  
Which of the above values of $x$ is/are the solutions of the equation $\tan ^{-1}(2 x)+\tan ^{-1}(3 x)=\frac{\pi}{4}$
questions.solution:
$\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x+3 x}{1-2 x .3 x}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\begin{gathered}
\tan ^{-1} \frac{5 x}{1-6 x^2}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\

\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{6},-1

Here $x=-1$ rejected.

Put $\mathrm{x}=\tan \theta . \Rightarrow \theta=\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x}y=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 \tan \theta}{\left(1+\tan ^2 \theta\right)}\right)=\cos ^{-1}(\sin 2 \theta)\begin{aligned} & =\cos ^{-1}\left(\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2 \theta\right)\right) \\ & =\frac{\pi}{2}-2 \theta \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2 \theta\right)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2 \tan ^{-1} x\right) \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-2}{1+x^2}, \text { when }|x| \lt 1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z}$ be positive real numbers such that $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z}$ are in GP and $\tan ^{-1} x, \tan ^{-1} y$ and $\tan ^{-1} z$ are in AP. Then which one of the following is correct?

$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \tan ^{-1} y=\tan ^{-1} x+\tan ^{-1} z \\
& \left(\therefore \tan ^{-1}, \tan ^{-1} y, \tan ^{-1} z \text { are in A.P }\right) \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a-b}{a+b}\right)$ equal to?
