questions.q: If the angle between the lines whose direction ratios are $(2,-1,2)$ and $(x, 3,5)$ is $\frac{\pi}{4}$, then the smaller value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Given direction ratios are $(2,-1,2)$ and $(\mathrm{x}, 3,5)$ We know that the angle between the lines whose direction ratios are $\left(a_1, b_1, c_1\right)$ and $\left(a_2, b_2, c_2\right)$ is
$\begin{aligned} & \cos \theta=\frac{\mathrm{a}_1 \mathrm{a}_2+\mathrm{b}_1 \mathrm{~b}_2+\mathrm{c}_1 \mathrm{c}_2}{\sqrt{\mathrm{a}_1^2+\mathrm{b}_1^2+\mathrm{c}_1^2} \sqrt{\mathrm{a}_2^2+\mathrm{b}_2^2+\mathrm{c}_2^2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{2 \mathrm{x}-3+10}{\sqrt{4+1+4} \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+9+25}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{x}+7}{\sqrt{9} \cdot \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+34}}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{2 x+7}{3 \sqrt{x^2+34}} \Rightarrow 2 x+7=3 \sqrt{\frac{x^2+34}{2}}\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{x}^2+49+28 \mathrm{x}=\frac{9\left(\mathrm{x}^2+34\right)}{2}$ (Squaring on both sides)
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2\left(4 x^2+49+28 x\right)=9 x^2+306 \\ & \Rightarrow 8 x^2+98+56 x=9 x^2+306 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2-56 x+208=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{x}=\frac{56 \pm \sqrt{3136-812}}{2}=\frac{56 \pm 48}{2}=28 \pm 24 \\ & =4,52 \\ & \text {Smaller value }=4\end{aligned}$

Eqn. of line

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A}(0,0,0), \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{a}, 0,0), \mathrm{C}(0, \mathrm{~b}, 0), \mathrm{D}(0,0, \mathrm{c})$
Let the equidistant point be $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z})\begin{aligned}
& \text { i.e, } A P=B P, A P=C P, A P=D P \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{(x-0)^2+(y-0)^2+(z-0)^2} \\
& =\sqrt{(x-a)^2+y^2+z^2} \\
& \Rightarrow x^2+y^2+z^2=(x-a)^2+y^2+z^2 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2=x^2-2 a x+a^2 \\
& \Rightarrow a^2-2 a x=0 \\
& \Rightarrow a(a-2 x)=0
\end{aligned}$
Since $a \neq 0, a=2 x \Rightarrow x=\frac{a}{2}$

questions.solution:
The equation of sphere is

Comparing the equation with general form of sphere, $x^2+y^2+z^2+2 u x+2 v y+2 w z-d=0\begin{aligned} & \text { we get, }=\frac{-6}{2}=-3, v=\frac{8}{2}=4, w=\frac{-10}{2}=-5, d=1 \\ & \text {Radius }=\sqrt{u^2+v^2+w^2-d} \\ & =\sqrt{(-3)^2+(4)^2+(-5)^2-1} \\ & =\sqrt{9+16+25-1} \\ & =\sqrt{49}=7\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Paragraph: A line L passes through the point $\mathrm{P}(5,-6,7)$ and is parallel to the planes $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}=1$ and $2 \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}-2 \mathrm{z}=3$.
Question: What are the direction ratios of the line of intersection of the given planes?
questions.solution:
Let $a, b, c$ be the direction ratios of the line. Then its equation is
$\frac{x-5}{a}=\frac{y+6}{b}=\frac{z-7}{c}$...(i)
Since (i) is parallel to the planes $x+y+z=1$ and $2 x-y-2 z=3$ then
$a(1)+b(1)+c(1)=0 \text { and } a(2)+b(-1)+c(-2)=0$
By cross multiplication
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{a}{-1}=\frac{b}{4}=\frac{c}{-3}=\lambda \\
& \Rightarrow a=-\lambda, b=4 \lambda, c=-3 \lambda
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ Direction ratios of the line are
$ \lt -1,4,-3 \gt = \lt 1,-4,3 \gt $
Substituting a, $\mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ in (i), we get
$\frac{x-5}{-1}=\frac{y+6}{4}=\frac{z-7}{-3}$  ...(ii)
Hence equation of the line is
$\frac{x-5}{-1}=\frac{y+6}{4}=\frac{z-7}{-3}$

questions.q:
Paragraph: Let Q be the image of the point $\mathrm{P}(-2,1,-5)$ in the plane $3 x-2 y+2 z+1=0$.
Question: Consider the following: 1. The coordinates of $Q$ are $(4,-3,-1)$. 2. PQ is of length more than 8 units. 3. The point $(1,-1,-3)$ is the mid-point of the line segment PQ and lies on the given plane. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let $Q\left(x_1, y_1, z_1\right)$ be the image of the point $P$.
The direction ratios of $P Q$ are $3,-2,2$. ...(i)
The Equation of line $P Q$ is $\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y-1}{-2}=\frac{z+5}{2}=r$ Coordinates of any point on the line $P Q$ is $3 r-2,-2 r+$ 1 and $2 r-5$.
Let $Q(3 r-2,-2 r+1,2 r-5)$ be such a point.
Let $L$ be the mid point of $P Q, L=\left(\frac{3 r}{2}-2,1-r, r-5\right)$
Since $L$ lies on the plane $3 x-2 y+2 z+1=0$
So, $3\left(\frac{3 r}{2}-2\right)-2(1-r)+2(r-5)+1=0\Rightarrow \frac{17}{2} r-17=0 \Rightarrow r=2$
So, coordinates of $Q$ are $(3 \times 2-2,-2 \times 2+1,2 \times 2-5)=(4,-3,-1)$  ...(ii)
Also the mid point of $P Q$ is $L=\left(\frac{3 \times 2}{2}-2,1-2,2-5\right)=(1,-1,-3)$...(iii)
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore P Q=\sqrt{(-2-4)^2+(1+3)^2+(-5+1)^2}=\sqrt{68} \\
& \Rightarrow P Q=2 \sqrt{17} \gt 8
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (4) is correct.

questions.q: The equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes $x+y+z=1,2 x+3 y+4 z=7$, and perpendicular to the plane $x-5 y+3 z=5$ is given by
questions.solution:
Given planes, $p_1: x+y+z=1\mathrm{p}_2: 2 \mathrm{x}+3 \mathrm{y}+4 \mathrm{z}=7$
So, equation of plane passing through intersection of planes $p_1$ and $p_2$ is
$\begin{aligned} & x+y+z-1+k(2 x+3 y+4 z-7)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x+y+z-1+2 k x+3 k y+4 k z-7 k=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x(1+2 k)+y(1+3 k)+z(1+4 k)-1-7 k=0\end{aligned}$
This is perpendicular to $x-5 y+3 z=5$.
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}-5 \mathrm{y}+3 \mathrm{z}-5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 1(1+2 \mathrm{k})-5(1+3 \mathrm{k})+3(1+4 \mathrm{k})=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 1+2 \mathrm{k}-5-15 \mathrm{k}+3+12 \mathrm{k}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow-\mathrm{k}-1=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=-1\end{aligned}\therefore$ Equation of plane is
$\begin{aligned} & x+y+z-1-1(2 x+3 y+4 z-7)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x+y+z-1-2 x-3 y-4 z+7=0 \\ & \Rightarrow-x-2 y-3 z+6=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x+2 y+3 z-6=0\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
$\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ be distinct real numbers
$\begin{aligned}
& \vec{a}=\alpha \hat{i}+\beta \hat{j}+\gamma \hat{k} \\
& \vec{b}=\beta \hat{i}+\gamma \hat{j}+\alpha \hat{k} \\
& \vec{c}=\gamma \hat{i}+\alpha \hat{j}+\beta \hat{k}
\end{aligned}$
Let $\alpha=1, \beta=2$ and $\alpha=3$
then, $\quad \vec{a}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}\begin{aligned}
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}
\end{aligned}$
Now, $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{ab}}|=\sqrt{(2-1)^2}+(3-2)^2+(1-3)^2=\sqrt{6}$
Similarly $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{bc}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{ac}}|=\sqrt{6}$
Hence, point for equilateral triangle.

What are the direction ratios of the line of intersection of the given planes?
questions.solution:
To find, intersection point first put $z=0\begin{aligned}
& 2 x-y=2 \\
& x+y=1 \\
& \hline 3 x=3 \\
& x=1 \\
& x+y=1 \\
& y=1-x
\end{aligned}$
At $x=1, y=0(x, y, z) \equiv(1,0,0)$
Putting $x=0\begin{aligned}
& y-z=1 \\
& \frac{-y+3 z=2}{2 z=3} \\
& z=\frac{3}{2} \\
& y=1+z=1+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\
& (x, y, z) \equiv\left(0, \frac{5}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Point of intersection $\left(x_1, y_1, z_1\right) \equiv(1,0,0)\left(x_2, y_2, z_2\right) \equiv\left(0, \frac{5}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)$
Hence direction ratios of the line of intersection of given plane $\langle 2,-5,-3\rangle$.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & a=\mathrm{BC}=\sqrt{(2)^2+(-1)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{4+1+1}=\sqrt{6} \\ & b=\mathrm{CA}=\sqrt{(2)^2+(2)^2+(2)^2}=\sqrt{4+4+4}=\sqrt{12} \\ & c=\mathrm{AB}=\sqrt{(4)^2+(1)^2+(1)^2}=\sqrt{16+1+1}=\sqrt{18} .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \cos \mathrm{B} & =\frac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2 a c}=\frac{6+18-12}{2 \sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{18}} \\ & =\frac{12}{2 \sqrt{108}}=\frac{12}{2 \times 6 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$

Question : What is the area of the triangle?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & a=\mathrm{BC}=\sqrt{(2)^2+(-1)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{4+1+1}=\sqrt{6} \\ & b=\mathrm{CA}=\sqrt{(2)^2+(2)^2+(2)^2}=\sqrt{4+4+4}=\sqrt{12} \\ & c=\mathrm{AB}=\sqrt{(4)^2+(1)^2+(1)^2}=\sqrt{16+1+1}=\sqrt{18} .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \cos \mathrm{C} & =\frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2 a b} \\ & =\frac{6+12-18}{2 \sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{12}}=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \cos \mathrm{C} & =\cos 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow \angle \mathrm{C}=90^{\circ} \end{aligned}\therefore$ It is right triangle. $\text { Area of } \begin{aligned} \triangle \mathrm{ABC} & =\frac{1}{2} \times \text { base } \times \text { height } \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{12}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{72} \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \sqrt{2}=3 \sqrt{2} \text { square unit. } \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A triangular plane ABC with centroid (1, 2, 3) cuts the coordinate
axes at A, B, C respectively.
What is the equation of plane ABC?
questions.solution:
The plane passes through the point $\mathrm{A}(3,0,0), \mathrm{B}(0,6,0)$ and $C(0,0,9)$. So, it should satisfy the equation given in option for all the three points.
From option (A)
For point A $(3,0,0)x+2 y+3 z=1\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & 3+0+0 \neq 1 \\ \therefore & \text { option (A) is wrong. } \\ & \text {From option (B) } \\ & \text {For point } A(3,0,0) \\ & 3 \mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}=3 \\ \therefore & 3(3)+0+0 \neq 3 \\ \therefore & \text { option (B) is wrong. } \\ & \text {From option (C) } \\ & \text {For point } \mathrm{A}(3,0,0) \\ & 2 \mathrm{x}+3 \mathrm{y}+6 \mathrm{z}=18 \\ \therefore \quad & 2(3)+0+0 \neq 18 \\ \therefore \quad & \text { option }(\mathrm{C}) \text { is wrong. } \\ & \text {From option }(\mathrm{D}) \\ & \text {For point } \mathrm{A}(3,0,0) \\ & 6 \mathrm{x}+3 \mathrm{y}+2 \mathrm{z}=18\end{array}
$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & 6(3)+0+0=18 \\
& \text { For point } B(0,6,0) \\
& 6 x+3 y+2 z=18 \\
\therefore \quad & 0+3(6)+0=18 \\
& \text { For point } C(0,0,9) \\
& 6 x+3 y+2 z=18 \\
& 0+0+2 \times 9=18
\end{array}
$\therefore \quad$ Option (D) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What are the direction ratios of the line of intersection of the planes $x=3 z+4$ and $y=2 z-3$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll} & x=3 z+4 \\ \text { and } & y=2 z-3\end{array}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x-4}{3}=z$
and $\quad \frac{y+3}{2}=z\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x-4}{3}=\frac{y+3}{2}=\frac{z}{1}\therefore$ Direction ratios are proportional to $ \lt 3,2,1 \gt $.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the number of solutions of the equation $\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 3 x=1$ for $0 \lt  x \lt  \pi ?$
questions.solution:
We have given, $\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 3 x=1$ (given)
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \cos 2 x \cdot \cot 3 x-\sin 2 x \cdot \sin 3 x=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos (2 x+3 x)=\cos 5 x=0
\end{aligned}$
Hence $5 x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{5 \pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{2}, \frac{9 \pi}{2}, \ldots$
But $0 \lt  x \lt  \pi\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{10}, \frac{3 \pi}{10}, \frac{5 \pi}{10}, \frac{7 \pi}{10}, \frac{9 \pi}{10}$
Thus only five values of $x$ are possible.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then what is the number of values of $x$ satisfying the equation $\tan x + \sec x = 2\cos x$?
questions.solution:
The given equation is $\tan x + \sec x = 2\cos x$.

Rewriting the equation in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$:

$\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{1}{\cos x} = 2\cos x$

For the equation to be defined, $\cos x \neq 0$, which means $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Thus, $x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

Multiplying both sides by $\cos x$:

$\sin x + 1 = 2\cos^2 x$

Substituting $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$:

$\sin x + 1 = 2(1 - \sin^2 x)$

$2\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0$

Factoring the quadratic equation:

$(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1) = 0$

This gives $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $\sin x = -1$.

Since $x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\sin x \geq 0$. Therefore, $\sin x = -1$ is rejected.

For $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, the only solution in the given interval is $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Thus, there is exactly $1$ value of $x$ satisfying the equation.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the general solution of $\cos ^{100} x-\sin ^{100} x=1$ ?
where $n$ is an integer.
questions.solution:
Since, $\cos ^2 \mathrm{x} \in[0,1] \Rightarrow \cos ^{100} \mathrm{x} \in[0,1]$ and $\sin ^2 x \in[0,1] \Rightarrow \sin ^{100} x \in[0,1]$
Hence, $\cos ^{100} \mathrm{x}-\sin ^{100} \mathrm{x}=1$ is only possible when
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos ^{100} x=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos ^2 x=1 \Rightarrow x=n \pi \pm 0 \Rightarrow x=n \pi
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $\cos(2x + 3y) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\cos(3x + 2y) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, where $-\pi \lt (2x + 3y) \lt \pi$ and $-\pi \lt (3x + 2y) \lt \pi$.

How many values does $(y - x)$ have?
questions.solution:
Let $A = 2x + 3y$ and $B = 3x + 2y$.

We are given $\cos A = \dfrac{1}{2}$ with $-\pi \lt A \lt \pi$.

The possible values for $A$ are $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

We are also given $\cos B = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ with $-\pi \lt B \lt \pi$.

The possible values for $B$ are $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

We need to find the number of values of $(y - x)$.

Observe that $A - B = (2x + 3y) - (3x + 2y) = y - x$.

The possible values for $A - B$ are:

$\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$-\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$-\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Since all four values are distinct, $(y - x)$ has four values.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the smallest positive $x$ satisfying $\log_{\sin x}\cos x+\log_{\cos x}\sin x=2$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $t = \log_{\sin x}\cos x$.

The given equation becomes $t + \dfrac{1}{t} = 2$.

$t^2 - 2t + 1 = 0$

$(t - 1)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1$

$\log_{\sin x}\cos x = 1$

$\cos x = \sin x$

$\tan x = 1$

The smallest positive value of $x$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

For $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\cos x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, which satisfy the conditions for the base and argument of logarithms (positive and not equal to $1$).

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $\cos(2x + 3y) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\cos(3x + 2y) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, where $-\pi \lt (2x + 3y) \lt \pi$ and $-\pi \lt (3x + 2y) \lt \pi$.

How many values does $(x + y)$ have?
questions.solution:
Let $2x + 3y = u$ and $3x + 2y = v$.

Given $\cos u = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $-\pi \lt u \lt \pi$, the possible values of $u$ are $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Given $\cos v = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $-\pi \lt v \lt \pi$, the possible values of $v$ are $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Adding the two equations, we get $u + v = 5(x + y) \Rightarrow x + y = \dfrac{u + v}{5}$.

The possible values of $u + v$ are:

$\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$-\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = -\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$-\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Since all four values of $u + v$ are distinct, there are exactly four distinct values for $x + y$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan (\pi \cos \theta)=\cot (\pi \sin \theta), 0 \lt \theta \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$; then what is the value of $8 \sin ^2\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{ll}\text { Given, } & \tan (\pi \cos \theta)=\cot (\pi \sin \theta) \\ \text { Let } & \tan (\pi \cos \theta)=\cot (\pi \sin \theta)=\mathrm{k} \\ \Rightarrow & \pi \cos \theta=\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{k}, \pi \sin \theta=\cot ^{-1} \mathrm{k} \\ \text { Since, } & \pi \cos \theta+\pi \sin \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \cos \theta+\sin \theta=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \sin \left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \\ \Rightarrow & 8 \sin ^2\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $1+2(\sin x+\cos x)(\sin x-\cos x)=0$ where $0 \lt x \lt 360^{\circ}$, then how many values does $x$ take?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 1+2(\sin x+\cos x)(\sin x-\cos x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 1+2\left(\sin ^2 x-\cos ^2 x\right)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 1-2 \cos ^2 2 x=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 2 x=\frac{1}{2} \quad \Rightarrow \cos 2 x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \Rightarrow x=n \pi \pm \frac{\pi}{8} \quad \therefore \quad x=0, \pi-\frac{\pi}{8} \\ & \pi+\frac{\pi}{8}, 2 \pi-\frac{\pi}{8} . \text { Four values. }\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $4 \sin ^2 x=3$, where $0 \leq x \leq \pi$. What is $\tan 3 x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \sin ^2 x=\frac{3}{4}=\sin x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{2 \pi}{3}[\therefore 0 \leq x \leq \pi] \\ & \therefore \tan 3 x=\tan \pi=\tan 2 \pi=0\end{aligned}$

So, $3\left[3-\tan ^2\left(-60^{\circ}\right)-\cot \left(-60^{\circ}\right)\right]^2=3\left[3-3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right]^2=3 \times \frac{1}{3}=1$

questions.q: The value of $x$, satisfying the equation $\log _{\cos x} \sin x=1$, where $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$, is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \log _{\cos x} \sin x=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\log \sin x}{\log \cos x}=1\end{aligned}$
For $x=\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\log \sin \frac{\pi}{4}}{\log \cos \frac{\pi}{4}}=\frac{\log \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{\log \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}=1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the equation: $k \sin x+\cos 2 x=2 k-7$
If the equation possesses solution, then what is the minimum value of k ?
questions.solution:
$K \sin x+\cos 2 x=2 K-7K \sin x+\left(1-2 \sin ^2 x\right)=(2 K-7)2 \sin ^2 x-K \sin x+(2 K-8)=0$
This is a quadratic equation in $\sin x$.
$\sin x=\frac{-(-K) \pm \sqrt{K^2-4(2)(2 K-8)}}{2 \times 2}$
For minimum value of $K$, $\sin x=-1\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{K \pm \sqrt{K^2-16 K+64}}{4}=-1 \\
& \Rightarrow( \pm) \sqrt{K^2-16 K+64}=-K-4
\end{aligned}$
Squaring both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& K^2-16 K+64=K^2+16+8 K \\
& \Rightarrow 24 K=48 \\
& \Rightarrow K=2
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is/are the solutions of the trigonometric equation $\operatorname{cosec} \mathrm{x}+\cot \mathrm{x}=\sqrt{3}$, where $0 \lt \mathrm{x} \lt 2 \pi$ ?
questions.solution:
Given equation:
$\begin{aligned}
& \operatorname{cosec} x+\cot x=\sqrt{3} \\
& \operatorname{cosec} x-\cot x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \operatorname{cosec} x=\sqrt{3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \operatorname{cosec} x=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}$
Possible values of $x=\frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{2 \pi}{3}\therefore$ Option (2) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which one of the following is one of the solutions of the equation $\tan 2 \theta \cdot \tan \theta=1$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \tan 2 \theta \cdot \tan \theta=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 \tan \theta}{1-\tan ^2 \theta} \times \tan \theta=1 \\
& 2 \tan ^2 \theta=1-\tan ^2 \theta \\
& 3 \tan ^2 \theta=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \tan ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \tan \theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\tan 30^{\circ} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta=30^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{6}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\theta$ lies in the fourth quadrant and $3\cot\theta+4=0$, then what is the value of $\sin 2\theta+\cos 2\theta$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $3\cot\theta + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow \cot\theta = -\dfrac{4}{3}$

Since $\theta$ lies in the fourth quadrant, $\cos\theta \gt 0$ and $\sin\theta \lt 0$.

From $\cot\theta = -\dfrac{4}{3}$, we can consider the base as $4$ and the perpendicular as $3$.

Hypotenuse $= \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5$

Therefore, $\sin\theta = -\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Using double angle formulas:

$\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2\left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right) = -\dfrac{24}{25}$

$\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^2 - \left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16}{25} - \dfrac{9}{25} = \dfrac{7}{25}$

Adding both values:

$\sin 2\theta + \cos 2\theta = -\dfrac{24}{25} + \dfrac{7}{25} = -\dfrac{17}{25}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{17}{25}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos\alpha+\cos\beta=0=\sin\alpha+\sin\beta$, $\alpha\neq\beta$ then what is a value of $\cos 2\alpha+\cos 2\beta+2\cos(\alpha+\beta)$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $z_1 = \cos\alpha + i\sin\alpha$ and $z_2 = \cos\beta + i\sin\beta$.

From the given conditions:

$z_1 + z_2 = (\cos\alpha + \cos\beta) + i(\sin\alpha + \sin\beta) = 0$

Squaring both sides:

$(z_1 + z_2)^2 = 0$

$z_1^2 + z_2^2 + 2z_1 z_2 = 0$

Using De Moivre's theorem, $z_1^2 = \cos 2\alpha + i\sin 2\alpha$ and $z_2^2 = \cos 2\beta + i\sin 2\beta$. The product term is $2z_1 z_2 = 2(\cos(\alpha+\beta) + i\sin(\alpha+\beta))$.

Substituting these into the squared equation:

$(\cos 2\alpha + \cos 2\beta + 2\cos(\alpha+\beta)) + i(\sin 2\alpha + \sin 2\beta + 2\sin(\alpha+\beta)) = 0$

Equating the real part to zero:

$\cos 2\alpha + \cos 2\beta + 2\cos(\alpha+\beta) = 0$

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $2\sec 4\beta=\tan 2\alpha+\cot 2\alpha$, then which one of the following is a possible value of $(\alpha+\beta)$ ?
questions.solution:
The given equation is $2\sec 4\beta = \tan 2\alpha + \cot 2\alpha$

We know that $\tan \theta + \cot \theta = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} + \dfrac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta \cos \theta} = \dfrac{2}{\sin 2\theta}$

Substituting $\theta = 2\alpha$, we get $\tan 2\alpha + \cot 2\alpha = \dfrac{2}{\sin 4\alpha}$

The equation becomes $2\sec 4\beta = \dfrac{2}{\sin 4\alpha}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\cos 4\beta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin 4\alpha}$

$\Rightarrow \cos 4\beta = \sin 4\alpha$

$\Rightarrow \cos 4\beta = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 4\alpha\right)$

The general solution is $4\beta = 2n\pi \pm \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 4\alpha\right)$ where $n$ is an integer.

Taking the positive sign, we get:

$4\beta = 2n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 4\alpha$

$\Rightarrow 4(\alpha + \beta) = 2n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = \dfrac{n\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{8}$

For $n = 0$, a possible value is $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{8}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x=\sec\theta-\tan\theta$ and $y=\csc\theta+\cot\theta$, then which one of the following is correct ?
questions.solution:
Given $x = \sec\theta - \tan\theta = \dfrac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$

$y = \csc\theta + \cot\theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$

Consider $x(y+1)$:

$x(y+1) = \left(\dfrac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) \left(\dfrac{1 + \cos\theta}{\sin\theta} + 1\right)$

$x(y+1) = \left(\dfrac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) \left(\dfrac{1 + \cos\theta + \sin\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)$

$x(y+1) = \dfrac{1 + \cos\theta + \sin\theta - \sin\theta - \sin\theta\cos\theta - \sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$

$x(y+1) = \dfrac{(1 - \sin^2\theta) + \cos\theta - \sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$

$x(y+1) = \dfrac{\cos^2\theta + \cos\theta - \sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$

$x(y+1) = \dfrac{\cos\theta(\cos\theta + 1 - \sin\theta)}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$

$x(y+1) = \dfrac{1 + \cos\theta - \sin\theta}{\sin\theta}$

$x(y+1) = \csc\theta + \cot\theta - 1$

Substituting $y = \csc\theta + \cot\theta$:

$x(y+1) = y - 1$

$xy + x - y + 1 = 0$

Answer: $x-y+xy+1=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{3}$, then what is the value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right)$ ?
questions.solution:
Using the trigonometric identity $2\sin A \sin B = \cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B)$, we have:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) - \cos\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2} + \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}[\cos\theta - \cos(2\theta)]$

Using the double angle formula $\cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$, we get:

$\cos(2\theta) = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 - 1 = \dfrac{2}{9} - 1 = -\dfrac{7}{9}$

Substituting the values of $\cos\theta$ and $\cos(2\theta)$:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{7}{9}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{3}{9} + \dfrac{7}{9}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{10}{9}\right] = \dfrac{5}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{9}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are acute angles such that $2A+2B=\pi$, then what is the maximum value of $\sin A\cdot\sin B$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $2A + 2B = \pi$, which simplifies to $A + B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Since $A$ and $B$ are acute angles, $B = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - A$.

The expression to maximize is $\sin A \cdot \sin B$.

Substituting $B = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - A$, we get $\sin A \cdot \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - A\right) = \sin A \cdot \cos A$.

Multiplying and dividing by $2$, we obtain $\dfrac{2\sin A \cos A}{2} = \dfrac{\sin 2A}{2}$.

The maximum value of $\sin 2A$ is $1$, which occurs when $2A = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, or $A = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Therefore, the maximum value of $\sin A \cdot \sin B$ is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $\sin A + \sin B = p$ and $\cos A + \cos B = q$.

What is $\dfrac{p^2 - q^2}{p^2 + q^2}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sin A + \sin B$ and $q = \cos A + \cos B$.

Squaring both equations:

$p^2 = \sin^2 A + \sin^2 B + 2\sin A \sin B$

$q^2 = \cos^2 A + \cos^2 B + 2\cos A \cos B$

Adding the two equations:

$p^2 + q^2 = (\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) + (\sin^2 B + \cos^2 B) + 2(\cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B)$

$p^2 + q^2 = 1 + 1 + 2\cos(A - B) = 2(1 + \cos(A - B))$

Subtracting $q^2$ from $p^2$:

$p^2 - q^2 = (\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A) + (\sin^2 B - \cos^2 B) - 2(\cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B)$

$p^2 - q^2 = -\cos 2A - \cos 2B - 2\cos(A + B)$

Using the sum-to-product formula $\cos 2A + \cos 2B = 2\cos(A + B)\cos(A - B)$:

$p^2 - q^2 = -2\cos(A + B)\cos(A - B) - 2\cos(A + B)$

$p^2 - q^2 = -2\cos(A + B)(1 + \cos(A - B))$

Dividing $p^2 - q^2$ by $p^2 + q^2$:

$\dfrac{p^2 - q^2}{p^2 + q^2} = \dfrac{-2\cos(A + B)(1 + \cos(A - B))}{2(1 + \cos(A - B))}$

$\dfrac{p^2 - q^2}{p^2 + q^2} = -\cos(A + B)$

Using the property $\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos \theta$:

$-\cos(A + B) = \cos(\pi - (A + B)) = \cos(\pi - A - B)$

Answer: $\cos(\pi - A - B)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $p = \text{cosec}\, 20°$ and $q = \text{cosec}\, 70°$.

What is $\dfrac{p^2 + q^2}{p^2 q^2}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \text{cosec}\, 20^\circ$ and $q = \text{cosec}\, 70^\circ$.

The given expression is $\dfrac{p^2 + q^2}{p^2 q^2}$.

This can be rewritten as $\dfrac{1}{q^2} + \dfrac{1}{p^2}$.

Substituting the values of $p$ and $q$:

$\dfrac{1}{\text{cosec}^2 70^\circ} + \dfrac{1}{\text{cosec}^2 20^\circ}$

$= \sin^2 70^\circ + \sin^2 20^\circ$

Since $\sin 70^\circ = \sin(90^\circ - 20^\circ) = \cos 20^\circ$, we get:

$= \cos^2 20^\circ + \sin^2 20^\circ$

$= 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $\sin A + \sin B = p$ and $\cos A + \cos B = q$.

What is $\dfrac{p}{q}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sin A + \sin B$ and $q = \cos A + \cos B$.

Using the sum-to-product formulas:

$p = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)$

$q = 2 \cos\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)$

Dividing $p$ by $q$:

$\dfrac{p}{q} = \dfrac{2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)}{2 \cos\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)}$

$\dfrac{p}{q} = \tan\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $p = \text{cosec}\, 20°$ and $q = \text{cosec}\, 70°$.

What is $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\,p}{4} - \dfrac{q}{4}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \text{cosec}\, 20^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sin 20^\circ}$ and $q = \text{cosec}\, 70^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sin 70^\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\cos 20^\circ}$

Substituting $p$ and $q$ into the given expression:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\,p}{4} - \dfrac{q}{4} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4 \sin 20^\circ} - \dfrac{1}{4 \cos 20^\circ}$

Taking the common denominator:

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \cos 20^\circ - \sin 20^\circ}{4 \sin 20^\circ \cos 20^\circ}$

Multiplying and dividing the numerator by $2$, and rewriting the denominator:

$= \dfrac{2 \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos 20^\circ - \dfrac{1}{2} \sin 20^\circ \right)}{2 (2 \sin 20^\circ \cos 20^\circ)}$

Using the identities $\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$, and $\sin 2\theta = 2 \sin \theta \cos \theta$:

$= \dfrac{2 (\sin 60^\circ \cos 20^\circ - \cos 60^\circ \sin 20^\circ)}{2 \sin 40^\circ}$

Using the identity $\sin(A - B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B$:

$= \dfrac{2 \sin(60^\circ - 20^\circ)}{2 \sin 40^\circ}$

$= \dfrac{2 \sin 40^\circ}{2 \sin 40^\circ}$

$= 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the three (03) items that follow:
Let $p = \sin 35°$, $q = \sin 25°$ and $r = \sin(-95°)$.

What is $(p + q + r)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sin 35^\circ$, $q = \sin 25^\circ$, and $r = \sin(-95^\circ)$.

We need to find the value of $p + q + r$.

$p + q = \sin 35^\circ + \sin 25^\circ$

Using the formula $\sin A + \sin B = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)$:

$p + q = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{35^\circ + 25^\circ}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{35^\circ - 25^\circ}{2}\right)$

$p + q = 2 \sin 30^\circ \cos 5^\circ$

Since $\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$:

$p + q = 2 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cos 5^\circ = \cos 5^\circ$

Now, evaluating $r$:

$r = \sin(-95^\circ) = -\sin 95^\circ$

$r = -\sin(90^\circ + 5^\circ) = -\cos 5^\circ$

Therefore, $p + q + r = \cos 5^\circ - \cos 5^\circ = 0$

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the three (03) items that follow:
Let $p = \sin 35°$, $q = \sin 25°$ and $r = \sin(-95°)$.

What is $(pq + qr + rp)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sin 35^\circ$, $q = \sin 25^\circ$, and $r = \sin(-95^\circ) = -\sin(90^\circ + 5^\circ) = -\cos 5^\circ$.

$p + q + r = \sin 35^\circ + \sin 25^\circ - \cos 5^\circ$

Using $\sin A + \sin B = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)$:

$p + q + r = 2 \sin 30^\circ \cos 5^\circ - \cos 5^\circ = 2 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cos 5^\circ - \cos 5^\circ = 0$

We know that $(p + q + r)^2 = p^2 + q^2 + r^2 + 2(pq + qr + rp) = 0$

$pq + qr + rp = -\dfrac{1}{2}(p^2 + q^2 + r^2)$

Now, $p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = \sin^2 35^\circ + \sin^2 25^\circ + \cos^2 5^\circ$

Using $\sin^2 \theta = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}$ and $\cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}$:

$p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = \dfrac{1 - \cos 70^\circ}{2} + \dfrac{1 - \cos 50^\circ}{2} + \dfrac{1 + \cos 10^\circ}{2}$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos 70^\circ + \cos 50^\circ - \cos 10^\circ)$

Using $\cos C + \cos D = 2 \cos\left(\dfrac{C+D}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{C-D}{2}\right)$:

$\cos 70^\circ + \cos 50^\circ = 2 \cos 60^\circ \cos 10^\circ = 2 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cos 10^\circ = \cos 10^\circ$

So, $p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos 10^\circ - \cos 10^\circ) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Therefore, $pq + qr + rp = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{3}{4}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the three (03) items that follow:
Let $p = \sin 35°$, $q = \sin 25°$ and $r = \sin(-95°)$.

What is $(p^2 + q^2 + r^2)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \sin 35^\circ$, $q = \sin 25^\circ$, and $r = \sin(-95^\circ)$.

Simplifying $r$:

$r = -\sin(90^\circ + 5^\circ) = -\cos 5^\circ$

We need to find the value of $p^2 + q^2 + r^2$:

$p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = \sin^2 35^\circ + \sin^2 25^\circ + \cos^2 5^\circ$

Using the identities $\sin^2 \theta = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}$ and $\cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}$:

$p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = \dfrac{1 - \cos 70^\circ}{2} + \dfrac{1 - \cos 50^\circ}{2} + \dfrac{1 + \cos 10^\circ}{2}$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos 70^\circ + \cos 50^\circ - \cos 10^\circ)$

Using the sum-to-product formula $\cos C + \cos D = 2 \cos\left(\dfrac{C+D}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{C-D}{2}\right)$:

$\cos 70^\circ + \cos 50^\circ = 2 \cos\left(\dfrac{70^\circ + 50^\circ}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{70^\circ - 50^\circ}{2}\right)$

$= 2 \cos 60^\circ \cos 10^\circ$

$= 2 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cos 10^\circ = \cos 10^\circ$

Substituting this back into the expression:

$p^2 + q^2 + r^2 = \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos 10^\circ - \cos 10^\circ)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} - 0 = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90°)|$.

What is the maximum value of $p$?
questions.solution:
Given $p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90^\circ)|$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(\alpha - 90^\circ) = -\sin(90^\circ - \alpha) = -\cos\alpha$

Substituting this into the expression for $p$

$p = |\sin\alpha - (-\cos\alpha)| = |\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha|$

The maximum value of the expression $a\sin\alpha + b\cos\alpha$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$

Here, $a = 1$ and $b = 1$

Maximum value of $\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$

Therefore, the maximum value of $p$ is $\sqrt{2}$

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90°)|$.

What is the minimum value of $p$?
questions.solution:
$p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90^\circ)|$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(\alpha - 90^\circ) = -\sin(90^\circ - \alpha) = -\cos\alpha$, we get:

$p = |\sin\alpha - (-\cos\alpha)| = |\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha|$

Multiplying and dividing the expression inside the modulus by $\sqrt{2}$:

$p = \sqrt{2} \left| \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha \right|$

$p = \sqrt{2} |\sin(\alpha + 45^\circ)|$

Since the absolute value of any real expression is non-negative, the minimum possible value of $p$ is $0$. This minimum is achieved when $\sin(\alpha + 45^\circ) = 0$, which occurs at $\alpha = -45^\circ$.

Therefore, the minimum value of $p$ is $0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the three (03) items that follow:
Let $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$ and $q = \cot\alpha - \cot 2\alpha$.

What is $(p/q)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$ and $q = \cot\alpha - \cot 2\alpha$

Expressing $q$ in terms of $\tan$ gives:

$q = \dfrac{1}{\tan\alpha} - \dfrac{1}{\tan 2\alpha}$

$q = \dfrac{\tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha}{\tan\alpha \tan 2\alpha}$

Substituting $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$ into the expression for $q$:

$q = \dfrac{p}{\tan\alpha \tan 2\alpha}$

Rearranging the terms yields:

$\dfrac{p}{q} = \tan\alpha \tan 2\alpha$

Answer: $\tan\alpha \cdot \tan 2\alpha$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the three (03) items that follow:
Let $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$ and $q = \cot\alpha - \cot 2\alpha$.

What is $(p + q)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$ and $q = \cot\alpha - \cot 2\alpha$.

Simplifying $p$:
$p = \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha} - \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha \cos\alpha - \cos 2\alpha \sin\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin(2\alpha - \alpha)}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha}$

Simplifying $q$:
$q = \dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha} - \dfrac{\cos 2\alpha}{\sin 2\alpha} = \dfrac{\cos\alpha \sin 2\alpha - \sin\alpha \cos 2\alpha}{\sin\alpha \sin 2\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin(2\alpha - \alpha)}{\sin\alpha \sin 2\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\sin\alpha \sin 2\alpha} = \dfrac{1}{\sin 2\alpha}$

Now, adding $p$ and $q$:
$p + q = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\sin 2\alpha}$

Using $\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha \cos\alpha$:
$p + q = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{2\sin\alpha \cos\alpha}$

$p + q = \dfrac{2\sin^2\alpha + \cos 2\alpha}{2\sin\alpha \cos\alpha \cos 2\alpha}$

Using the identity $\cos 2\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^2\alpha$ in the numerator and $2\sin\alpha \cos\alpha = \sin 2\alpha$ in the denominator:
$p + q = \dfrac{2\sin^2\alpha + (1 - 2\sin^2\alpha)}{\sin 2\alpha \cos 2\alpha}$

$p + q = \dfrac{1}{\sin 2\alpha \cos 2\alpha}$

Multiplying and dividing by $2$:
$p + q = \dfrac{2}{2\sin 2\alpha \cos 2\alpha} = \dfrac{2}{\sin 4\alpha}$

$p + q = 2\csc 4\alpha$

Answer: $2\csc 4\alpha$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the three (03) items that follow:
Let $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$ and $q = \cot\alpha - \cot 2\alpha$.

What is $\tan^2\alpha$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $p = \tan 2\alpha - \tan\alpha$

$p = \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha} - \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha \cos\alpha - \cos 2\alpha \sin\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha}$

$p = \dfrac{\sin(2\alpha - \alpha)}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha \cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\tan\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha}$

Also given $q = \cot\alpha - \cot 2\alpha$

$q = \dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha} - \dfrac{\cos 2\alpha}{\sin 2\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha \cos\alpha - \cos 2\alpha \sin\alpha}{\sin 2\alpha \sin\alpha}$

$q = \dfrac{\sin(2\alpha - \alpha)}{\sin 2\alpha \sin\alpha} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\sin 2\alpha \sin\alpha} = \dfrac{1}{\sin 2\alpha}$

Dividing $p$ by $q$, we get:

$\dfrac{p}{q} = \dfrac{\tan\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha} \times \sin 2\alpha = \tan\alpha \tan 2\alpha$

Using the formula $\tan 2\alpha = \dfrac{2\tan\alpha}{1 - \tan^2\alpha}$:

$\dfrac{p}{q} = \tan\alpha \left( \dfrac{2\tan\alpha}{1 - \tan^2\alpha} \right) = \dfrac{2\tan^2\alpha}{1 - \tan^2\alpha}$

$p(1 - \tan^2\alpha) = 2q\tan^2\alpha$

$p - p\tan^2\alpha = 2q\tan^2\alpha$

$p = \tan^2\alpha(p + 2q)$

$\tan^2\alpha = \dfrac{p}{p + 2q}$

Answer: $\dfrac{p}{p+2q}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $2\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha = 2$, where $0 \lt \alpha \lt 90°$.

What is $\tan\alpha$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $2\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha = 2$

Dividing both sides by $\cos\alpha$, we get:

$2\tan\alpha + 1 = 2\sec\alpha$

Squaring both sides:

$(2\tan\alpha + 1)^2 = 4\sec^2\alpha$

$4\tan^2\alpha + 4\tan\alpha + 1 = 4(1 + \tan^2\alpha)$

$4\tan^2\alpha + 4\tan\alpha + 1 = 4 + 4\tan^2\alpha$

$4\tan\alpha = 3$

$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $2\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha = 2$, where $0 \lt \alpha \lt 90°$.

What is $2\sin 2\alpha + \cos 2\alpha$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $2\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha = 2$

$\cos\alpha = 2(1 - \sin\alpha)$

Squaring both sides:

$\cos^2\alpha = 4(1 - \sin\alpha)^2$

$1 - \sin^2\alpha = 4(1 - 2\sin\alpha + \sin^2\alpha)$

$5\sin^2\alpha - 8\sin\alpha + 3 = 0$

$(5\sin\alpha - 3)(\sin\alpha - 1) = 0$

Since $0 \lt \alpha \lt 90^\circ$, $\sin\alpha \neq 1$. Thus, $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

This gives $\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Now, $\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha = 2\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right) = \dfrac{24}{25}$

$\cos 2\alpha = \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha = \left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^2 - \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{7}{25}$

Therefore, $2\sin 2\alpha + \cos 2\alpha = 2\left(\dfrac{24}{25}\right) + \dfrac{7}{25} = \dfrac{48 + 7}{25} = \dfrac{55}{25} = \dfrac{11}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{11}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a triangle $\mathrm{ABC}, \tan \mathrm{A}+\tan \mathrm{B}+\tan \mathrm{C}=k$ What is the value of $\cot A \cot B \cot C$ ?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}, \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C}=\pi$
Taking $\tan$ both side, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \tan (A+B+C)=\tan \pi=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\tan A+\tan B+\tan C-\tan A \tan B \tan C}{1-\tan A \cdot \tan B-\tan B \cdot \tan C-\tan C \cdot \tan A}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \tan A \cdot \tan B \cdot \tan C=\tan A+\tan B+\tan C \\
& \Rightarrow \cot A \cdot \cot B \cdot \cot C=\frac{1}{\tan A+\tan B+\tan C} \\
& =\frac{1}{K}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sin 12^{\circ} \sin 48^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text {  Let } \mathrm{I}=\sin 12^{\circ} \cdot \sin 48^{\circ} \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{2 \sin 12^{\circ} \sin 48^{\circ}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos \left(36^{\circ}\right)-\cos \left(60^{\circ}\right)\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\right]=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{8}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\cos x+\sqrt{3}\sin x$ is maximum when $x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given expression is $f(x) = \cos x + \sqrt{3} \sin x$

Multiplying and dividing by $\sqrt{1^2 + (\sqrt{3})^2} = 2$

$f(x) = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \cos x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin x \right)$

$f(x) = 2 \left( \cos \dfrac{\pi}{3} \cos x + \sin \dfrac{\pi}{3} \sin x \right)$

$f(x) = 2 \cos \left( x - \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)$

The maximum value of $\cos \left( x - \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)$ is $1$, which occurs when $x - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 0$

$x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following numbers:
A. $\tan 22.5^{\circ}$
B. $\cot 22.5^{\circ}$
C. $\tan 22.5^{\circ}-\cot 22.5^{\circ}$
How many of the above are irrational numbers?
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{t}=\tan 22.5^{\circ}=\tan \frac{45^{\circ}}{2}$
Now, $\tan 45^{\circ}=\tan \left(2 \times \frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}=\frac{2 \tan \left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}}{1-\tan ^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 1=\frac{2 t}{1-t^2} \Rightarrow t^2+2 t-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t=\frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4+4}}{2}=-1 \pm \sqrt{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \tan \left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}=-1 \pm \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow \tan \left(\frac{45}{2}\right)^{\circ}=-1+(\sqrt{2})
\end{aligned}\left\{\therefore\right.$ In $\mathrm{I}^{\text {st }}$ quadrant $\tan$ is positive $\}$
(II) Now, $\cot 22.5^{\circ}=\frac{1}{\tan 22.5^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{-1+\sqrt{2}}=1+\sqrt{2}$ which is also an irrational number.
(III) Since, $\tan 22.5^{\circ}-\cot 22.5^{\circ}=-1+\sqrt{2}-(1+\sqrt{2})=-2$ which is not an irrational number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a triangle $ABC$, $\sin A=\cos B+\cos C$ then what is $\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)+\cot\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Given $\sin A = \cos B + \cos C$

Using the half-angle and sum-to-product formulas:

$2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = 2 \cos\left(\dfrac{B+C}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)$

In $\Delta ABC$, $A + B + C = \pi$, so $\dfrac{B+C}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}$.

This yields $\cos\left(\dfrac{B+C}{2}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$.

Substituting this into the equation:

$2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)$

Since $A \in (0, \pi)$, $\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \neq 0$. Dividing both sides by $2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$:

$\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \cos\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)$

Since both $\dfrac{A}{2}$ and $\dfrac{B-C}{2}$ lie in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, we have:

$\dfrac{A}{2} = \pm \dfrac{B-C}{2}$

This implies either $A = B - C$ or $A = C - B$.

If $A = B - C$, then $B = A + C$. Since $A + B + C = \pi$, we get $2B = \pi \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

If $A = C - B$, then $C = A + B$. Since $A + B + C = \pi$, we get $2C = \pi \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Simplifying the required expression:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) + \cot\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)}{\cos\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)} + \dfrac{\cos\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin^2\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) + \cos^2\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{\sin B}$

If $B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the value is $\dfrac{2}{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)} = 2$.

If $C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $B \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, which means $\sin B \lt 1$ and $\dfrac{2}{\sin B} \gt 2$.

Since the given options are constants and the minimum possible value is $2$, the only valid choice among the options is $2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are complementary angles such that $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $m\tan\beta=n\tan\alpha$, then what is $\left(\dfrac{m+n}{m-n}\right)$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Since $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are complementary angles, $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

We are given $\alpha - \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Adding the two equations yields $2\alpha = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Subtracting the two equations yields $2\beta = \dfrac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

From the given relation $m\tan\beta = n\tan\alpha$, we have:

$\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{\tan\alpha}{\tan\beta} = \dfrac{\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}{\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} = 3$

Therefore, $\dfrac{m+n}{m-n} = \dfrac{3+1}{3-1} = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of the $a \cos x+b \sin x+c$ ?
questions.solution:
We know
Maximum value of $a \cos x+b \sin x$ is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$
So Maximum value of $a \cos x+b \sin x+c$ is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}+c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $p \tan \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)=q \tan \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)$, then what is $\frac{(p+q)}{(p-q)}$
equal to? equal to?
questions.solution:
We have.
$\begin{aligned}
& p \tan \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)=q \tan \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{p}{q}=\frac{\tan \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)}{\tan \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)} \\
& =\frac{\sin \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \cos \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)}{\cos \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \sin \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)}
\end{aligned}$
Using componendo and dividendo rule,
$\begin{gathered}
\Rightarrow \frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{\sin \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \cos \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)+\cos \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \sin \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)}{\sin \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \cos \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)-\cos \left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right) \sin \left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{\sin \left[\left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)+\left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)\right]}{\sin \left[\left(\theta+120^{\circ}\right)-\left(\theta-30^{\circ}\right)\right]}=\frac{\sin \left(90^{\circ}+2 \theta\right)}{\sin \left(150^{\circ}\right)} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{\sin \left(90^{\circ}+2 \theta\right)}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}=2 \cos 2 \theta
\end{gathered}$

questions.q: If $A B C$ is a triangle, then what is the value of the determinant $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\cos C & \sin \mathrm{~B} & 0 \\ \tan \mathrm{~A} & 0 & \sin \mathrm{~B} \\ 0 & \tan (\mathrm{~B}+\mathrm{C}) & \cos \mathrm{C}\end{array}\right|$ ?
questions.solution: $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\cos C & \sin B & 0 \\ \tan A & 0 & \sin B \\ 0 & \tan (B+C) & \cos C\end{array}\right|\begin{aligned} & =\cos C[-\sin B \cdot \tan (B+C) \\ & =-\sin B \cdot \cos C\left[\frac{\sin (B+C)}{\cos (B+C)}+\frac{\sin A}{\cos A}\right] \\ & =-\sin B \cdot \cos C\left[\frac{\sin (B+C) \cos A+\sin A \cos (B+C)}{\cos A \cdot \cos (B+C)}\right] \\ & =-\sin B \cdot \cos C \frac{\sin (A+B+C)}{\cos A \cdot \cos (B+C)} \\ & =\frac{-\sin B \cdot \cos C \sin \pi}{\cos A \cdot \cos (B+C)}=0 .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: ABC is a triangle such that angle $\mathrm{C}=60^{\circ}$, then what is $\frac{\cos \mathrm{A}+\cos \mathrm{B}}{\cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}}{2}\right)}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \frac{\cos \mathrm{A}+\cos \mathrm{B}}{\cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}}{2}\right)} & =\frac{2 \cos \frac{\mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{\mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{B}}{2}}{\cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{B}}{2}\right)} \\ & =2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi-\mathrm{C}}{2}\right) \\ & =2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{C}}{2}\right)=2 \sin \frac{\mathrm{C}}{2} \\ & =2 \sin 30^{\circ}=2 \times \frac{1}{2}=1 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(\theta)=\frac{1}{1+\tan \theta}$ and $\alpha+\beta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}$, then what is the value of $f(\alpha) f(\beta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\alpha+\beta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}\begin{aligned} & \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan 5 \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \times \tan \beta}=\tan \left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \times \tan \beta}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \times \tan \beta \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta+\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta=1 \\ & \because f(\theta)=\frac{1}{1+\tan \theta} \\ & f(\alpha) \cdot f(\beta)=\frac{1}{1+\tan \alpha+\tan \beta+\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta}=\frac{1}{1+1}=\frac{1}{2} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \alpha$ and $\tan \beta$ are the roots of the equation $x^2-6 x+8=0$, then what is the value of $\cos (2 \alpha+2 \beta) ?$
questions.solution: $\because \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=6\begin{aligned} \tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta & =8 \\ \tan (\alpha+\beta) & =\frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta} \\ & =\frac{6}{1-8}=\frac{6}{-7} \\ \cos (2 \alpha+2 \beta) & =\cos 2(\alpha+\beta) \\ & =\frac{1-\tan ^2(\alpha+\beta)}{1+\tan ^2(\alpha+\beta)} \\ & =\frac{1-\frac{36}{49}}{1+\frac{36}{49}} \\ & =\frac{13}{85}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\tan 65^{\circ}+2 \tan 45^{\circ}-2 \tan40^{\circ}-\tan 25^{\circ} ?$
questions.solution: $\tan (90-25)^{\circ}+2-2 \tan 40^{\circ}-\tan 25^{\circ}\begin{aligned} & =\cot 25^{\circ}-\tan 25^{\circ}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =\frac{\cos 25^{\circ}}{\sin 25^{\circ}}-\frac{\sin 25^{\circ}}{\cos 25^{\circ}}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =\frac{\cos ^2 25^{\circ}-\sin ^2 25^{\circ}}{\sin 25^{\circ} \cdot \cos 25^{\circ}}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =\frac{\cos 2\left(25^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 25^{\circ} \cdot \cos 25^{\circ}}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =\frac{2 \times \cos 50^{\circ}}{2 \sin 25^{\circ} \cdot \cos 25^{\circ}}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =\frac{2 \cos 50^{\circ}}{\sin 50^{\circ}}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =2 \cot 50^{\circ}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2 \\ & =2 \tan 40^{\circ}-2 \tan 40^{\circ}+2=2 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \alpha=\frac{1}{7}, \sin \beta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} ; 0 \lt \alpha, \beta \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$ then what is the value of $\cos (\alpha+2 \beta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Since, } \cos (\alpha+2 \beta) \\ &=\cos \alpha \cos 2 \beta-\sin \alpha \sin 2 \beta \\ &=\cos \alpha\left(1-2 \sin ^2 \beta\right)-\sin \alpha(2 \sin \beta \cos \beta) \\ &=\frac{7}{\sqrt{50}}\left(1-2 \times \frac{1}{10}\right)-\left(2 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \times \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\right) \frac{1}{\sqrt{50}} \\ &=\frac{7}{\sqrt{50}} \times \frac{8}{10}-\frac{6}{10 \sqrt{50}}=\frac{50}{10 \sqrt{50}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\cos \left(\frac{5 \pi}{17}\right)+\cos \left(\frac{7 \pi}{17}\right)+2 \cos \left(\frac{11 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right) ?$
questions.solution:
Concept:
$\cos C+\cos \mathrm{D}=2 \cos \left(\frac{C+D}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{C-D}{2}\right)$
Calculation:
Given, $\cos \left(\frac{5 \pi}{17}\right)+\cos \left(\frac{7 \pi}{17}\right)+2 \cos \left(\frac{11 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right)$
Using identity (i),
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 2 \cos \left(\frac{\frac{5 \pi}{17}+\frac{7 \pi}{17}}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\frac{5 \pi}{17}-\frac{7 \pi}{17}}{2}\right)+2 \cos \left(\frac{11 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \cos \left(\frac{6 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(-\frac{\pi}{17}\right)+2 \cos \left(\frac{11 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 2\left[\cos \left(\frac{6 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right)+\cos \left(\frac{11 \pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right)\right] \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right)\left[\cos \left(\frac{6 \pi}{17}\right)+\cos \left(\frac{11 \pi}{17}\right)\right]
\end{aligned}$
Again using (i),
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right)\left[2 \cos \left(\frac{\frac{6 \pi}{17}+\frac{11 \pi}{17}}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\frac{6 \pi}{17}-\frac{11 \pi}{17}}{2}\right)\right] \\
& \Rightarrow 4 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{5 \pi}{34}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 4 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{17}\right) \times 0 \times \cos \left(\frac{5 \pi}{34}\right)=0
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\tan \left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}\right)$ ?
questions.solution:
$\because \quad \tan \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-1$
Let $\frac{3 \pi}{4}=\theta \quad \Rightarrow \quad \tan \theta=-1$
Now, $\tan \theta=\frac{2 \tan \theta / 2}{1-\tan ^2 \theta / 2}$
Let $\tan \theta / 2=x\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad-1=\frac{2 x}{1-x^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x^2-2 x-1=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x=1 \pm \sqrt{2} \\
& \therefore \quad \tan \frac{3 \pi}{8}=1+\sqrt{2} \quad\left(\because 0 \lt \frac{3 \pi}{8} \lt \frac{\pi}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 10^{\circ}-\sin 10^{\circ}}{\sin 25^{\circ} \cos 25^{\circ}}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 10^{\circ}-\sin 10^{\circ}}{\sin 25^{\circ} \cdot \cos 25^{\circ}} \\ &=\frac{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \cos 10^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2} \sin 10^{\circ}\right)}{2 \frac{2 \sin 25^{\circ} \cdot \cos 25^{\circ}}{2 \times 2}} \\ &= 4\left(\frac{\sin 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 10^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \sin 10^{\circ}}{\sin 50^{\circ}}\right) \\ &= \frac{4 \cdot \sin \left(60^{\circ}-10^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 50^{\circ}} \\ &= \frac{4 \sin 50^{\circ}}{\sin 50^{\circ}}=4 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\sin 10^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ}+\sin 50^{\circ}$. $\sin 250^{\circ}+\sin 250^{\circ} \cdot \sin 10^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin 10^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ}+ \sin 50^{\circ} \cdot \sin 250^{\circ} \\ &+\sin 250^{\circ} \cdot \sin 10^{\circ}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}+\cos 200^{\circ}\right. \\ & \quad-\cos 300^{\circ}+\cos 240^{\circ}-\cos 260^{\circ} \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\begin{array}{l}\cos 40^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}+\cos (180+20)^{\circ}-\cos (360-60)^{\circ} \\ +\cos (180+60)^{\circ}-\cos (180+80)^{\circ}\end{array}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 40^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}+\cos 80^{\circ}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}+\cos 80^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 40^{\circ}+\cos 80^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \cos \left(\frac{80+40}{2}\right) \times \cos \left(\frac{80-40}{2}\right)-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \times \frac{1}{2} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[-\frac{3}{2}\right]=-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\tan ^2 165^{\circ}+\cot ^2 165^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution:
Concept:
- $\tan \left(180^{\circ}-\theta\right)=-\tan \theta$
- $\cot \left(180^{\circ}-\theta\right)=-\cot \theta$
- $\tan 15^{\circ}=2-\sqrt{3}$
- $\cot 15^{\circ}=2+\sqrt{3}$
Formula used:
$\begin{aligned}
& (a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2 a b \\
& (a-b)^2=a^2+b^2-2 a b
\end{aligned}$
Calculation:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Given, } \tan ^2 165^{\circ}+\cot ^2 165^{\circ} \\
& \Rightarrow\left(\tan (180-15)^{\circ}\right)^2+\left(\cot (180-15)^{\circ}\right)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow\left(-\tan ^2 15^{\circ}\right)+\left(-\cot ^2 15^{\circ}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \tan ^2 15^{\circ}+\cot ^2 15^{\circ} \\
& \Rightarrow(2-\sqrt{3})^2+(2+\sqrt{3})^2 \\
& \Rightarrow(4+3-4 \sqrt{3})+(4+3+4 \sqrt{3}) \\
& \Rightarrow \tan ^2 165^{\circ}+\cot ^2 165^{\circ}=14
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\sec x=\frac{25}{24}$ and $x$ lies in the fourth quadrant, then what is the value of $\tan x+\sin x$ ?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of $\sin \left(2 n \pi+\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right) \sin \left(2 n \pi-\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)$,
where $n \in Z$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin \left(2 n \pi+\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right) \sin \left(2 n \pi-\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right) \\ & =-\sin \frac{5 \pi}{6} \cdot \sin \left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)=-\sin ^2\left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\ & =-\sin ^2 \frac{\pi}{6}=-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
In a triangle $A B C$,
$\sin A-\cos B-\cos C=0$
What is angle $B$ equal to?
questions.solution: In $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}A+B+C=\pi\sin A=\cos B+\cos C=2 \cos \frac{B+C}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{B-C}{2}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \sin A=2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{A}{2}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{B-C}{2}\right) & \\ & {[\because B+C=\pi-A] }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{A}{2}=2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cdot \cos \left(\frac{B-C}{2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos \frac{A}{2}=\cos \left(\frac{B-C}{2}\right)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{A}{2}=\frac{B-C}{2} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{~A}=\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{B} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \pi-\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{B} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad B=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \left(45^{\circ}+\theta\right)=1+\sin 2 \theta$, where $-\frac{\pi}{4} \lt \theta \lt \frac{\pi}{4}$, then what is the value of $\cos 2 \theta$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \tan \left(45^{\circ}+\theta\right)=1+\sin 2 \theta \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\tan 45^{\circ}+\tan \theta}{1-\tan 45^{\circ} \cdot \tan \theta}-1=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1+\tan \theta}{1-\tan \theta}-1=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2 \tan \theta}{1-\tan \theta}=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta} \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \tan \theta\left(1+\tan ^2 \theta\right)=2 \tan \theta(1-\tan \theta) \\ & \Rightarrow \tan ^2 \theta\left[1+\tan ^2 \theta-1+\tan \theta\right]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \tan ^2 \theta(\tan \theta+1)=0 \\ & \therefore \tan \theta=0 \text { or } \tan \theta=-1 \quad \text { (Not possible) }\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \theta=0 \quad\left[\therefore \frac{-\pi}{4} \lt \theta \lt \frac{\pi}{4}\right]$
Now, $\cos 2 \theta=\cos \theta=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $\sin 2 \theta=\cos 3 \theta$, where $\theta$ is acute angle. What is the value of $1+4 \sin \theta$ ?
$\left(\right.$ given that $\left.\sin 18^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\right)$
questions.solution: $\Rightarrow \begin{aligned} & \sin 2 \theta=\cos 3 \theta=\sin \left(90^{\circ}-3 \theta\right) \\ & 2 \theta=90^{\circ}-3 \theta \quad \Rightarrow \quad \theta=18^{\circ} \\ & \text {Now, } 1+4 \sin \theta=1+4 \sin 18^{\circ}\end{aligned}=1+4 \cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}\right)=\sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \theta=-\frac{5}{12}$, then what can be the value of $\sin \theta$ ?
questions.solution:
$\tan \theta=\frac{-5}{12}=\frac{p}{b} ;$ Let $p=5 k \quad b=12 k\therefore \quad \mathrm{h}=\sqrt{p^2+b^2}=\sqrt{25 k^2+144 k^2}=13 k$
Since value of $\tan \theta$ is - ve therefore $\theta$ lies in 2 nd and 3rd quadrant.
$\therefore \quad \sin \theta=\frac{p}{h}= \pm \frac{5}{13}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\cos ^4 \frac{7 \pi}{8}+\cos ^4 \frac{5 \pi}{8}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos ^4 \frac{7 \pi}{8}+\cos ^4 \frac{5 \pi}{8}=\left(\cos ^2 \frac{7 \pi}{8}\right)^2+\left(\cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)^2 \\ = & \left(\cos ^2 \frac{7 \pi}{8}-\cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)^2+2 \cos ^2 \frac{7 \pi}{8} \cdot \cos ^2 \frac{5 \pi}{8} \\ = & {\left[(-1) \sin \left(\frac{7 \pi}{8}+\frac{5 \pi}{8}\right) \sin \left(\frac{7 \pi}{8}-\frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)\right]^2+\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \cos \frac{7 \pi}{8} \cdot \cos \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right]^2 } \\ = & {\left[\sin \frac{3 \pi}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right]^2+\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos \frac{3 \pi}{2}+\cos \frac{\pi}{4}\right]^2 }\end{aligned}=\left[(-1) \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]^2+\frac{1}{2}\left[0+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]^2=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)-\sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)-\sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right) \\ & =\sin \left[\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right] \sin \left[\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta-\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right]\end{aligned}\left[\because \quad \sin ^2 x-\sin ^2 y=\sin (x+y) \cdot \sin (x-y)\right]=\sin \frac{\pi}{2} \cdot \sin 2 \theta=\sin 2 \theta$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $\sin \beta$ be the GM of $\sin \alpha$ and $\cos \alpha ; \tan \gamma$ be the AM of $\sin\alpha$ and $\cos \alpha$
Question: What is the value of of $\sec 2 \gamma$ ?
questions.solution:
$\sec 2 \gamma=\frac{1}{\cos 2 \gamma}=\frac{1+\tan ^2 \gamma}{1-\tan ^2 \gamma}$
Hence $\operatorname{Sec}_2 y \operatorname{stan} \gamma=\frac{\operatorname{Sin} \alpha+\operatorname{Cos} \alpha}{2}=\frac{1+\left(\frac{\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha}{2}\right)^2}{1-\left(\frac{\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha}{2}\right)^2}=\frac{4+(\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha)^2}{4-(\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha)^2}=\frac{4+(1+\sin 2 \alpha)}{4-(1+\sin 2 \alpha)}=\frac{5+\sin 2 \alpha}{3-\sin 2 \alpha}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta$, where then which of the following is one of the values of $(\alpha+\beta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta \\ & \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta}=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ \Rightarrow & \alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $(1+\tan \theta)(1+\tan 9 \theta)=2$, then what is the value of $\tan (10 \theta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because(1+\tan \theta)(1+\tan 9 \theta)=2 \\ \Rightarrow & 1+\tan 9 \theta+\tan \theta+\tan \theta \cdot \tan 9 \theta=2 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan \theta+\tan 9 \theta=1-\tan \theta \cdot \tan 9 \theta \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\tan \theta+\tan 9 \theta}{1-\tan \theta \cdot \tan 9 \theta}=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan (\theta+9 \theta)=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \tan 10 \theta=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\sin 0^{\circ}+\sin 10^{\circ}+\sin 20^{\circ}+\sin 30^{\circ}+\ldots .+\sin 360^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin 0^{\circ}+\sin 10^{\circ}+\sin 20^{\circ}+\sin 30^{\circ}+\ldots .+\sin 360^{\circ} \\ & =\left(\sin 0^{\circ}+\sin 360^{\circ}\right)+\left(\sin 10^{\circ}+\sin 350^{\circ}\right)+\left(\sin 20^{\circ}+\right. \\ & \left.\sin 340^{\circ}\right)+\ldots+\sin 180^{\circ} \\ & =2 \sin 180^{\circ} \cdot \cos 180^{\circ}+2 \sin 180^{\circ} \cdot \cos 170^{\circ}+ \\ & \left.2 \sin 180^{\circ} \cdot \cos 160^{\circ}\right)+\ldots+\sin 180^{\circ} \\ & =0+0+0 \ldots .+0 \quad\left[\because \sin 180^{\circ}=0\right] \\ & =0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{\tan x+\cot x}$, where $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$ ?
questions.solution: $f(x)=\frac{1}{\tan x+\cot x}=\frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} \sin 2 \mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\cos 2 \mathrm{x}=0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-2 \sin 2 \mathrm{x}=-2 \sin \frac{\pi}{4}=-2 \lt 0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \text { is maximum at } \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \therefore \text { Maximum value is } \\ & \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let the equation $\sec x \cdot \operatorname{cosec} x=p$ have a solution, where $p$ is a positive real number. What should be the smallest value of $p$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\sin x \cdot \cos x}=p \Rightarrow 2 \sin x \cdot \cos x=\frac{2}{P} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 x=\frac{2}{P} \\
& \text { since }-1 \leq \sin \leq 1 \text { and } \mathrm{P} \gt 0 \\
& \therefore \frac{2}{P} \geq 1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P} \leq 2
\end{aligned}$
So, smallest value of $P$ is 2 .

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $A B C$ be a triangle. If $\cos 2 A+\cos 2 B+\cos 2 C=-1$ then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \therefore A+B+C=\pi \\ & \Rightarrow C=\pi-(A+B) \\ & \text {Now, } \cos 2 A+\cos 2 B+\cos 2 C=-1 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \cos (A+B) \cdot \cos (A-B)+2 \cos ^2 C-1=-1 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \cos (A+B) \cdot \cos (A-B)+2 \cos ^2(\pi-(A+B))=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \cos (A+B)[\cos (A-B)+\cos (A+B)]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \cos (\pi-C)[2 \cos A \cdot \cos B]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow-4 \cos C \cdot \cos A \cdot \cos B=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \cos A \cdot \cos B \cdot \cos C=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\sin x+\sin y=\cos x+\cos y$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. What is $\tan\left(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{y}{2}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given.
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin x+\sin y=\cos x+\cos y \\
& 2 \sin \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right) \\
& =2 \cos \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$
On dividing $2 \cos \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)$ both side
$\tan \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin (A+B)=1$ and $2 \sin (A-B)=1$, where $0 \lt A, B \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$, then what is $\tan A: \tan B$ equal to?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cot 2 x \cot 4 x-\cot 4 x \cot 6 x-\cot 6 x \cot 2 x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cot (6 x)=\cot (2 x+4 x) \\ & \Rightarrow \cot 6 x=\frac{\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 4 x-1}{\cot 2 x+\cot 4 x}\end{aligned}\therefore \cot 2 x \cdot \cot 6 x+\cot 6 x \cdot \cot 4 x=\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 4 x-1$ or, $\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 4 x-\cot 4 x \cdot \cot 6 x-\cot 6 x \cdot \cot 2 x=1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: 16. If $\tan x=-\frac{3}{4}$ and $x$ is in the second quadrant, then what is the value of $\sin x \cdot \cos x$ ?
questions.solution:
$\tan x=-\frac{3}{4}$ ( Here $90^{\circ} \lt x \lt 180^{\circ}$ )
$\sin x=\frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos x=-\frac{4}{5}$
Now,
$\sin x \cdot \cos x=\frac{3}{5} \cdot\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)=-\frac{12}{25}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of the following? $\tan 31^{\circ} \tan 33^{\circ} \tan 35^{\circ}$ ________ $\tan 57^{\circ} \tan 59^{\circ}$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan 31^{\circ} \cdot \tan 33^{\circ} \cdot \tan 35^{\circ} \ldots \ldots \ldots \tan 55^{\circ} \cdot \tan 57^{\circ} \cdot \tan 59^{\circ} \\ & =\tan 31^{\circ} \cdot \tan 33^{\circ} \cdot \tan 35^{\circ} \ldots \ldots \ldots\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \tan \left(90^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\right) \cdot \tan \left(90^{\circ}-33^{\circ}\right) \cdot \tan \left(90^{\circ}-31^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\tan 31^{\circ} \cdot \tan 33^{\circ} \cdot \tan 35^{\circ} \ldots \ldots \ldots \tan 45^{\circ} \ldots \ldots \ldots . .\end{aligned}\cot 35^{\circ} \cdot \cot 33^{\circ} \cdot \cot 31^{\circ}=1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the range of the function $f(x)=1-\sin x$ defined on entire real line?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(x)=1-\sin x \\ & -1 \mathrm{~d}^{\prime \prime} \sin x \mathrm{~d}^{\prime \prime} 1 \\ & 1 \mathrm{e} \mathrm{e}^{\prime \prime}-\sin x \mathrm{e} "-1 \\ & 2 \mathrm{e} " 1-\sin x \mathrm{e} " 0 \\ & \therefore \text { Range }=[0,2]\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of the following?
$\left(\sin 24^{\circ}+\cos 66^{\circ}\right)\left(\sin 24^{\circ}-\cos 66^{\circ}\right)$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \left(\sin 24^{\circ}+\cos 66^{\circ}\right)\left(\sin 24^{\circ}-\cos 66^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\sin ^2 24^{\circ}-\cos ^2 66^{\circ}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\sin ^2 24^{\circ}-\cos ^2\left(90^{\circ}-24^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\sin ^2 24^{\circ}-\sin ^2 24^{\circ}=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of $3(\sin x-\cos x)+4\left(\cos ^3 x\right.\left.-\sin ^3 x\right) ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } f(x)=3(\sin x-\cos x)+4\left(\cos ^3 x-\sin ^3 x\right) \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=3(\cos x+\sin x)-12 \sin x \cos x(\cos x+\sin x) \\ & =3(\cos x+\sin x)(1-2 \sin 2 x)=0 \\ & \begin{array}{l}\Rightarrow x=\frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{6} \\ f^{\prime \prime}(x)=3(-\sin x+\cos x)(1-2 \sin 2 x) \\ -3(\cos x+\sin x)(-4 \cos 2 x) \\ f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \lt 0 \text { and } f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \gt 0\end{array} \\ & \therefore \quad f(x) \text { is maximum at } x=\frac{3 \pi}{4} \\ & f\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=3\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+4\left(\frac{-1}{2 \sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}\right) \\ & =3 \sqrt{2}-2 \sqrt{2}=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $(1+\cot \theta-\operatorname{cosec} \theta)(1+\tan \theta+\sec \theta)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (1+\cot \theta-\operatorname{cosec} \theta)(1+\tan \theta+\sec \theta) \\ & =\left(\frac{\sin \theta+\cos \theta-1}{\sin \theta}\right)\left(\frac{\sin \theta+\cos \theta+1}{\cos \theta}\right)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2-1^2}{\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-1}{\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta}\end{aligned}=\frac{1+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-1}{\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta}=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\cot ^2 \theta}-\left(\frac{1-\tan \theta}{1-\cot \theta}\right)^2$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\cot ^2 \theta}-\left(\frac{1-\tan \theta}{1-\cot \theta}\right)^2\begin{aligned}& =\frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{\frac{\tan ^2 \theta+1}{\tan ^2 \theta}}-\left(\frac{1-\tan \theta}{\frac{\tan \theta-1}{\tan \theta}}\right)^2 \\& =\tan ^2 \theta-(-\tan \theta)^2=0 .
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $7 \sin \theta+24 \cos \theta=25$, then what is the value of $(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & 7 \sin \theta+24 \cos \theta=25 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{7}{25} \cdot \sin \theta+\frac{24}{25} \cdot \cos \theta=1 \\ & \text {Again, }(7)^2+(24)^2=(25)^2\end{aligned}\therefore$ Let $\frac{7}{25}=\cos \alpha$ and $\frac{24}{25}=\sin \alpha$
Then, $\sin \theta \cdot \cos \alpha+\cos \theta \cdot \sin \alpha=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sin (\theta+\alpha)=\sin \frac{\pi}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \theta+\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)\end{aligned}$
Now, $\sin \theta+\cos \theta=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of the following?
$\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right) \sec \left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)$
questions.solution: $\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right) \cdot \sec \left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)\begin{aligned} & =\operatorname{cosec}\left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \cdot \sec \left(2 \pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ & =-\operatorname{cosec} \frac{\pi}{6} \cdot \sec \frac{\pi}{3}=(-2)(2)=-4\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $3 \cos \theta=4 \sin \theta$, then what is the value of $\tan \left(45^{\circ}+\right.\theta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 3 \cos \theta=4 \sin \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=\frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}\therefore \tan (45+\theta)=\frac{\tan 45^{\circ}+\tan \theta}{1-\tan 45^{\circ} \cdot \tan \theta}=\frac{1+\frac{3}{4}}{1-\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{7}{1}=7$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ and $2 \tan \alpha=1$, then what is $\tan 2 \beta$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \because \quad 2 \tan \alpha=1 \quad \Rightarrow 2 \tan \alpha=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \alpha+\beta=\frac{\pi}{4} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta}=1\Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \frac{1}{2}+\tan \beta=1-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \tan \beta \\ \Rightarrow & 1+2 \tan \beta=2-\tan \beta \\ & \tan \beta=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$
Now, $\tan 2 \beta=\frac{2 \tan \beta}{1-\tan ^2 \beta}=\frac{2 \times \frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{9}}=\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{8}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan A=\frac{1}{7}$, then what is $\cos 2 A$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\tan A=\frac{1}{7}, \cos 2 A=\frac{1-\tan ^2 A}{1+\tan ^2 A}=\frac{1-\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)^2}{1+\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)^2}=\frac{24}{25}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of $\sin 2 x \cdot \cos 2 x ?$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & y=\sin 2 x \cdot \cos 2 x \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d}{d x}(\sin 2 x) \cdot \cos 2 x+\frac{d}{d x}(\cos 2 x) \cdot \sin 2 x\end{aligned}=\cos ^2 2 x-\sin ^2 2 x=\cos 4 x$
For maximum or minimum value
$\frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \cos 4 x=0\therefore 4 x=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}$
Now, $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=-4 \cdot \sin 4 x$
At $x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}, \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=-4 \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{2}=-4$.
$\therefore y$ is max. at $x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\begin{aligned} y_{\max } & =\sin 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\right) \cdot \cos 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\right) \\ & =\sin \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is value of $\cot ^2 15^{\circ}+\tan ^2 15^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cot ^2 15^{\circ}+\tan ^2 15^{\circ} \\ & =\operatorname{cosec}^2 15^{\circ}-1+\sec ^2 15^{\circ}-1 \\ & =\operatorname{cosec}^2 15^{\circ}+\sec ^2 15^{\circ}-2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{\sin ^2 15^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\cos ^2 15^{\circ}}-2 \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 15^{\circ}+\cos ^2 15^{\circ}}{\frac{1}{4}\left(4 \sin ^2 15^{\circ} \cdot \cos ^2 15^{\circ}\right)}-2 \\ & =\frac{4}{\sin ^2 30^{\circ}}-2=\frac{4}{\frac{1}{4}}-2=16-2=14\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer that follow: Let $a \sin ^2 x+b \cos ^2 x=c ; b \sin ^2 y+a \cos ^2 y=d$ and $p \tan x=q \tan y$.
Question: What is $\tan ^2 x$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { From } a \sin ^2 x+b \cos ^2 x=c \\
& a \sin ^2 x+b \cos ^2 x=c\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) \\
& (a-c) \sin ^2 x=(c-b) \cos ^2 x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\sin ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x}=\frac{(c-b)}{(a-c)} \\
& \Rightarrow \tan ^2 x=\frac{(c-b)}{(a-c)}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
