Question: What is $\frac{p^2}{q^2}$ equal to?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer Let $t_n=\sin ^n \theta+\cos ^n \theta$.
Question: What is $\frac{t_3-t_5}{t_5-t_7}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$t_n=\sin ^n \theta+\cos ^n \theta$
Now, $\frac{t_3-t_5}{t_5-t_7}=\frac{\sin ^3 \theta+\cos ^3 \theta-\sin ^5 \theta-\cos ^5 \theta}{\sin ^5 \theta+\cos ^5 \theta-\sin ^7 \theta-\cos ^7 \theta}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\sin ^3 \theta\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right)+\cos ^3 \theta\left(1-\cos ^2 \theta\right)}{\sin ^5 \theta\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right)+\cos ^7 \theta\left(1-\cos ^2 \theta\right)} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^3 \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta+\cos ^3 \theta \cdot \sin ^2 \theta}{\sin ^5 \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta+\cos ^7 \theta \cdot \sin ^2 \theta}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\sin ^2 \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)}{\sin ^2 \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta\left(\sin ^3 \theta+\cos ^3 \theta\right)} \\ & =\frac{(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)}{\left(\sin ^3 \theta+\cos ^3 \theta\right)}=\frac{t_1}{t_3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: Let $\alpha=\beta=15^{\circ}$.
Question: What is the value of $\sin 7 \alpha-\cos 7 \beta$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin 7 \alpha-\cos 7 \beta \\ = & \sin 7\left(15^{\circ}\right)-\cos 7\left(15^{\circ}\right)=\sin \left(105^{\circ}\right)-\cos \left(105^{\circ}\right) \\ = & \sin \left(90^{\circ}+15^{\circ}\right)-\cos \left(90^{\circ}+15^{\circ}\right)\end{aligned}=\cos 15^{\circ}-\left(-\sin \left(15^{\circ}\right)\right)=\cos 15^{\circ}+\sin 15^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin x+\sin y=\cos y-\cos x$, where $0 \lt y \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$, then what is $\tan \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\sin x+\sin y=\cos y-\cos x\frac{\sin x+\sin y}{\cos y-\cos x}=1\frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)}{2 \sin \left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) \cdot \sin \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)}=1\cot \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)=1 \Rightarrow \tan \left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: Let $\alpha=\beta=15^{\circ}$.
Question: What is $\sin \left(\alpha+1^{\circ}\right)+\cos \left(\beta+1^{\circ}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\sin \left(\alpha+1^{\circ}\right)+\cos \left(\beta+1^{\circ}\right)=\sqrt{2}\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sin \left(\alpha+1^{\circ}\right)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \cos \left(\beta+1^{\circ}\right)\right\}\begin{aligned}=\sqrt{2}\left\{\cos 45^{\circ} \cdot \sin (\alpha+1)+\sin 45^{\circ} \cdot \cos (\alpha+1)\right\} & \\ & (\because \alpha=\beta)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{2}\left\{\sin \left(\alpha+1+45^{\circ}\right)\right\}=\sqrt{2} \cdot \sin \left(15^{\circ}+1^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\sqrt{2} \cdot \sin 61^{\circ} (i)
\end{aligned}$
Again
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\sqrt{3} \cdot \cos 1^{\circ}+\sin 1^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \cos 1^{\circ}+\frac{1}{2} \sin 1^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\sqrt{2} \cdot\left(\sin 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 1^{\circ}+\cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \sin 1^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left(\sin 61^{\circ}\right) (ii) \\ 
& \text { Thus }(\text { i })=(\text { ii })
\end{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\sqrt{3} \cdot \cos 1^{\circ}+\sin 1^{\circ}\right)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: Let $\frac{\tan 3 A}{\tan A}=K$, where $\tan A \neq 0$ and $K \neq \frac{1}{3}$.
Question: What is $\tan ^2 A$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  \frac{\tan 3 A}{\tan A}=K \\
& \frac{3 \tan A-\tan ^3 A}{\tan A \cdot\left(1-3 \tan ^2 A\right)}=K \\
& \frac{\left(3-\tan ^2 A\right)}{\left(1-3 \tan ^2 A\right)}=K
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3-\tan ^2 A=K-3 K \tan ^2 A \\ & (3 K-1) \tan ^2 A=K-3 \Rightarrow \tan ^2 A=\frac{K-3}{(3 K-1)}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: Let $\frac{\tan 3 A}{\tan A}=K$, where $\tan A \neq 0$ and $K \neq \frac{1}{3}$.
Question: For real values of $\tan A, K$ cannot lie between
questions.solution:
$\tan A=\sqrt{\frac{(K-3)}{(3 K-1)}}$
For real value of $\tan A,\left(\frac{K-3}{3 K-1}\right) \gt 0$.
$\therefore$ For, $\frac{1}{3} \lt K \lt 3$.
$\tan \mathrm{A}$ is not real.
Also, for $\frac{1}{2} \lt \mathrm{k} \lt 2$, $\tan \mathrm{A}$ is not real.

questions.subject: Mathematics

Paragraph: Read the following information and answer Let $t_n=\sin ^n \theta+\cos ^n \theta$.
Question: What is the value of $t_{10}$ where $\theta=45^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution:
$t_{10}=\sin ^{10}(\theta)+\cos ^{10}(\theta)$
When $\theta=45^{\circ}$,
$t_{10}=\sin ^{10}\left(45^{\circ}\right)+\cos ^{10}\left(45^{\circ}\right)\begin{aligned} & =\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{10}+\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{10}=2 \cdot\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{10} \\ & =2 \times \frac{1}{32}=\frac{1}{16}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \theta=\frac{\cos 17^{\circ}-\sin 17^{\circ}}{\cos 17^{\circ}+\sin 17^{\circ}}$, then what is the value of $\theta$ ?
questions.solution: $\tan \theta=\frac{\cos 17^{\circ}-\sin 17^{\circ}}{\cos 17^{\circ}+\sin 17^{\circ}}=\frac{1-\frac{\sin 17^{\circ}}{\cos 17^{\circ}}}{1+\frac{\sin 17^{\circ}}{\cos 17^{\circ}}}=\frac{1-\tan 17^{\circ}}{1+\tan 17^{\circ}}\begin{aligned} & \tan \theta=\frac{\tan 45^{\circ}-\tan 17^{\circ}}{1+\tan 45^{\circ} \cdot \tan 17^{\circ}} \\ & \tan \theta=\tan \left(45^{\circ}-17^{\circ}\right) \\ & \tan \theta=\tan \left(28^{\circ}\right) \Rightarrow \theta=28^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: $A B C D$ is a trapezium such that $A B$ and $C D$ are parallel and $B C$ is perpendicular to them. Let $\angle A D B=\theta, \angle A B D=\alpha, B C=p$ and $C D=q$ and $C D=q$.
Question: What is $A B$ equal to?
questions.solution:
From $\triangle A B D$,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{A B}{\sin \theta}=\frac{B D}{\sin \left(180^{\circ}-(\alpha+\theta)\right)} \\
& \Rightarrow A B=\frac{B D \cdot \sin \theta}{\sin (\alpha+\theta)}=\frac{B D \cdot \sin \theta}{\sin \alpha \cdot \cos \theta+\cos \alpha \cdot \sin \theta}
\end{aligned}$
Again from $\triangle B C D$,
$\begin{aligned} & B D=\sqrt{(B C)^2+(C D)^2}=\sqrt{p^2+q^2} \\ & \sin \alpha=\frac{B C}{B D}=\frac{p}{\sqrt{p^2+q^2}} \\ & \cos \alpha=\frac{C D}{B D}=\frac{q}{\sqrt{p^2+q^2}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore A B & =\frac{\sqrt{p^2+q^2} \cdot \sin \theta}{\frac{p \cdot \cos \theta}{\sqrt{p^2+q^2}}+\frac{q \cdot \sin \theta}{\sqrt{p^2+q^2}}} \\ & =\frac{\left(p^2+q^2\right) \cdot \sin \theta}{p \cdot \cos \theta+q \cdot \sin \theta}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer Let $t_n=\sin ^n \theta+\cos ^n \theta$.
Question: What is $t_1^2-t_2$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & t_1^2-t_2=(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2-\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ = & \sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ = & 1+\sin 2 \theta-1=\sin 2 \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $A$ and $B$ are positive acute angles such that $\cos 2 B=3 \sin ^2 A$ and $3 \sin 2 A=2 \sin 2 B$. What is the value of $(A+2 B)$ ?
questions.solution:
From question, we have
$\cos 2 B=3 \sin ^2 A \text { and } 3 \sin 2 A=2 \sin 2 B$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos (A+2 B)=\cos A \cdot \cos 2 B-\sin A \cdot \sin 2 B \\
& =\cos A \cdot 3 \sin ^2 A-\sin A \cdot \frac{3}{2} \sin 2 A
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =3 \cos A \cdot \sin ^2 A-\frac{3}{2} \cdot \sin A \cdot(2 \sin A-\cos A) \\ & =3 \cos A \cdot \sin ^2 A-3 \cos A \cdot \sin ^2 A=0 \\ & \therefore \cos (A+2 B)=\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\ & \therefore A+2 B=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: Let $\alpha=\beta=15^{\circ}$.
Question: What is the value of $\sin \alpha+\cos \beta$ ?
questions.solution:
$\alpha=\beta=15^{\circ}$  (given)
Now, $\sin \alpha+\cos \beta\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{2} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sin \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \cos \alpha\right) \quad\{\because \alpha=\beta\} \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left(\sin \alpha \cdot \cos 45^{\circ}+\cos \alpha \cdot \sin 45^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left(\sin \left(\alpha+45^{\circ}\right)\right)=\sqrt{2} \cdot \sin \left(15^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\sqrt{2} \cdot \sin 60^{\circ}=\sqrt{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$

Range of $\cos x=[-1,1]\begin{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $8 \cos 10^{\circ} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ} \cdot \cos 40^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 8 \cdot \cos 10^{\circ} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ} \cdot \cos 40^{\circ} \\ &= \frac{4}{\sin 10^{\circ}}\left[2 \cdot \cos 10^{\circ} \cdot \sin 10^{\circ}\right] \cdot \cos 20^{\circ} \cdot \cos 40^{\circ} \\ &= \frac{4}{\sin 10^{\circ}}\left[\sin 20^{\circ}\right] \cdot \cos 20^{\circ} \cdot \cos 40^{\circ} \\ &= \frac{2}{\sin 10^{\circ}}\left[2 \sin 20^{\circ} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ}\right] \cdot \cos 40^{\circ}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{2}{\sin 10^{\circ}}\left[\sin 40^{\circ} \cdot j 0 \cos 40^{\circ}\right. \\ & =\frac{1}{\sin 10^{\circ}}\left[2 \sin 40^{\circ} \cdot \cos 40^{\circ}\right]=\frac{\sin 80^{\circ}}{\sin 10^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{\sin \left(90^{\circ}-10^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 10^{\circ}}=\frac{\cos 10^{\circ}}{\sin 10^{\circ}}=\cot 10^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$y=\sin x \cdot \cos x=\frac{2 \sin x \cdot \cos x}{2}=\frac{\sin 2 x}{2}$
Now, maximum value of $\sin 2 x=1$.
$\therefore y_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} \text {. }$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\operatorname{cosec} \theta=\frac{29}{21}$ where $0 \lt \theta \lt 90^{\circ}$, then what is the value of $4 \sec \theta+4 \tan \theta$ ?
questions.solution:
Given: $\operatorname{cosec} \theta=\frac{29}{21}=\frac{H}{P}\because$ we have Pythagorean triplet of $(20,21,29)\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad P=21 \\
& B=20 \\
& H=29
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore 4(\sec \theta+\tan \theta)=4\left(\frac{29}{21}+\frac{21}{20}\right) \\ & \approx \frac{200}{20}=10\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. $\cos \theta+\sec \theta$ can never be equal to 1.5 .
2. $\tan \theta+\cot \theta$ can never be less than 2 .
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { (i) } \cos \theta+\sec \theta=\frac{3}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1+\cos ^2 \theta}{\cos \theta}=\frac{3}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \cos ^2 \theta-3 \cos \theta+2=0
\end{aligned}$
here discriminant is negative
$\therefore$ No real roots
$\therefore$ No solution.
(ii) In second quadrant both $\tan \theta$ and $\cot \theta$ are negative
$\therefore$ In second quadrant value is less than 2 .
So only statement 1 is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the minimum value of $3 \cos \left(A+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ where $A \in R$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $y=3 \cdot \cos \left(A+\frac{\pi}{3}\right), y^{\prime}=-3 \cdot \sin \left(A+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$
For extremum value, $y^{\prime}=0\begin{aligned}
& \sin \left(A+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0 \Rightarrow A+\frac{\pi}{3}=0 \Rightarrow A=-\frac{\pi}{3} \\
& y^{\prime \prime}=-3 \cdot \cos \left(A+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\
& \quad=-3 \cos \left(-\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-3 \cos (0)=-3
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sin (\alpha+\beta)-2 \sin \alpha \cos \beta+\sin (\alpha-\beta)$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$\sin (\alpha+\beta)-2 \sin \alpha \cos \beta+\sin (\alpha-\beta)$ by applying formula
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin C+\sin D=2 \sin \left(\frac{C+D}{2}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{C-D}{2}\right) \\
& =2 \sin \alpha \cdot \cos \beta-2 \sin \alpha \cdot \cos \beta \\
& =0
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \mathrm{A}-\tan \mathrm{B}=x$ and $\cot \mathrm{B}-\cot \mathrm{A}=y$, then what is the value of $\cot (A-B)$ ?
questions.solution:
Given:
$\begin{aligned}
& \tan A-\tan B=x \\
& \text { and } \cot B-\cot A=y \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\tan A-\tan B}{\tan A \cdot \tan B}=y \\
& \Rightarrow \tan A \cdot \tan B=\frac{x}{y} \\
& \text { for } \cot (A-B), \\
& \cot (A-B)=\frac{1+\tan A \tan B}{\tan A-\tan B} \\
& =\frac{1+\frac{x}{y}}{x}=\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If angle $C$ of a triangle $A B C$ is a right angle, then what is $\tan \mathrm{A}+\tan \mathrm{B}$ equal to?
questions.solution: we have $c^2=a^2+b^2\begin{aligned} & \tan A+\tan B=\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{a} \\ & =\frac{a^2+b^2}{a b}=\frac{c^2}{a b} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cot \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)-\tan \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  \cot \frac{A}{2}-\tan \frac{A}{2} \\
& =\frac{\cos \frac{A}{2}}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}-\frac{\sin \frac{A}{2}}{\cos \frac{A}{2}} \\
& =\frac{\cos ^2 \frac{A}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{A}{2}}{\sin \frac{A}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{A}{2}} \times \frac{2}{2} \\
& =2 \cdot \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}=2 \cot A
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cos 80^{\circ}+\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \because \cos C+\cos D \\ & =2 \cos \left(\frac{C+D}{2}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{C-D}{2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \cos 80^{\circ}+\cos 40^{\circ} \\ & =2 \cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ} \\ & =2 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ}=\cos 20^{\circ} \\ & \therefore \quad \cos 80^{\circ}+\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cot \mathrm{A}+\operatorname{cosec} \mathrm{A}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \cot A+\operatorname{cosec} A \\ & =\frac{\cos A}{\sin A}+\frac{1}{\sin A}=\frac{1+\cos A}{\sin A} \\ & =\frac{2 \cos ^2 \frac{A}{2}}{2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{A}{2}}=\cot \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\tan 25^{\circ} \tan 15^{\circ}+\tan 15^{\circ} \tan 50^{\circ}+\tan 25^{\circ} \tan 50^{\circ}$ equal to?

$\begin{aligned}

& =\tan 15^{\circ}\left(\tan 15^{\circ}+\tan 50^{\circ}\right)+\tan 50^{\circ} \cdot \tan 25^{\circ} \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of
$\frac{\sin 34^{\circ} \cos 236^{\circ}-\sin 56^{\circ} \sin 124^{\circ}}{\cos 28^{\circ} \cos 88^{\circ}+\cos 178^{\circ} \sin 208^{\circ}} ?$
questions.solution: $\frac{\sin 34^{\circ} \cos 236^{\circ}-\sin 56^{\circ} \sin 124^{\circ}}{\cos 28^{\circ} \cos 88^{\circ}+\cos 178^{\circ} \sin 208^{\circ}}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\sin 34^{\circ}\left(-\cos 56^{\circ}\right)-\sin 56^{\circ} \cos 34^{\circ}}{\cos 28^{\circ} \sin 2^{\circ}+\cos 2^{\circ} \sin 28^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{-\sin 34^{\circ} \cos 56^{\circ}-\sin 56^{\circ} \cos 34^{\circ}}{\sin \left(28^{\circ}+2^{\circ}\right)}\end{aligned}=-\frac{\sin \left(34^{\circ}+56^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 30^{\circ}}=\frac{-\sin 90^{\circ}}{\sin 30^{\circ}}=\frac{-1}{\frac{1}{2}}=-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph:
If $\mathrm{p}=\mathrm{X} \cos \theta-\mathrm{Y} \sin \theta, \mathrm{q}=X \sin \theta+\mathrm{Y} \cos \theta$ and $\mathrm{p}^2+4 \mathrm{pq}+\mathrm{q}^2=A X^2+B Y^2, 0 \leq 0 \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$
Question:What is the value of 0?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{x} \cos \theta-\mathrm{y} \sin \theta \\ & \mathrm{q}=\mathrm{x} \sin \theta+\mathrm{y} \cos \theta \\ & \text {Given, } \mathrm{p}^2+4 p q+\mathrm{q}^2=A x^2+B y^2\end{aligned}$
Let us take $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$\begin{aligned} & p=x \cos \frac{\pi}{4}-y \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{x-y}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & q=x \sin \frac{\pi}{4}+y \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{x+y}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & p q=\frac{x^2-y^2}{2} \Rightarrow 2 p q=x^2-y^2\end{aligned}\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{pq}=2 \mathrm{x}^2-2 \mathrm{y}^2$...(1)
Now, $p^2+q^2=x^2 \cos ^2 \theta+y^2 \sin ^2 \theta-2 x y \cos \theta \sin \theta+x^2 \sin ^2 \theta+y^2 \cos ^2 \theta+2 x y \sin \theta \cos \theta=x^2+y^2$...(2)
From (1), (2), $\begin{aligned} p^2+q^2+4 p q & =x^2+y^2+2 x^2-2 y^2 \\ & =3 x^2-y^2\end{aligned}$
Comparing this with the given form, we get $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}, A=3, B=-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph:It is given that $\cos (\theta-\alpha)=a, \cos (\theta-\beta)=b$
Question:What is $\cos (\alpha-\beta)$ equal to?
questions.solution: Given, $\cos (\theta-\alpha)=\mathrm{a} \Rightarrow \sin (\theta-\alpha)=\sqrt{1-a^2}\begin{aligned} & \cos (\theta-\beta)=\mathrm{b} \Rightarrow \sin (\theta-\beta)=\sqrt{1-b^2} \\ & \therefore \cos (\alpha-\beta)=\cos (\theta-\beta-(\theta-\alpha)) \\ & =\cos (\theta-\beta) \cos (\theta-\alpha)+\sin (\theta-\beta) \sin (\theta-\alpha) \\ & \quad=(b)(a)+\sqrt{1-b^2} \sqrt{1-a^2} \\ & \quad=a b+\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Paragraph:It is given that $\cos (\theta-\alpha)=a, \cos (\theta-\beta)=b$
Question:What is $\sin ^2(\alpha-\beta)+2 a b \cos (\alpha-\beta)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\sin ^2(\alpha-\beta)+2 \mathrm{ab} \cos (\alpha-\beta)=1-\cos ^2(\alpha-\beta)+2 \mathrm{ab}\begin{aligned} & \cos (\alpha-\beta)=1-\cos (\alpha-\beta)[\cos (\alpha-\beta)-2 \mathrm{ab}] \\ & \quad= 1-\left(a b+\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}\right)\left[a b+\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}-2 a b\right] \\ &= 1-\left(\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}+a b\right)\left(\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}-a b\right) \\ &= 1-\left[\left(\sqrt{1-a^2} \sqrt{1-b^2}\right)^2-(a b)^2\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =1-\left[\left(1-a^2\right)\left(1-b^2\right)-a^2 b^2\right) \\ & =1-\left(1-b^2-a^2+a^2 b^2-a^2 b^2\right) \\ & =1-1+b^2+a^2=a^2+b^2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \theta=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\tan \varphi=\frac{1}{3}$, then what is the value of $(\theta+\varphi)$ ?
questions.solution: $\tan \theta=\frac{1}{2}\begin{aligned} & \tan \phi=\frac{1}{3} \\ & \tan (\theta+\phi)=\frac{\tan \theta+\tan \phi}{1-\tan \theta \tan \phi} \\ & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}}{1-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)}=\frac{\frac{5}{6}}{\frac{5}{6}}=1 \\ & \therefore \theta+\phi=\tan ^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\cos 48^{\circ}-\cos 12^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos 48^{\circ}-\cos 12^{\circ} \\ = & 2 \cdot \sin \left(\frac{48^{\circ}+12^{\circ}}{2}\right) \cdot \sin \left(\frac{12^{\circ}-48^{\circ}}{2}\right) \\ = & 2 \cdot \sin 30^{\circ} \cdot \sin \left(-18^{\circ}\right)=-\sin 18^{\circ} \\ = & -\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\right)=\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{4}\right) .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos A=\frac{3}{4}$, then what is the value of $\sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{3 A}{2}\right)$ ?
questions.solution: $\cos A=\frac{3}{4}\begin{aligned} & \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \cdot \sin \left(\frac{3 A}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{3 A}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos \left(\frac{3 A}{2}-\frac{A}{2}\right)-\cos \left(\frac{3 A}{2}+\frac{A}{2}\right)\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}[\cos A-\cos 2 A]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos A-\left(2 \cos ^2 A-1\right)\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos A-2 \cos ^2 A+1\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)-2\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2+1\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3}{4}-\frac{18}{16}+1\right]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{12-18+16}{16}\right]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{10}{16}\right]=\frac{5}{16}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin 2 \theta=\cos 3 \theta$, where $0 \lt \theta \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$, then what is $\sin \theta$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\sin 2 \theta=\cos 3 \theta\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta=\sin \left(90^{\circ}-3 \theta\right) \\ & 2 \theta=90^{\circ}-3 \theta \\ & \Rightarrow 5 \theta=90^{\circ} \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=18^{\circ} \\ & \therefore \sin \theta=\sin 18^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $2 \tan \mathrm{~A}-3 \tan \mathrm{~B}-1$, then what is $\tan (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text {  Given : } 2 \tan A=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \tan A=\frac{1}{2} \text { and } \tan B=\frac{1}{3} \\ & \because \tan (A-B)=\frac{\tan A-\tan B}{1+\tan \cdot A \tan B} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan (A-B)=\frac{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}}{1+\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{3}}=\frac{\frac{1}{6}}{\frac{7}{6}}=\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $(1+\tan \alpha \tan \beta)^2+(\tan \alpha-\tan \beta)^2-\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta$ equal to
questions.solution: $(1+\tan \alpha \tan \beta)^2+(\tan \alpha-\tan \beta)^2-\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta\begin{aligned} & =1+\tan ^2 \alpha \tan ^2 \beta+2 \tan \alpha \tan \beta+\tan ^2 \alpha+\tan ^2 \beta \\ & \qquad-2 \tan \alpha \tan \beta-\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta \\ & =1+\tan ^2 \alpha \tan ^2 \beta+\tan ^2 \alpha+\tan ^2 \beta-\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta \\ & =\left(1+\tan ^2 \alpha\right)\left(1+\tan ^2 \beta\right)-\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta \\ & =\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta-\sec ^2 \alpha \sec ^2 \beta \\ & =0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $p=\operatorname{cosec} \theta-\cot \theta$ and $q=(\operatorname{cosec} \theta+\cot \theta)^{-1}$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{p}=\operatorname{cosec} \theta-\cot \theta\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{q}=(\operatorname{cosec} \theta+\cot \theta)^{-1} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{q}=\operatorname{cosec} \theta+\cot \theta\end{aligned}$
We know, $\operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta-\cot ^2 \theta=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(\operatorname{cosec} \theta+\cot \theta)(\operatorname{cosec} \theta-\cot \theta)=1 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{1}{q}\right)(p)=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{q}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \theta+\cos \theta=\sqrt{2} \cos \theta$, then what is $(\cos \theta-\sin \theta)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\sin \theta+\cos \theta=\sqrt{2} \cos \theta$...(1)
Let $\cos \theta-\sin \theta=P$...(2)
$\begin{aligned} & (1)^2+(2)^2 \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cos \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+\sin ^2 \theta- \\ & 2 \sin \theta \cos \theta=2 \cos ^2 \theta+\mathrm{p}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 2=2 \cos ^2 \theta+\mathrm{p}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{p}^2=2\left(1-\cos ^2 \theta\right)=2 \sin ^2 \theta \\ & \Rightarrow p=\sqrt{2} \sin \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{\sec ^2 \theta} \\ & =2 \tan \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta \\ & =2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta=\sin 2 \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sec (\theta-\alpha), \sec \theta$ and $\sec (\theta+\alpha)$ are in AP, where $\cos\alpha \neq 1$, then what is the value of $\sin ^2 \theta+\cos \alpha$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \frac{2}{\cos \theta}=\frac{\cos (\theta+\alpha)+\cos (\theta-\alpha)}{\cos (\theta+\alpha) \cos (\theta-\alpha)}=\frac{2 \cos \theta \cdot \cos \alpha}{\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \alpha} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta \cos \alpha=\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \alpha=\cos ^2 \theta(1-\cos \alpha) \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{\sin ^2 \alpha}{1-\cos \alpha}=1+\cos \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow 1-\sin ^2 \theta=1+\cos \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta+\cos \alpha=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C}=180^{\circ}$, then what is $\sin 2 \mathrm{~A}-\sin 2 \mathrm{~B}-\sin 2 \mathrm{C}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \sin 2 A-\sin 2 B-\sin 2 C \\ & =2 \cos (A+B) \cdot \sin (A-B)+\sin (2 A+2 B) \\ & =2 \cos (A+B) \sin (A-B)+2 \sin (A+B) \cos (A+B) \\ & =2 \cos (A+B)[\sin (A-B)+\sin (A+B)] \\ & =-2 \cos C 2 \sin A \cdot \cos B] \\ & =-4 \sin A \cos B \cos C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\theta=\frac{\pi}{8}$, then what is the value of $(2 \cos \theta+1)^{10}(2 \cos 2 \theta-1)^{10}(2 \cos \theta-1)^{10}(2 \cos 4 \theta-1)^{10}$ ?
questions.solution:
$[(2 \cos \theta+1)(2 \cos \theta-1)]^{10}[2 \cos 2 \theta-1]^{10}[2 \cos 4 \theta-1]^{10}$
when, $\theta=\frac{\pi}{8}$ (given)
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(4 \cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{8}-1\right)^{10}\left(2 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-1\right)^{10}(-1)^{10} \\
& =\left(4 \times \frac{2+\sqrt{2}}{4}-1\right)^{10}(\sqrt{2}-1)^{10} \\
& =[(\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{2}-1)]^{10}=1^{10}=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A=\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta$, the for all real $\theta$, which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
A & =\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta \\
& =\sin ^2 \theta+\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right)^2 \\
& =1+\sin ^4 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta \\
& =1-\sin ^2 \theta\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right) \\
& =1-\sin ^2 \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta \\
& =\frac{4-4 \sin ^2 \theta \cdot \cos ^2 \theta}{4}=\frac{4-\sin ^2(2 \theta)}{4}
\end{aligned}$
As, we know, $0 \leq \sin ^2 2 \theta \leq 1\therefore \quad \mathrm{A}=\frac{4-0}{4} \text { or } \frac{4-1}{4} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{4} \leq \mathrm{A} \leq 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}, \sin y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$, where $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{2}, 0 \lt y \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$ then what is $(x+y)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}, \sin y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}, 0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{2}, 0 \lt y \lt \frac{\pi}{2} \\ & \because \cos x=\sqrt{1-\sin ^2 x} \quad \& \cos y=\sqrt{1-\sin ^2 y} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos x=\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{5}} \quad \& \quad \cos y=\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{10}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \cos x=\sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \quad \& \cos y=\sqrt{\frac{9}{10}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ & \sin (x+y)=\sin x \cos y+\cos x \sin y \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \cdot \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{10}}=\frac{\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{10}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{10}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \therefore \quad x+y=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sin 105^{\circ}+\cos 105^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{Sin} 105^{\circ}+\cos 105^{\circ} \\ & =\sin \left(60^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right)+\cos \left(60^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\left(\sin 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 45^{\circ}+\cos 60^{\circ} \sin 45^{\circ}\right)+\left(\cos 60^{\circ} \cos 45^{\circ}\right. \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & =\frac{2}{2 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{\sin 5 x-\sin 3 x}{\cos 5 x+\cos 3 x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sin 5 x-\sin 3 x}{\cos 5 x+\cos 3 x} \\ & \sin c-\sin d=2 \cos \left(\frac{c+d}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{c-d}{2}\right) \\ & \cos c-\cos d=2 \cos \left(\frac{c+d}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{c-d}{2}\right) \\ & \therefore \frac{\sin 5 x-\sin 3 x}{\cos 5 x+\cos 3 x}=\frac{2 \cos \left(\frac{5 x+3 x}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{5 x-3 x}{2}\right)}{2 \cos \left(\frac{5 x+3 x}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{5 x-3 x}{2}\right)} \\ & =\frac{\sin \left(\frac{2 x}{2}\right)}{\cos \left(\frac{2 x}{2}\right)}=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\tan x\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $\sin \beta$ is the harmonic mean of $\sin \alpha$ and $\cos \alpha$, and $\sin \theta$ is the arithmetic mean of $\sin \alpha$ and $\cos \alpha$, then which of the following is/are correct?
1. $\sqrt{2} \sin \left(\alpha+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \sin \beta=\sin 2 \alpha$
2. $\sqrt{2} \sin \theta=\cos \left(\alpha-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
  
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
From question, $\sin \alpha, \sin \beta$ and $\cos \alpha$ are in H.P.
then, $\sin \beta=\frac{2 \sin \alpha \cos \alpha}{\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha}$ and $\sin \alpha, \sin \theta$ and $\cos \alpha$ are in A.P. then, $2 \sin \theta=\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha$
Statement 1: $\sqrt{2} \sin \left(\alpha+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \cdot \sin \beta\begin{aligned}
& =(\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha) \cdot \frac{2 \sin \alpha \cos \alpha}{\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha} \\
& =2 \sin \alpha \cos \alpha=\sin 2 \alpha
\end{aligned}$
Statement 2: $\cos \left(\alpha-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha)=\frac{2 \sin \theta}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2} \sin \theta$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\tan 54^{\circ}$ can be expressed as
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \tan 54^{\circ}=\tan \left(45^{\circ}+9^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\frac{\tan 45^{\circ}+\tan 9^{\circ}}{1-\tan 45^{\circ} \cdot \tan 9^{\circ}}=\frac{1+\tan 9^{\circ}}{1-\tan 9^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{1+\frac{\sin 9^{\circ}}{\cos 9^{\circ}}}{1-\frac{\sin 9^{\circ}}{\cos 9^{\circ}}}=\frac{\cos 9^{\circ}+\sin 9^{\circ}}{\cos 9^{\circ}-\sin 9^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{\sin (x+y)}{\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b}{a-b}$, then what is $\frac{\tan x}{\tan y}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\frac{\sin (x+y)}{\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b}{a-b}$
Applying componendo and dividendo, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\sin (x+y)+\sin (x-y)}{\sin (x+y)-\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b+a-b}{a+b-a+b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{x+y+x-y}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{x+y-x+y}{2}\right)}{2 \cos \left(\frac{x+y+x-y}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{x+y-x+y}{2}\right)}=\frac{2 a}{2 b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\sin x \cdot \cos y}{\cos x \cdot \sin y}=\frac{a}{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\tan x}{\tan y}=\frac{a}{b}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \alpha+\sin \beta=0=\cos \alpha+\cos \beta$, where $0 \lt \beta \lt \alpha \lt 2 \pi$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin \alpha+\sin \beta=0=\cos \alpha+\cos \beta \\ & \sin \alpha+\sin \beta=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \alpha=-\sin \beta \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \alpha=\sin (\pi+\beta) \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=\pi+\beta\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Suppose $\cos A$ is given. If only one value of $\cos \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)$ is possible, then A must be
questions.solution:
Given, $\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}$ has only one value.
We know, $\cos \mathrm{A}=2 \cos ^2 \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}-1\Rightarrow 2 \cos ^2 \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}=\cos \mathrm{A}+1 \Rightarrow \cos \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{\cos \mathrm{A}+1}{2}}$
Since, $\cos \frac{A}{2}$ is single value, $\frac{\cos A+1}{2}=0\Rightarrow \cos \mathrm{A}=-1$
So, A is an odd multiple of $180^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos \alpha+\cos \beta+\cos \gamma=0$, where $0 \lt \alpha \leq \frac{\pi}{2}, 0 \lt \beta \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$, $0 \lt \gamma \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$, then what is the value of $\sin \alpha+\sin \beta+\sin \gamma ?$
questions.solution:
$\cos \alpha+\cos \beta+\cos \gamma=0...(1)$
Given, $0 \lt \alpha \leq \frac{\pi}{2}, 0 \lt \beta \leq \frac{\pi}{2}, 0 \lt \gamma \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$.
(1) is satisfied when $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2}, \beta=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\gamma=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \sin \alpha+\sin \beta+\sin \gamma=\sin \frac{\pi}{2}+\sin \frac{\pi}{2}+\sin \frac{\pi}{2} \\
& =1+1+1=3
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha=p$, then what is $\cos ^2(2 \alpha)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha=p\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(\sin \alpha+\cos \alpha)^2=\mathrm{p}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \alpha+\cos ^2 \alpha+2 \sin \alpha \cos \alpha=\mathrm{p}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 1+\sin 2 \alpha=\mathrm{p}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin 2 \alpha=\mathrm{p}^2-1 \\ & \cos ^2 2 \alpha=1-\sin ^2 2 \alpha=1-\left(\mathrm{p}^2-1\right)^2 \\ & =1-\left(\mathrm{p}^4+1-2 \mathrm{p}^2\right)=-\mathrm{p}^4+2 \mathrm{p}^2 \\ & =\mathrm{p}^2\left(2-\mathrm{p}^2\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle \mathrm{PQR}, \angle \mathrm{R}=\frac{\pi}{2}$. If than $\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}\right)$ and $\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}\right)$ are the roots of the equation $a x^2+b x+c=0$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$\angle \mathrm{R}=\frac{\pi}{2}$
$\therefore \angle \mathrm{P}+\angle \mathrm{Q}=\frac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{\angle \mathrm{P}+\angle \mathrm{Q}}{2}=\frac{\pi}{4}$ \ldots(1) $\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}+\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}\right)=\frac{\tan \frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}+\tan \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}}{1-\tan \frac{\mathrm{P}}{2} \tan \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}}$ \ldots(2) Given, $\tan \frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}$ and $\tan \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}$ are roots of $a x^2+b x+c=0$. $\therefore \tan \frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}+\tan \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}=\frac{-\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}} ; \tan \frac{\mathrm{P}}{2} \cdot \tan \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{a}}$. $\therefore(2) \Rightarrow \tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}+\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2}\right)=\frac{\frac{-\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}}{1-\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{a}}}\Rightarrow \tan \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\frac{-\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}}{1-\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{a}}}$ (from (1)) $\Rightarrow 1=\frac{-b}{a-c} \Rightarrow-b=a-c \Rightarrow a+b=c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\tan 9^{\circ}-\tan 27^{\circ}-\tan 63^{\circ}+\tan 81^{\circ}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \tan 9^{\circ}-\tan 27^{\circ}-\tan 63^{\circ}+\tan 81^{\circ} \\ & =\tan 9^{\circ}-\tan 27^{\circ}-\tan \left(90^{\circ}-27^{\circ}\right)+\tan \left(90^{\circ}-9^{\circ}\right)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\tan 9^{\circ}-\tan 27^{\circ}-\cot 27^{\circ}+\cot 9^{\circ} \\ & =\tan 9^{\circ}+\cot 9^{\circ}-\left(\tan 27^{\circ}+\cot 27^{\circ}\right)\end{aligned}$
We know,
$\begin{aligned} & \tan \theta+\cot \theta=\frac{1}{\sin \theta \cos \theta}=\frac{2}{2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}=\frac{2}{\sin 2 \theta} \\ & \therefore \tan 9^{\circ}+\cot 9^{\circ}-\left(\tan 27^{\circ}+\cot 27^{\circ}\right)\end{aligned}=\frac{2}{\sin 18^{\circ}}-\frac{2}{\sin 54^{\circ}}=2\left(\frac{\sin 54^{\circ}-\sin 18^{\circ}}{\sin 18^{\circ} \sin 54^{\circ}}\right)$
We also know, $\sin C-\sin D\begin{aligned} & =2 \cos \frac{(\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D})}{2} \sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{D}}{2}\right) . \\ & \therefore 2\left(\frac{\sin 54^{\circ}-\sin 18^{\circ}}{\sin 18^{\circ} \sin 54^{\circ}}\right)=2 \cdot 2 \cdot \frac{\cos 36^{\circ} \sin 18^{\circ}}{\sin 18^{\circ} \sin 54^{\circ}}\end{aligned}=2 \cdot 2 \cdot \frac{\sin 54^{\circ} \cdot \sin 18^{\circ}}{\sin 18^{\circ} \cdot \sin 54^{\circ}}=4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Angle $\alpha$ is divided into two parts A and B such that $A-B=x$ and $\tan A: \tan B=p: q$. The value of $\sin x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{x}$ and $\tan \mathrm{A}: \tan \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{p}: \mathrm{q}$
Also, given $\alpha=\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{x}$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}\Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=\frac{\mathrm{x}+\alpha}{2}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\frac{\alpha-\mathrm{x}}{2}$
Now, $\frac{\tan \mathrm{A}}{\tan \mathrm{B}}=\frac{\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\alpha}{2}\right)}{\tan \left(\frac{\alpha-\mathrm{x}}{2}\right)}=\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{q}}$ (Given)
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{\alpha+x}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\alpha-x}{2}\right)}{2 \cos \left(\frac{\alpha+x}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{\alpha-x}{2}\right)}=\frac{p}{q} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\sin \alpha+\sin x}{\sin \alpha-\sin x}=\frac{p}{q}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin x}=\frac{p+q}{p-q} \Rightarrow \sin x=\frac{(\sin \alpha)(p-q)}{p+q}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \mathrm{A}=\frac{3}{5}$, where $450^{\circ} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt 540^{\circ}$, then $\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:

$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \cos ^2 \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}=\frac{1+\cos \mathrm{A}}{2}=\frac{1}{10} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{10}}\left(\because \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2} \text { lies in Q3 }\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\cos \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ in the interval $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is attained at
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\cos \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right] \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left[\sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \cos \frac{\pi}{4}+\cos \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right] \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left[\sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right] \\
& (\because \sin (A+B)=\sin A \cos B+\cos A \sin B \\
& =\sqrt{2}\left[\sin \left(x+\frac{5 \pi}{12}\right)\right]
\end{aligned}$
Given interval is $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$
For, maximum value $\mathrm{x}+\frac{5 \pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{5 \pi}{12}=\frac{6 \pi-5 \pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{12}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $K=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{18}\right) \sin \left(\frac{5 \pi}{18}\right) \sin \left(\frac{7 \pi}{18}\right)$, then what is the value of K ?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{K}=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{18}\right) \sin \left(\frac{5 \pi}{18}\right) \sin \left(\frac{7 \pi}{18}\right)$
We know, $2 \sin \mathrm{~A} \sin \mathrm{~B}=\cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})-\cos (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{18}\left[2 \sin \frac{5 \pi}{18} \sin \frac{7 \pi}{18}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{18}\left[\cos \frac{2 \pi}{18}-\cos \frac{12 \pi}{18}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\left[2 \sin \frac{\pi}{18} \cos \frac{2 \pi}{18}-2 \sin \frac{\pi}{18} \cos \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[\sin \left(\frac{3 \pi}{18}\right)+\sin \left(\frac{-\pi}{18}\right)-2 \sin \frac{\pi}{18} \cos \left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[\sin \frac{\pi}{6}-\sin \frac{\pi}{18}+2 \sin \frac{\pi}{18} \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{3}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[\sin \frac{\pi}{6}-\sin \frac{\pi}{18}+2 \sin \frac{\pi}{18} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4} \sin \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{8}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \theta=3 \sin (\theta+2 \alpha)$, then the value of $\tan (\theta+\alpha)+2 \tan \alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\sin \theta=3 \sin (\theta+2 \alpha)\Rightarrow \frac{\sin (\theta+2 \alpha)}{\sin \theta}=\frac{1}{3}$
Apply componendo and dividendo rule
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{\sin (\theta+2 \alpha)+\sin \theta}{\sin (\theta+2 \alpha)-\sin \theta}=\frac{1+3}{1-3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 \sin (\theta+\alpha) \cos \alpha}{2 \cos (\theta+\alpha) \sin \alpha}=\frac{4}{-2}=-2 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\tan (\theta+\alpha)}{\tan \alpha}=-2 \\
& \Rightarrow \tan (\theta+\alpha)=-2 \tan \alpha \Rightarrow \tan (\theta+\alpha)+2 \tan \alpha=0
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan (\alpha+\beta)=2$ and $\tan (\alpha-\beta)=1$, then $\tan (2 \alpha)$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan (\alpha+\beta)=2 \\ & \tan (\alpha-\beta)=1 \\ & \tan 2 \alpha=\tan [(\alpha+\beta)+(\alpha-\beta)] \\ & =\frac{\tan (\alpha+\beta)+\tan (\alpha-\beta)}{1-\tan (\alpha+\beta) \cdot \tan (\alpha-\beta)} \\ & =\frac{2+1}{1-2.1}=\frac{3}{-1}=-3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sec \theta-\operatorname{cosec} \theta=\frac{4}{3}$, then what is $(\sin \theta-\cos \theta)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sec \theta-\operatorname{cosec} \theta=\frac{4}{3} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\cos \theta}-\frac{1}{\sin \theta}=\frac{4}{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\sin \theta-\cos \theta}{\sin \theta \cos \theta}=\frac{4}{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{(\sin \theta-\cos \theta)^2}{(\sin \theta \cos \theta)^2}=\frac{16}{9} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta \cos ^2 \theta}=\frac{16}{9} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1-2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta \cos ^2 \theta}=\frac{16}{9}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text { Let } \sin \theta \cos \theta=x \Rightarrow \frac{1-2 x}{x^2}=\frac{16}{9} \\
& \Rightarrow 16 x^2+18 x-9=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(8 x-3)(2 x+3)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{3}{8}, x=\frac{-3}{2} \\
& \therefore \sin \theta \cos \theta=\frac{3}{8}
\end{aligned}$
from (i), $\sin \theta-\cos \theta=\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{3}{8}=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
$\sin \mathrm{A}+2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}+\sin 3 \mathrm{~A}$ is equal to which of the following?
1. $4 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A} \cos ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}\right)$
2. $2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}\left(\sin \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)^2$
3. $8 \sin \mathrm{~A} \cos \mathrm{~A} \cos ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}\right)$
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{A}=30^{\circ}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & \sin \mathrm{A}+2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}+\sin 3 \mathrm{~A}=\sin 30^{\circ}+2 \sin 60^{\circ}+\sin 90^{\circ} \\
\quad & \frac{1}{2}+\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{2}+1=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}+3}{2} \\
& \left(\because 2 \cos ^2 \mathrm{~A}=1+\cos 2 \mathrm{~A}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Now, $4 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A} \cos ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}\right)=2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}[1+\cos \mathrm{A}]=2 \sin 60^{\circ}\left[1+\cos 30^{\circ}\right]=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}+3}{2}$
Also, $\sin 2 \mathrm{~A}=2 \sin \mathrm{~A} \cos \mathrm{~A} \& \sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}+\cos ^2 \mathrm{~A}=1\begin{aligned}
& 2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}\left[\sin \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right]^2 \\
& =2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}\left[\sin ^2 \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}+\cos ^2 \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}+2 \sin \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2} \cos \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}\right] \\
& =2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}[1+\sin \mathrm{A}]=2 \sin 60^{\circ}\left[1+\sin 30^{\circ}\right] \\
& =\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \& 8 \sin A \cos A \cos ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}\right) \\
& =4 \sin \mathrm{~A} \cos \mathrm{~A}[1+\cos \mathrm{A}] \\
& =4 \sin 30^{\circ} \cos 30^{\circ}\left[1+\cos 30^{\circ}\right] \\
& =\frac{2 \sqrt{3}+3}{2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \theta_1+\sin \theta_2+\sin \theta_3+\sin \theta_4=4$, then what is the value of $\cos \theta_1+\cos \theta_2+\cos \theta_3+\cos \theta_4=?$
questions.solution:
$\sin \theta_1+\sin \theta_2+\sin \theta_3+\sin \theta_4=4$  ...(1)
Since max. value of $\sin \theta=1$
We have four terms in LHS of eq. (1).

Now,

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x=\sin 70^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ}$ and $y=\cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 80^{\circ}$, then what is $x y$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & x=\sin 70^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ} \text { and } y=\cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 80^{\circ} \\ & \Rightarrow x y=\cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \sin 70^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ} \cdot \cos 80^{\circ} \\ & x y=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \sin (90-20) \cdot \sin (90-40) \cdot \cos 80 \\ & \Rightarrow x y=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \cos 20 \cdot \cos 40 \cdot \cos 80 \\ & \quad(\because \sin (90-x)=\cos x) \\ & \Rightarrow x y=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ} \cdot \cos (60-20)^{\circ} \cdot \cos (60+20)^{\circ} \\ & \Rightarrow x y=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{4} \cos 3\left(20^{\circ}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \cos 60^{\circ}=\frac{1}{16} . \\ & \quad\left[\because \cos \theta \cdot \cos (60-\theta) \cdot \cos (60+\theta)=\frac{1}{4} \cos 3 \theta\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of
$\left(1+\cos \frac{\pi}{8}\right)\left(1+\cos \frac{3 \pi}{8}\right)\left(1+\cos \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right)\left(1+\cos \frac{7 \pi}{8}\right) ?$
questions.solution:
$\left[1+\cos \frac{\pi}{8}\right]\left[1+\cos \frac{3 \pi}{8}\right]\left[1+\cos \frac{5 \pi}{8}\right]\left[1+\frac{\cos 7 \pi}{8}\right]$
We have,
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos \frac{7 \pi}{8}=\cos \left[\pi-\frac{\pi}{8}\right]=-\cos \frac{\pi}{8} \\
& \text { and } \cos \frac{5 \pi}{8}=\cos \left[\pi-\frac{3 \pi}{8}\right]=-\cos \frac{3 \pi}{8} \\
& \therefore=\left[1+\cos \frac{\pi}{8}\right]\left[1+\cos \frac{3 \pi}{8}\right]\left[1-\cos \frac{\pi}{8}\right]\left[1-\cos \frac{3 \pi}{8}\right] \\
& =\left[1-\cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{8}\right]\left[1-\cos ^2 \frac{3 \pi}{8}\right]=\sin ^2 \frac{\pi}{8} \cdot \sin ^2 \frac{3 \pi}{8} \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[2 \sin ^2 \frac{\pi}{8} \cdot 2 \sin ^2 \frac{3 \pi}{8}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(1-\cos \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\left(1-\cos \frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{8}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{x} \cos \theta+\mathrm{y} \sin \theta=\mathrm{z}$, then what is the value of $(\mathrm{x} \sin \theta-\mathrm{y} \cos \theta)^2$ ?
questions.solution:
Here, $z=x \cos \theta+y \sin \theta\begin{aligned}
& z^2=x^2 \cos ^2 \theta+y^2 \sin ^2 \theta+2 x y \sin \theta \cos \theta \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x y \sin \theta \cos \theta=z^2-x^2 \cos ^2 \theta-y^2 \sin ^2 \theta
\end{aligned}$
Let, $L=(x \sin \theta-y \cos \theta)^2\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow L=x^2 \sin ^2 \theta+y^2 \cos ^2 \theta-2 x y \sin \theta \cos \theta \\
& \Rightarrow L=x^2 \sin ^2 \theta+y^2 \cos ^2 \theta-\left[z^2-x^2 \cos ^2 \theta-y^2 \sin ^2 \theta\right] \\
& \Rightarrow L=x^2\left[\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\right]+y^2\left[\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\right]-z^2 \\
& \Rightarrow L=x^2+y^2-z^2
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin 18^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}$, then what is the value of $\sin 81^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \because \quad & \sin 18^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4} \\ & \mathrm{x}^2=4^2-(\sqrt{5}-1)^2 \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}=\sqrt{10+2 \sqrt{5}} \\ \Rightarrow & \cos 18^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{10+2 \sqrt{5}}}{4} \\ \Rightarrow & 2 \cos ^2 9-1=\frac{\sqrt{10+2 \sqrt{5}}}{4} \\ \Rightarrow & \cos ^2 9=\frac{\sqrt{10+2 \sqrt{5}}+4}{8} \\ \Rightarrow & \sin ^2 81=\frac{4+\sqrt{10+2 \sqrt{5}}}{8} \end{aligned}$ After squaring all the options available, we come to a conclusion that option (1) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{1-\tan 2^{\circ} \cot 62^{\circ}}{\tan 152^{\circ}-\cot 88^{\circ}}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & L=\frac{1-\tan 2^{\circ} \cot 62^{\circ}}{\tan 152^{\circ}-\cot 88^{\circ}}=\frac{1-\tan 2^{\circ} \cot (90-28)^{\circ}}{\tan (180-28)^{\circ}-\cot (90-2)^{\circ}} \\ & \Rightarrow L=\frac{1-\tan 2^{\circ} \tan 28^{\circ}}{-\tan 28^{\circ}-\tan 2^{\circ}}=-\left[\frac{1-\tan 2^{\circ} \tan 28^{\circ}}{\tan 2^{\circ}+\tan 28^{\circ}}\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow L=-\frac{1}{\tan (2+28)^{\circ}} & =-\frac{1}{\tan 30^{\circ}}=-\sqrt{3} \\ & {\left[\because \tan (A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A \tan B}\right] }\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the function $\mathrm{f}(\theta)=4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta\right)$
What is the minimum value of the function $f(\theta)$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} f(\theta)= & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta\right) \\ = & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right)\right) \\ = & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta \cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ = & 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right) \\ & {[\because \sin 2 \theta=2 \sin \theta \cos \theta] }\end{aligned}$
For minimum value of $f(\theta), \sin ^2 2 \theta$ should be maximum i.e. $\sin ^2 2 \theta=1$.
$\left.f(\theta)\right|_{\min }=4\left(1-\frac{1}{4}(1)\right)=4 \times \frac{3}{4}=3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the function $f(\theta)=4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta\right)$
Consider the following statements:
1. $f(\theta)=2$ has no solution.
2. $\mathrm{f}(\theta)=\frac{7}{2}$ has a solution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} f(\theta)= & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^4 \theta\right) \\ = & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\left(1-\sin ^2 \theta\right)\right) \\ = & 4\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta \cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ = & 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right) \\ & {[\because \sin 2 \theta=2 \sin \theta \cos \theta] }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& f(\theta)=2 \\
& 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right)=2 \\
& \Rightarrow 1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=\frac{2}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=+\frac{1}{2}-1 \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=-\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^2 2 \theta=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta= \pm \sqrt{2}
\end{aligned}$
Since $\sin \theta$ cannot have vlaue greater than $1\&$ less than -1.
Hence $f(\theta)=2$ has no solution.
$\begin{aligned} & f(\theta)=\frac{7}{2} \\ & 4\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right)=\frac{7}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow\left(1-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta\right)=\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=\frac{7}{8}-1 \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{4} \sin ^2 2 \theta=-\frac{1}{8} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^2 2 \theta=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta= \pm \sin \frac{\pi}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow \sin 2 \theta=\sin ( \pm \pi / 4) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \theta= \pm \pi / 4 \\
& \theta=( \pm) \frac{\pi}{8}
\end{aligned}$
Hence $f(\theta)=\frac{7}{2}$ has a solution.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider a triangle ABC in which
$\cos A+\cos B+\cos C=\sqrt{3} \sin \frac{\pi}{3}$
What is the value of $\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2} \sin \frac{C}{2}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given } \cos A+\cos B+\cos C=\sqrt{3} \sin \frac{\pi}{3} \\ & \cos A+\cos B+\cos C \\ & =2 \cos \frac{A+B}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{A-B}{2}+\left(1-2 \sin ^2 \frac{C}{2}\right)  \\ & =2 \sin \frac{C}{2} \cos \frac{A-B}{2}+1-2 \sin ^2 \frac{C}{2} \left(\because \frac{A+B}{2}=90^{\circ}-\frac{C}{2}\right)\\ & =1+2 \sin \frac{C}{2}\left[\cos \frac{A-B}{2}-\sin \frac{C}{2}\right] \\ & =1+2 \sin \frac{C}{2}\left[\cos \frac{A-B}{2}-\cos \frac{A+B}{2}\right] \\ & =1+4 \sin \frac{C}{2} \sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2} \\ & \cos A+\cos B+\cos C=\sqrt{3} \sin \frac{\pi}{3} \\ & 1+4 \sin \frac{C}{2} \sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2}=\sqrt{3} \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 1+4 \sin \frac{C}{2} \sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2}=\sqrt{3} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 4 \sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2} \sin \frac{C}{2}=\frac{3}{2}-1\end{aligned}\sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2} \sin \frac{C}{2}=\frac{1}{8}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\sqrt{1+\sin \mathrm{A}}=-\left(\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)$ is true if
questions.solution:
$\sqrt{1+\sin \mathrm{A}}=-\left(\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)$
We know, $1+\sin \mathrm{A}=\left(\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)^2\therefore \sqrt{1+\sin \mathrm{A}}=\left|\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right|$
We know, $|x|=\left\{\begin{array}{c}x \text { if } x \geq 0 \\ -x \text { if } x \lt 0\end{array}\right.\left|\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right|= \begin{cases}\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}, & \text { if } 2 \mathrm{n} \pi-\frac{\pi}{4} \leq \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2} \leq 2 \mathrm{n} \pi+\frac{3 \pi}{4} \\ -\left(\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right), & \text { if otherwise }\end{cases}\therefore \sqrt{1+\sin \mathrm{A}}=-\left(\sin \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\right)$
when,
$\frac{3 \pi}{4} \lt \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2} \lt \frac{7 \pi}{4}\Rightarrow \frac{3 \pi}{2} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \frac{7 \pi}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\sqrt{3} \operatorname{cosec} 20^{\circ}-\sec 20^{\circ}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sqrt{3} \operatorname{cosec} 20^{\circ}-\sec 20^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sin 20^{\circ}}-\frac{1}{\cos 20^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 20^{\circ}-\sin 20^{\circ}}{\sin 20^{\circ} \cos 20^{\circ}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2} \sin 20^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 20^{\circ} \cos 20^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{2\left(\cos 30^{\circ} \cos 20^{\circ}-\sin 30^{\circ} \sin 20^{\circ}\right)}{\left(\frac{2 \sin 20^{\circ} \cos 20^{\circ}}{2}\right)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{4\left[\cos \left(30^{\circ}+20^{\circ}\right)\right]}{\sin 40^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{4 \cos 50^{\circ}}{\sin 40^{\circ}}=\frac{4 \cos \left(90^{\circ}-40^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 40^{\circ}}=\frac{4 \sin 40^{\circ}}{\sin 40^{\circ}}=4 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: On simplifying $\frac{\sin ^3 \mathrm{~A}+\sin 3 \mathrm{~A}}{\sin \mathrm{~A}}+\frac{\cos ^3 \mathrm{~A}-\cos 3 \mathrm{~A}}{\cos \mathrm{~A}}$, we get
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sin ^3 \mathrm{~A}+\sin 3 \mathrm{~A}}{\sin \mathrm{~A}}+\frac{\cos ^3 \mathrm{~A}-\cos 3 \mathrm{~A}}{\cos \mathrm{~A}} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\sin ^3 \mathrm{~A}+3 \sin \mathrm{~A}-4 \sin ^3 \mathrm{~A}}{\sin \mathrm{~A}}+\frac{\cos ^3 \mathrm{~A}-\left[4 \cos ^3 \mathrm{~A}-3 \cos \mathrm{~A}\right]}{\cos \mathrm{A}} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{3 \sin \mathrm{~A}-3 \sin ^3 \mathrm{~A}}{\sin \mathrm{~A}}+\frac{\left(-3 \cos ^3 \mathrm{~A}+3 \cos \mathrm{~A}\right)}{\cos \mathrm{A}} \\ = & 3-3 \sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}-3 \cos ^2 \mathrm{~A}+3 \\ = & 6-3\left(\cos ^2 \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}\right) \\ = & 6-3(1) \\ = & 3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin x+\sin y=a$ and $\cos x+\cos y=b$, then $\tan ^2\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)+\tan ^2\left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin \mathrm{x}+\sin \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{a} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)=\mathrm{a}....(1) \\
& \cos \mathrm{x}+\cos \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)=\mathrm{b}....(2)
\end{aligned}$
dividing eq (1) \& (2)
$\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{~b}}$
Squaring eq (1) \& (2) and adding -
$\begin{aligned}
& 4 \cos ^2\left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)=a^2+b^2 \\
& \sec ^2\left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)=\frac{4}{a^2+b^2}
\end{aligned}$
again-
$\begin{aligned}
& \tan ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)+\tan ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}}{2}\right) \\
= & \left(\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{~b}}\right)^2+\sec ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)-1 \\
= & \frac{\mathrm{a}^2}{\mathrm{~b}^2}+\frac{4}{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}-1 \\
= & \frac{\mathrm{a}^4-\mathrm{b}^4+4 \mathrm{~b}^2}{\mathrm{a}^2 \mathrm{~b}^2+\mathrm{b}^4}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{1}{\sin 10^{\circ}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\cos 10^{\circ}}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\sin 10^{\circ}}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\cos 10^{\circ}}=\frac{\cos 10^{\circ}-\sqrt{3} \sin 10^{\circ}}{\sin 10^{\circ} \cos 10^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{2 \times 2\left[\frac{1}{2} \cos 10^{\circ}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin 10^{\circ}\right]}{2 \sin 10^{\circ} \cos 10^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{4\left(\cos 60^{\circ} \cos 10^{\circ}-\sin 60^{\circ} \sin 10^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 20^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{4 \cdot \cos \left(60^{\circ}+10^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 20^{\circ}}=4 \cdot \frac{\cos 70^{\circ}}{\sin 20^{\circ}}=4 \cdot \frac{\sin 20^{\circ}}{\sin 20^{\circ}}=4\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $\mathrm{p}=\tan \left(-\frac{11 \pi}{6}\right), \mathrm{q}=\tan \left(\frac{21 \pi}{4}\right)$ and $\mathrm{r}=\cot \left(\frac{283 \pi}{6}\right)$, then which of the following is/are correct?
1. The value of $\mathrm{p} \times \mathrm{r}$ is 2 .
2. $p, q$ and $r$ are in G.P.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{p}=\tan \left(-\frac{11 \pi}{6}\right) \\
& \mathrm{p}=-\tan \left(2 \pi-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\
& \mathrm{p}=\tan \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \mathrm{q}=\tan \left(\frac{21 \pi}{4}\right) \\
&=\tan \left(6 \pi-\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \\
& \mathrm{q}=-\tan \frac{3 \pi}{4}=+\tan \frac{\pi}{4}=1 \\
& \mathrm{r}=\cot \left(\frac{283 \pi}{6}\right) \\
&=\cot \left(46 \pi+\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right)=\cot \left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\
& \mathrm{r}=\cot \frac{\pi}{6}=\sqrt{3} \\
& \mathrm{p} \times \mathrm{r}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \sqrt{3}=1
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Statement (1) is incorrect.
also $\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{q}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
Sop, $q, r$ are in G.P.
$\therefore$ Statement (2) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\theta$ be a positive angle. If the number of degrees in $\theta$ is divided by the number of radians in $\theta$, then an irrational number $\frac{180}{\pi}$ results. If the number of degrees in $\theta$ is multiplied by the number of radians in $\theta$, then an irrational number $\frac{125 \pi}{9}$ results. The angle $\theta$ must be equal to
questions.solution:
From going by the options,
option (A), $\theta=30^{\circ}$, as we know that
$180^{\circ}=\pi$ radian
$\therefore \quad 30^{\circ}=\frac{30 \pi}{180}$ radian
Now according to question,
$\frac{30^{\circ} \times 180^{\circ}}{30^{\circ} \pi}=\frac{180}{\pi}$
Now number of degree in $\theta$ is multiplied by number of radians in $\theta$.
$\therefore \quad 30^{\circ} \times \frac{30 \pi}{180}=\frac{900 \pi}{180}=\frac{10 \pi}{2}=5 \pi \neq \frac{125 \pi}{9}$
From option (B),
$\begin{aligned} & \theta=45^{\circ} \\ \therefore \quad & 45^{\circ}=\frac{45^{\circ} \pi}{180} \text { radian }\end{aligned}$
Now according to question,
$\frac{45^{\circ} \times 180}{45^{\circ} \pi}=\frac{180}{\pi}$
Now number of degree in $\theta$ is multiplied by number of radian in $\theta$.
$\therefore \quad 45^{\circ} \times \frac{45^{\circ} \pi}{180^{\circ}}=\frac{45 \pi}{4} \neq \frac{125 \pi}{9}$
From option (C),
$\theta=50^{\circ}$
As we know that $180^{\circ}=\pi$ radian
$\therefore \quad 50^{\circ}=\frac{50 \pi}{180}$ radian
Now according to question
$\frac{50^{\circ} \times 180^{\circ}}{50^{\circ} \pi}=\frac{180}{\pi}$
Now number of degree in ' $\theta$ ' is multiplied by number of radian in $\theta$.
$\therefore \quad 50^{\circ} \times \frac{50 \pi}{180}=\frac{2500 \pi}{180}=\frac{125 \pi}{9}\therefore \quad$ Option (C) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $\alpha$ be the root of the equation $25 \cos ^2 \theta+5 \cos \theta-12=0$, 
where $\frac{\pi}{2} \lt \alpha \lt \pi$.
What is $\sin 2 \alpha$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin 2 \alpha=2 \sin \alpha \cdot \cos \alpha \\ & =2\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{-4}{5}\right) \\ & =\frac{6}{5} \times \frac{-4}{5}=\frac{-24}{25}\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (B) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $(1-\sin A+\cos A)^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & (1-\sin A+\cos A)^2 \\ & =1+\sin ^2 A+\cos ^2 A-2 \sin A \\ & \quad-2 \sin A \cdot \cos A+2 \cos A\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =2-2 \sin A-2 \sin A \cos A+2 \cos A \\
& =2(1-\sin A)+2 \cos A(1-\sin A) \\
& =2(1+\cos A)(1-\sin A)
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (B) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $\alpha$ be the root of the equation $25 \cos ^2 \theta+5 \cos \theta-12=0$, 
where $\frac{\pi}{2} \lt \alpha \lt \pi$.
What is $\tan \alpha$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Here $\alpha$ is the root of equation
$25 \cos ^2 \theta+5 \cos \theta-12=0\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow \quad 25 \cos ^2 \alpha+5 \cos \alpha-12=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 25 \cos ^2 \alpha+20 \cos \alpha-15 \cos \alpha-12=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 5 \cos \alpha(5 \cos \alpha+4)-3(5 \cos \alpha+4)=0 \\ & (5 \cos \alpha-3)(5 \cos \alpha+4)=0 \\ & \cos \alpha=\frac{3}{5} \text { or } \cos \alpha=\frac{-4}{5}\end{array}$
Here, $\frac{\pi}{2} \lt \alpha \lt \pi\cos \alpha=\frac{-4}{5}$
( $\because$ In $2^{\text {nd }}$ quadrant, $\cos \alpha$ value is negative)
Now, $\sin \alpha=\sqrt{1-\cos ^2 \alpha}=\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}}\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \sin \alpha=\frac{3}{5} \\
& \therefore \quad \tan \alpha=\frac{\sin \alpha}{\cos \alpha}=\frac{3}{5} \times \frac{-5}{4}=\frac{-3}{4}
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (A) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cot \mathrm{A}=2$ and $\cot \mathrm{B}=3$, then what is the value of $A+B$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cot A=2 \therefore \tan A=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \text {and } \cot B=3 \therefore \tan B=\frac{1}{3} \\ & \tan (A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A \cdot \tan B}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3}} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan (A+B)=\frac{5}{6} \times \frac{6}{5}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \tan (A+B)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A+B=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{\cos \theta}{1-\tan \theta}+\frac{\sin \theta}{1-\cot \theta}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\cos \theta}{1-\tan \theta}+\frac{\sin \theta}{1-\cot \theta} \\ & =\frac{\cos \theta}{1-\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}}+\frac{\sin \theta}{1-\frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}} \\ & =\frac{\cos ^2 \theta}{\cos \theta-\sin \theta}+\frac{\sin ^2 \theta}{\sin \theta-\cos \theta}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\cos ^2 \theta}{\cos \theta-\sin \theta}-\frac{\sin ^2 \theta}{\cos \theta-\sin \theta} \\ & =\frac{\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta}{\cos \theta-\sin \theta}=\frac{(\cos \theta-\sin \theta)(\cos \theta+\sin \theta)}{\cos \theta-\sin \theta}\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (B) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{\cos 7 x-\cos 3 x}{\sin 7 x-2 \sin 5 x+\sin 3 x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\cos 7 x-\cos 3 x}{\sin 7 x+\sin 3 x-2 \sin 5 x} \\ & =\frac{-2 \sin 5 x \cdot \sin 2 x}{2 \sin 5 x \cdot \cos 2 x-2 \sin 5 x} \\ & =\frac{-2 \sin 5 x \cdot \sin 2 x}{-2 \sin 5 x(1-\cos 2 x)}=\frac{\sin 2 x}{2 \sin ^2 x} \\ & =\frac{2 \sin x \cdot \cos x}{2 \sin x \cdot \sin x}=\cot x .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{\sin (x+y)}{\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b}{a-b}$, then what is $\frac{\tan x}{\tan y}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sin (x+y)+\sin (x-y)}{\sin (x+y)-\sin (x-y)}=\frac{a+b+a-b}{a+b-a+b} \\ & \frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{x+y+x-y}{2}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{x+y-x+y}{2}\right)}{2 \cos \left(\frac{x+y+x-y}{2}\right) \cdot \sin \left(\frac{x+y-x+y}{2}\right)}=\frac{2 a}{2 b} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin x \cdot \cos y}{\cos x \cdot \sin y}=\frac{a}{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \tan x \times \cot y=\frac{a}{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \tan x \times \frac{1}{\tan y}=\frac{a}{b} \quad \Rightarrow \frac{\tan x}{\tan y}=\frac{a}{b}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \mathrm{A} \sin \left(60^{\circ}-\mathrm{A}\right) \sin \left(60^{\circ}+\mathrm{A}\right)=k \sin 3 \mathrm{~A}$, then what is $k$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \sin \mathrm{A} \cdot\left(\sin ^2 60^{\circ}-\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}\right) & =\mathrm{k} \sin 3 \mathrm{~A} \\ \sin \mathrm{~A}\left(\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2-\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}\right) & =k \sin 3 \mathrm{~A} \\ \sin \mathrm{~A}\left(\frac{3}{4}-\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}\right) & =k \sin 3 \mathrm{~A} \\ \frac{3 \sin \mathrm{~A}-4 \sin ^3 \mathrm{~A}}{4} & =k \sin 3 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \frac{\sin 3 \mathrm{~A}}{4} & =\frac{k \sin 3 \mathrm{~A}}{1} \\ 4 k & =1 \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. If $3 \theta$ is an acute angle such that $\sin 3 \theta=\cos 2 \theta$, then the measurement of $\theta$ in radian equals to $\frac{\pi}{10}$.
2. One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc of the same circle whose length is equal to the diameter of that circle.
  
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin 3 \theta=\cos 2 \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \cos \left(90^{\circ}-3 \theta\right)=\cos 2 \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 90^{\circ}-3 \theta=2 \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 5 \theta=90^{\circ} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta=18^{\circ} \\
& \therefore \quad 180^{\circ}=\pi \text { radian } \\
& \therefore \quad 18^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{180} \times 18=\frac{\pi}{10} \text { radian }
\end{aligned}$
1 is true.
2 is not true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{1+\sin A}{1-\sin A}-\frac{1-\sin A}{1+\sin A}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1+\sin \mathrm{A}}{1-\sin \mathrm{A}}-\frac{1-\sin \mathrm{A}}{1+\sin \mathrm{A}} \\ = & \frac{(1+\sin \mathrm{A})^2-(1-\sin \mathrm{A})^2}{(1-\sin \mathrm{A})(1+\sin \mathrm{A})} \\ = & \frac{\left(1+2 \sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}\right)-\left(1-2 \sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}\right)}{1-\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}} \\ = & \frac{1+2 \sin \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}-1+2 \sin \mathrm{~A}-\sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}}{\cos ^2 \mathrm{~A}} \\ = & \frac{4 \sin \mathrm{~A}}{\cos \mathrm{~A} \times \cos \mathrm{A}}=4 \sec \mathrm{~A} \cdot \tan \mathrm{~A} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C}=\pi$, then what is $\cos (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})+\cos \mathrm{C}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
\because \quad \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C} & =\pi \\
\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B} & =\pi-\mathrm{C} \\
\cos (\mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}) & =\cos (\pi-\mathrm{C}) \\
\Rightarrow \cos (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) & =-\cos \mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\cos (A+B)+\cos C=-\cos C+\cos C=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\cos 20^{\circ}+\cos 100^{\circ}+\cos 140^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos 20^{\circ}+\cos 100^{\circ}+\cos 140^{\circ} \\ & =2 \cos \frac{120^{\circ}}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{80^{\circ}}{2}+\cos 140^{\circ} \\ & =2 \cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 40^{\circ}+\cos 140^{\circ} \\ & =2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \cos 40^{\circ}+\cos 140^{\circ} \\ & =\cos 40^{\circ}+\cos 140^{\circ} \\ & =\cos 40^{\circ}+\cos \left(180^{\circ}-40^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 40^{\circ}=0 .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\sin ^2(3 \pi)+\cos ^2(4 \pi)+\tan ^2(5 \pi)$ equal to?

$\begin{aligned}
& \sin ^2(3 \pi)+\cos ^2(4 \pi)+\tan ^2(5 \pi) \\
& =(0)^2+(1)^2+\frac{\sin ^2(5 \pi)}{\cos ^2(5 \pi)} \\
& =0+1+0=1 \quad\left[\begin{array}{l}
\because \sin n \pi=0 \\
\cos n \pi=(-1)^n
\end{array}\right]
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\tan 15^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
From formula
$\begin{aligned}
\tan (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}) & =\frac{\tan \mathrm{A}-\tan \mathrm{B}}{1+\tan \mathrm{A} \cdot \tan \mathrm{~B}} \\
\tan \left(15^{\circ}\right) & =\tan \left(45^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\right) \\
& =\frac{\tan 45^{\circ}-\tan 30^{\circ}}{1+\tan 45^{\circ}+\tan 30^{\circ}} \\
& =\frac{1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1+1 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}=\frac{(\sqrt{3}-1)}{(\sqrt{3}+1)} \times \frac{(\sqrt{3}-1)}{(\sqrt{3}-1)}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(\sqrt{3}-1)^2}{(\sqrt{3})^2-(1)^2}=\frac{3+1-2 \sqrt{3}}{3-1} \\ & =\frac{4-2 \sqrt{3}}{2}=2-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. $\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$
2. $\tan \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)$
3. $\tan \left(\frac{5 \pi}{4}\right)$
4. $\tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)$
questions.solution:
From trigonometric values
1. $\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
2. $\tan \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-1$
3. $\tan \left(\frac{5 \pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1$
4. $\tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=\tan \left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-\sqrt{3}$
Hence, correct ascending order is $4 \lt 2 \lt 1 \lt 3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\sqrt{1+\sin 2 \theta}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \sqrt{1+\sin 2 \theta} & =\sqrt{\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta} \\ & =\sqrt{(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2} \\ & =\sin \theta+\cos \theta \\ & =\cos \theta+\sin \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cos x=\frac{1}{3}$, then what is $\sin x \cdot \cot x \cdot \operatorname{cosec} x \cdot \tan x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos x=\frac{1}{3} \\ & \sin x \cdot \cot x \cdot \operatorname{cosec} x \cdot \tan x \\ & =\sin x \cdot \frac{1}{\tan x} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x} \cdot \tan x=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{\cos 54^{\circ}}{\tan 36^{\circ}}+\frac{\tan 20^{\circ}}{\cot 70^{\circ}}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\cot 54^{\circ}}{\tan 36^{\circ}}+\frac{\tan 20^{\circ}}{\cot 70^{\circ}} \\ & \frac{\tan \left(90^{\circ}-54^{\circ}\right)}{\tan 36^{\circ}}+\frac{\tan 20^{\circ}}{\tan \left(90^{\circ}-70^{\circ}\right)} \\ & \frac{\tan 36^{\circ}}{\tan 36^{\circ}}+\frac{\tan 20^{\circ}}{\tan 20^{\circ}}=1+1=2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the angle (in circular measure) between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock when the time is half past $4 ?$
questions.solution:
Angle rotated by minute hand in 30 minutes
$=\frac{30}{60} \times 360^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$
Angle rotated by hour hand when it is at 4.5
$=\frac{4.5}{12} \times 360^{\circ}=135^{\circ}$
Angle between two hands $=180^{\circ}-135^{\circ}=45^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a triangle $A B C, \sin A-\cos B=\cos C$, then what is $B$ euqal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \quad \sin A-\cos B=\cos C \text { (given) } \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos B+\cos C=\sin A \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos \frac{B+C}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{B-C}{2}=\sin A \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{(B-C)}{2}=2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cdot \cos \frac{A}{2}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \cos \frac{(\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C})}{2}=\cos \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C}}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{A}\Rightarrow \quad B=A+C\because \quad A+B+C=180^{\circ}\Rightarrow \quad B+B=180^{\circ}\Rightarrow \quad 2 \mathrm{~B}=180^{\circ}\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{B}=90^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan \mathrm{A}-\tan \mathrm{B}=x$ and $\cot \mathrm{B}-\cot \mathrm{A}=y$, then what is $\cot (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \because \quad \tan \mathrm{A}-\tan \mathrm{B}=x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin \mathrm{~A}}{\cos \mathrm{~A}}-\frac{\sin \mathrm{B}}{\cos \mathrm{B}}=x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin (\mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{B})}{\cos \mathrm{A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{B}}=x\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B} \quad \ldots(i)\begin{aligned} & \cot \mathrm{B}-\cot \mathrm{A}=y \\ & \frac{\cos \mathrm{~B}}{\sin \mathrm{~B}}-\frac{\cos \mathrm{A}}{\sin \mathrm{A}}=y\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}$  ...(ii)
From (i) and (ii) $x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}=y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}\begin{aligned} & \cot (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=\frac{\cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})}{\sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})} \\ &=\frac{\cos \mathrm{A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{B}+\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B}}{x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}} \\ & {[\because x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}=y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}] }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B}}{x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}} \\ & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B}}{y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}} \\ & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\frac{1+\cos x}{\sin x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\frac{1+\cos x}{\sin x} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 x+(1+\cos x)^2}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 x+1+2 \cos x+\cos ^2 x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =\frac{\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right)+1+2 \cos x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =\frac{2+2 \cos x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\frac{2(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =2 \operatorname{cosec} x\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If an angle $\alpha$ is divided into two parts $A$ and $B$ such that $A-B=x$ and $\tan A: \tan B=2: 1$, then what is $\sinx$ equal to?

questions.q:
If
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos A+\cos B=m \\
& \sin A+\sin B=n
\end{aligned}$
where $m, n \neq 0$, then what is $\sin (A+B)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& m n=\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~A}+\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B} \\
& \quad+\quad \cos \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}+\cos \mathrm{B} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B} \\
& =\frac{\sin 2 \mathrm{~A}}{2}+\sin (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})+\frac{\sin 2 \mathrm{~B}}{2} \\
& =\sin (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})+\frac{1}{2}\{2 \sin (\mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}) \cdot \cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})\} \\
& =\sin (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})+\sin (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) \cdot \cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}) \\
& m n=\sin (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})\{1+\cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})\}...(i)
\end{aligned}$
Also, 
$\begin{aligned} m^2+n^2= & \cos ^2 \mathrm{~A}+\cos ^2 \mathrm{~B} \\ & +2 \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}+ \\ + & \sin ^2 \mathrm{~A}+\sin ^2 \mathrm{~B} \\ & +2 \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =2+2 \cos (\mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{B}) \\
& m^2+n^2=2\{1+\cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})\} \\
& \frac{m^2+n^2}{2}=1+\cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii)
$\sin (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})=\frac{2 m n}{m^2+n^2}$

questions.q: What is the value of $\sqrt{3} \operatorname{cosec} 20^{\circ}-\sec 20^{\circ} ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sqrt{3} \operatorname{cosec} 20^{\circ}-\sec 20^{\circ} \\ = & \sqrt{3} \times \frac{1}{\sin 20^{\circ}}-\frac{1}{\cos 20^{\circ}} \\ = & \frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 20^{\circ}-\sin 20^{\circ}}{\sin 20^{\circ} \cos 20^{\circ}} \\ = & \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2} \sin 20^{\circ}}{\frac{1}{2} \sin 20^{\circ} \cos 20^{\circ}} \\ = & 4 \frac{\sin \left(60^{\circ}-20^{\circ}\right)}{\sin 2 \times 20^{\circ}}=4\end{aligned}$
